sources.title: 24 Hour Rule
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/24 Hour Rule.pptx

units.heading: 24 Hour Rule
units.text:
When a customer enrolls due to a QLE, they technically have until the end of the following business day (~24 hours), to cancel or change. After the end of the following business day, any requests for cancellations or changes must be performed due to a valid QLE or during Open Season.
Note:
- Do not communicate the 24-hour rule to customers during their enrollment.
- Be aware of this timeframe in case an enrollee calls to request a change or cancellation.
- Check the Transaction log in Payroll UI to see if an enrollee is within the following business day (~24-hour) window.
- If the enrollment is processed on a Friday or over the weekend, the customer has until the end of Monday, the following business day, to change or cancel their enrollment.
Talking Point:
Customer calls in after the end of the following business day:
“I am sorry, but due to the rules and regulations of the FEDVIP you are required to have a valid QLE or must wait until Open Season to cancel or make changes to your enrollment.”
conditions: Note:
Do not communicate the 24-hour rule to customers during their enrollment.

sources.title: 5-Day Grace Period for Non-Pay Inactivation
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/5-Day Grace Period for Non-Pay Inactivation.pptx

units.heading: 5-Day Grace Period for Non-Pay Inactivation
units.text:
Accounts that have been inactivated due to non-pay are given a 5-day grace period where PAT will automatically reinstate if the payment is received. However, this 5-day grace period is only available for premiums that were remitted before the due date of a Direct Bill, Past Due Reinstatement Letter or termination notice. The 5-day grace period does not extend to accounts that have already been inactivated.
If an enrollee calls intending to remit payment, but the enrollee has missed the due date on the Past Due Reinstatement Letter, they may not make an overnight payment.
Past Due Reinstatement Letters are available in Image, where you will be able to check the due date.
Please review the Reinstatement For Non-Pay and the BENEFEDS Reinstatement/Re-enroll job aids (linked in the description below).

units.heading: ABW Scripting
units.text:
You must always read the following script each time you set up or change banking information for ABW on a plan.
Example: Primary AWD Create Enrollment Ticket

units.heading: Transcription of image content
units.text:
## Transcribed from image (Slide 1): ABW Terms and Conditions script (CS System screen)
Agent says: "I will now read you the Automatic Bank Withdrawal Terms and Conditions."
(Read the Terms and Conditions below.)
AUTOMATIC BANK WITHDRAWAL (ABW) AUTHORIZATION
"By selecting automatic bank withdrawal (ABW), you, [customer name], authorize BENEFEDS to debit your checking or savings account ending in [last 4 of account] on the fifth business day of each month for [$ monthly premium], beginning on [first withdrawal date]. You agree that the specified account is and will continue to be an account you own, and you will maintain sufficient funds to pay your monthly FEDVIP premiums.
The authorization, given today, [today's date], is for a recurring withdrawal. If you wish to cancel your ABW authorization, you must do so in writing by completing the Revoke ABW Authorization Form and returning it to BENEFEDS at least 10 business days before the next payment is scheduled. This form can be downloaded from the "Billing and Payments" section."
Agent asks: "Do you agree to the Terms and Conditions?" (select Yes / No, then Next)
(Screenshot example values: Richard Brown, account ending 6789, $137.50, beginning May 7, 2025, authorization given Mar 31, 2025.)

units.heading: AWD: Action Menu
units.text: The Action Menu is in the AWD tagline. Agents will click the three vertical dots to access. Most of the features in the Action Menu are not used by agents. However, the chart below provides an explanation of the features.

units.heading: AWD: Action Menu · Assign
units.text:
| Action Menu Option | Description |
| Assign | - Assigns the object to another user. / - Agents do not use this action. |

units.heading: AWD: Action Menu · Assign to Self
units.text:
| Action Menu Option | Description |
| Assign to Self | - Only displays in the action menu for tickets previously created. / - Assigns the object to you and adds it to your Worklist tab. / - Agents may use this when advised to close a Callout ticket. |

units.heading: AWD: Action Menu · Link From/To
units.text:
| Action Menu Option | Description |
| Link From/To | - Copies the selected object to the clipboard. / - The object remains in the clipboard until you overwrite it or close AWD. |

units.heading: AWD: Action Menu · Release
units.text:
| Action Menu Option | Description |
| Release | - Releases the ticket after one is locked to yourself but needs to go back into queue. / - Agents do not typically use this action. Comments can be added to the ticket without locking it to yourself. |

units.heading: AWD: Action Menu · Suspend
units.text:
| Action Menu Option | Description |
| Suspend | - Agents do not use this action. |

units.heading: AWD: Action Menu · View Data
units.text:
| Action Menu Option | Description |
| View Data | - Provides a listing of all defined line-of-business (LOB) and AWD fields for the selected object that have a value. |

units.heading: AWD: Action Menu · View History
units.text:
| Action Menu Option | Description |
| View History | - Enables you to view the history of the object. / - Information includes timestamps of the object as the ticket is worked on, manual or system comments, timestamps of the ticket statuses, etc. |

units.heading: AWD: Action Menu · Get Link
units.text:
| Action Menu Option | Description |
| Get Link | - Generates popup window which gives the Object ID. / - After it is copied to your clipboard, you can paste the link into an email, message, or document. / - This feature is not typically used. Agents will send the AWD ticket number when referencing a specific work item. |

units.heading: AWD: Action Menu · Split Attachment

units.heading: AWD: Creating a Work Item
units.text: This job aid demonstrates how to create a new AWD Work Item using Quick Create.

units.heading: AWD: Creating a Work Item
units.text:
From the Toolbar:
- Click the Quick Create button.
- A menu with all Work Item categories appears. Select the category from the menu.
- The category expands to reveal the Work Item types. Select the Work Item type to create.

units.heading: AWD: Creating a Work Item

units.heading: AWD: Creating a Work Item
units.text:

- Once the Work Item is submitted, the card will close and return you to the main Workspace. The Create card can be closed at this time.

units.heading: Enrollment Verification AWD Ticket
units.text:
Enrollment Verification AWD Work Items may be needed when the BENEFEDS System shows accurate and up-to-date information but the Carrier’s system does not show the same information.
BENEFEDS will send enrollment & change information to the Carrier and generally it takes 3 to 5 business days for the Carrier to load the information into their system. If the customer is calling after the coverage effective date, and you have confirmed with the Carrier that this information has not yet been updated, then you may need to submit an Enrollment Verification AWD Work Item.

units.heading: Enrollment Verification AWD Ticket

units.heading: Accessing AWD
units.text:
Accessing AWD
Recommended Browser: Edge
Use the AWD URL provided to reach the Sign In page.

units.heading: Changing Your Password
units.text:
Changing Your Password
For security reasons, it is recommended you change your password regularly. The following situations require a password change:
- new user
- locked user whose password has been reset
- expired password
To change your password, type in your username and existing password, then check the Change Password box and click Sign In. The Change Password box appears, giving you the FedPoint criteria for AWD passwords and prompting you to enter and confirm your new password.

units.heading: Navigation Tips
units.text:
Navigation Tips
- Do not have more than one AWD program open at a time.
- Do not use the internet browser buttons for navigation. Only use the navigation buttons within AWD.
- Sign Off the system; do not simply “X” out of the window.
- In certain circumstances, tickets or other work objects may open in new browser tabs or windows. Be sure to close all tabs before signing off.
conditions: Do not have more than one AWD program open at a time.
Do not use the internet browser buttons for navigation. Only use the navigation buttons within AWD.

units.heading: System Timeout
units.text:
System Timeout
The AWD system will log the user out after thirty (30) minutes of inactivity. On the time-out event, click Continue. By clicking Continue, users can cancel the time-out and continue working.
Note: If users do not click Continue within 30 seconds, a second dialog box appears. On the second dialog box, the browser will give the options to Leave or Cancel. Select Cancel to return to AWD and stay logged in.
conditions: Note: If users do not click Continue within 30 seconds, a second dialog box appears. On the second dialog box, the browser will give the options to Leave or Cancel. Select Cancel to return to AWD and stay logged in.

units.heading: System Lag
units.text:
System Lag
To prevent slow-down of AWD processing time, please:
- Close any cards that aren’t in use.
- Log Out of AWD (Sign Off) and close your browser pages when you go to lunch.
- Click on the Comment bubble icon to add comments. There is no need to open a work item to comment.

units.heading: Closing a Work Type Created in Error (CIE)
units.text:
Closing a Work Type Created in Error (CIE)
If you create a work item in error, it will populate in the Worklist.
Double click the ticket to open it. It will open in a new card. Lock it to yourself if it isn’t already locked to you.
Click Cancel Work. DO NOT ‘X’ OUT OF THE TICKET or it will become an orphan ticket which has to be manually removed later. Click Confirm Cancellation on the next page.

units.heading: AWD: Taglines
units.text: AWD taglines provide agents with a snapshot of the information in the AWD Work Item.

units.heading: AWD: Taglines
units.text:
- Business Area – Work Type – AWD Ticket Number
- Most BENEFEDS tickets are under the BENEFEDS Business Area.
- AWD ticket numbers are the insured’s first two initials, a unique set of numbers, then their last two initials.
- Ticket Information
- Displays details about the contents of the Work Item such as Status Code, Reason, Business Area, etc.
- Information displayed varies by ticket type.
- Process Step
- Each Work Type has specific steps as it moves through the system towards a resolution.
- Hover your cursor to display the current step the ticket is on in the progression towards a resolution.
- Some examples are Submit Work, Process Work, and Review Required.

sources.title: Account Review Request
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Account Review Request.pptx

units.heading: Account Review Request
units.text:
An Account Review is an escalation. It occurs when there is a discrepancy between what an enrollee perceives took place and what occurred during a phone call into BENEFEDS. This could be for both Open Season and Plan Year calls.
- Account reviews are processed in the order they are received, there is no time frame for resolution. Callers will receive a call back from the Research department when the review has been completed.
The following scenarios are examples of when an account review may be requested:
- Enrolled under incorrect carrier
- Enrollee claims they never enrolled, but an enrollment was submitted by an agent
- Enrollee states they did not disenroll and the plan was disenrolled
- Enrollee states they requested cancelation through IVR or agent, and account is still active
- Enrollee states they called about Going on Active Duty and account not inactivated
- Enrollee states an action was taken during Open Season and it was not done
- Examples include add/remove family, plan change, cancelation, or enrollment
- Enrollee was enrolled into a plan by a BENEFEDS rep who provided coverage info, or “recommended” a plan, and now wants to change plan (we would honor this)
- Enrollee claims they were given wrong information about Coverage Effective Date and had services
- BENEFEDS could be responsible for cost of claim (this is rare)
- Enrollee was termed for non-payment due to wrong information given about paying Direct Bills
- Survivor Annuitant coverage issues
- Prospective vs Retroactive enrollment

units.heading: Account Review Request
units.text: Follow the steps to log an account review in SharePoint CCC Workspace.

units.heading: Account Review Request
units.text: Step 1: Access CCC Workspace from the BENEFEDS System Access page in LEARN, then select Escalation Notification Log

units.heading: Account Review Request
units.text: Step 2: At the top left of the window, select New Item

units.heading: Step 3:
units.text:
Step 3:
- Complete the top portion of the form Member ID through Enrollee Email. In the escalation type field, select Account Review
- In Issue summary, be clear about the reason you are submitting the account review.

slides.title: Adding Sponsors Outside of Open Season

units.heading: Adding Sponsors Outside of Open Season
units.text: Background: In some instances, a Sponsor will mistakenly create their plan and establish themselves as the Sponsor when they really wanted to receive coverage as the primary enrollee. A Sponsor must answer "yes" to one of three criteria in order to enroll family members without the Sponsor as Primary; the Sponsor is now calling to enroll as the Primary because of a "mistake" meaning he/she does not meet one of the 3 criteria.

units.heading: Post Open Season within Belated Action timeframe
units.text:
Post Open Season within Belated Action timeframe
Scenario: If the caller (Sponsor) states they made an enrollment ‘mistake’ and enrolled family members, but now wishes coverage as the Primary.
Action to be taken: Create a ticket Primary/Disenrollment (not an inactivation AWD) under the incorrect account; Register the Sponsor, then create a Primary/ Create Enrollment AWD which needs to include dependents, plan information and ABW if applicable, for the enrollment to be processed.
Talking Points: Premium will be refunded from disenrolled account and double deductions will occur for belated Sponsor enrollment.

units.heading: Outside Open Season within 60 days of QLE
units.text:
Outside Open Season within 60 days of QLE
Scenario: If the caller (Sponsor) states they made an enrollment ‘mistake’ (within 60 days of QLE event date) and enrolled family members, but now wishes coverage as the Primary.
Action to be taken: Create a ticket Primary /Disenrollment (not an inactivation AWD) under incorrect account; Register the Sponsor, then create a Primary/Create Enrollment AWD which needs to include the dependents, QLE date, plan information and ABW, if applicable for the enrollment to be processed.
Talking Points: Premium refund on disenrolled account and double deductions for new Sponsor Enrollment; a gap in coverage may occur.

units.heading: Outside Open Season
units.text:
Outside Open Season
Scenario: Any request to create Sponsor as Primary for already enrolled family member under FEDVIP
Action to be taken: Primary/Inactivation ticket terminating FEDVIP coverage for ineligible family members.
Talking Points: Advise Sponsor open season to enroll and cover family members; coverage for ineligible family members will terminate (provide coverage end date), premiums will not be refunded.
*See page 2

slides.title: Adding Sponsors Outside of Open Season

units.heading: Steps to take on the first two scenarios:
units.text:
Steps to take on the first two scenarios:
- Create Primary/ Disenrollment ticket on incorrect account, reference the Create Enrollment AWD ticket in the comments box in AWD.
- ​Register the Sponsor (Create their account).
- Create Primary/Create Enrollment with all the information needed for the new enrollment and reference AWD Disenrollment ticket in the comment box in AWD.
- ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​There is no time frame as to when the enrollment will be completed.
- The enrollee will receive confirmation of enrollment once the ticket is processed.

units.heading: Adding or Removing Family Members in a Self and Family Plan
units.text: If the enrollee has a Self and Family plan, the enrollee has the option to add or remove family members. Family members are eligible to be added to Self and Family plans if a Self and Family plan exists; however, to receive services, they must be listed on the enrollment.

units.heading: Adding or Removing Family Members in a Self and Family Plan
units.text:
To manage the family members in a Self and Family plan, click the applicable FEDVIP program card. The family members who are currently on the enrollment will display on the program card.
Senior Reps can process additions or removals of family members by selecting Manage Family.
On the Covered Family screen, you will have access to:
- View/Edit each family member
- Add Family to Coverage
- Remove Family from Coverage
- See Inactive Family Members

units.heading: Note:
units.text:
Note:
Additions: The effective date of the added dependent is retro to the date the plan became SF, or the DOB of the dependent being added.
Removals: The effective date of the dependent being removed should be the last day of the current pay period (prospective).
The exception to this is a removal due to death or divorce. Use the actual QLE event date in this instance.
conditions: Note:

slides.title: Adding or Removing Family Members in a Self and Family Plan

units.heading: Add Family to Coverage
units.text:
Add Family to Coverage
- On the Covered Family screen, select Add Family to Coverage
- Select the family member(s) to add to the enrollment, then click Next.
- You may need to add the family member(s) by clicking Add Family Member.
- When adding a new family member, gather the following information:
- Relationship to primary
- Name
- Gender
- Date of birth
- Family member’s date of eligibility
- Family member’s residential address
- Review the changes and read the Family Member Certification scripting to the caller.
- Advise the caller the carrier should reflect the enrollment in their system in 3-5 business day.
conditions: Note: The effective date of the added dependent is retro to the date the plan became SF, or the DOB of the dependent being added.

units.heading: Remove Family from Coverage
units.text:
Remove Family from Coverage
Members cannot remove dependents without a QLE and should always use the QLE flow to remove a dependent.
- On the Covered Family screen, select Remove Family from Coverage.
- Select the reason the Family Member(s) are being removed.
- Select the family member(s) to remove, then click Next.
- Enter the date of ineligibility:
- Ineligible: QLE date is last day of the current pay period.
- Never Eligible: If family was added in the current year, QLE date is the day prior to the effective date. If family member was added in a previous year, enter 12/31/XX of the year prior to the current plan year.
- Review the changes and select Save.
- Advise the caller the carrier should reflect the enrollment in their system in 3-5 business day.

units.heading: What is an Administrative Leave?
units.text:
What is an Administrative Leave?
- Administrative leave (also referred to as “excused absence”) is an administratively authorized absence from duty without loss of pay or change to leave.
- Administrative leave has no impact to enrollee benefits or premium deductions from their agency.
- Enrollees on Administrative Leave continue to be eligible for the FEDVIP and will receive FEDVIP coverage without disruption, unless their status changes.
Agent Actions:
- If you receive a call from an enrollee concerned about how administrative leave will affect their benefits:
- Assure them that is will not impact their coverage.
- Let them know their premiums will continue to be deducted as normal.
Talking Points:
I’m on administrative leave. Will my benefits and/or deductions be affected?
"If you are placed on administrative leave, your pay and benefits will continue until you officially separate from employment with the Federal government.“
Is there anything I must do to keep my coverage while on Administrative Leave?
“No. Your coverage will remain in effect so long as you remain on Administrative Leave. If your status with your agency changes to something other than Administrative Leave, that may impact your eligibility for the FEDVIP. If you have further questions, speak with your Agency Benefits Officer or your HR Officer.”

units.heading: Advising of AWD Processing Timeframes
units.text:
Due to system limitations, we will no longer advise customers of Primary and Dependent AWD ticket processing timeframes.
Resolution:
When submitting Primary and Dependent AWD tickets for customers, please confirm the customer’s email address on file then advise them of the following:
“I have submitted a request on your behalf. Your ticket will be processed in the order in which it was received. Once processed, you may check your online account to validate the changes.”
Please do not suggest that customers should call in to check on the status of their ticket.
Exceptions:
- Dependent - Full-time Student Dependents who are being reactivated:
- Advise customers that updates will be made within 3–5 business days.
- Primary - Agency Name Change tickets:
- Advise tickets will be processed within 3 business days.
Other ticket timeframes:
- Enrollment Verification tickets:
- Advise tickets will be processed within 3 business days.
- Correspondence tickets:
- Advise tickets will be processed within 5-7 business days.
- Premium tickets: Premium ticket expectations have not changed. Please see BENEFEDS Premium AWD Work Item job aid.
- Premium Inquiry: Advise tickets will be processed within 3-5 business days.
- Refund Request: Advise tickets will be processed within 3-15 business days.
- Outstanding Refunds: Advise tickets will be processed within 14 business days.

- CIV to CIV
- USM to USM: If billing method is changing

sources.title: AutoSummary FAQ
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/AutoSummary FAQ.pptx

units.heading: What is AutoSummary?
units.text:
What is AutoSummary?
AutoSummary is a tool that listens to your call and automatically creates a comment summarizing the interaction.
Why are we transitioning to AutoSummary?
This transition centers on supporting representatives and improving the customer experience first and foremost. The goal is to make your job easier by removing the burden of detailed after‑call commenting, standardizing what needs to be captured, and allowing you to stay fully engaged with your caller without worrying about crafting notes.
Do I need to review or edit the AutoSummary comment before posting it?
No. Agents do not need to review or edit AutoSummary comments. The comments are designed to be accurate and effective without review.
Do the comments automatically save to the account?
Agents must manually copy and paste the Contact ID and the generated comment into the customer’s comment field. Please reference the Commenting with AutoSummary Job Aid.
What if the call is very short or has limited content?
Short or limited interactions may produce: “No Summarization – Short Interaction.”
Paste this exactly as generated.
Do calls through the Spanish line receive AutoSummary?
No. AutoSummary is not active for the Spanish skill. Calls received through the Spanish line require limited manual commenting. Please reference the Commenting with AutoSummary Job Aid.
Do I need to comment calls where a supervisor takes over?
No. If a supervisor takes over the call, they will complete the comment. You should return to Available status.
How does this impact QA process?
QA will only confirm that you copied and pasted the AutoSummary Comment as presented and that the Contact ID was captured.

units.heading: What if the AutoSummary contains PHI or PII?
units.text:
What if the AutoSummary contains PHI or PII?
Do not paste PHI/PII. Omit this information before saving the comment in the account. Notify your Team Lead anytime PHI/PII appears in the output.
When will I need to manually comment instead of using AutoSummary?
You must manually comment when:
• Spanish speaking calls
• When an AutoSummary Error presents or the disposition window is blank
• The system is experiencing issues
• PII/PHI appears (must remove this from the generating comment before saving in the account)
What do I do when I get a call from a customer and I don’t have a lot of details in comments from a previous interaction?
Practicing active listening and engaging in productive dialogue with the customer is the best way to understand a customer's request or concern. If their concern is regarding a prior transaction, utilize resources such as the transaction log, Image, Chorus, and LEARN to gather the details needed to resolve their inquiry.
Should agents still use comment templates?
No. Comment templates are no longer needed under the new requirements.
conditions: Do not paste PHI/PII. Omit this information before saving the comment in the account. Notify your Team Lead anytime PHI/PII appears in the output.

units.heading: BENEFEDS CXone Steady State QA Processes
units.text:
Refer to the steps below to view and act on your QA evaluations in CXone.
Call Review
- Please take the time to carefully review your evaluation and listen to the recording. NOTE: If you are scheduled 15 minutes of QA coaching time, reviewing your evaluation should be done during this time.
- For Instructions on viewing your QA evaluation, see: CXone softphone-QA Evaluations.
Acknowledgement
- Once you have reviewed your QA, and you don’t have any questions or concerns, select “Acknowledge” within 5 business days of receipt.
- If you have received a critical error, you will be coached by a Team Lead prior to receiving the evaluation in CXone. Once you have received the critical error evaluation, please “Acknowledge” within 2 business days of receipt. NOTE: Once you have acknowledged your evaluation, the evaluation is complete. The Request Review option will not be available.
Request Review
Agents may appeal a score and request reconsideration when warranted.
- After receipt of your QA, reach out to your Team Lead with any questions or concerns. Appeals must be submitted within 5 business days of receipt.
- Your team lead will review your QA and determine if a reconsideration is warranted.
- If reconsideration is warranted, your team lead will log the appeal in SharePoint and instruct you to select “Request Review”. If not warranted, you will be required to “Acknowledge” the QA form.
- QA will review your request and send your evaluation back within 3 business days.
- All scoring reconsiderations are final. Once your evaluation is sent back to you, it is automatically acknowledged/completed.
NOTE: You must receive approval from your Team Lead prior to selecting “Request Review” for a QA review. If the above process is not followed, request for your QA review will not be processed.

units.heading: BENEFEDS IVR
units.text:
When contacting BENEFEDS Customer Service, callers encounter an Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system. This IVR offers various options to help route the call to the most suitable agent (including Carriers, PSHB, Login.gov, etc.) and in many instances, offers the caller the ability to self-service their needs.
- The IVR has been designed to be both intuitive and as helpful as possible, providing options for callers to self-service and connect with an agent or organization that will meet their needs while minimizing transfers.
- In addition to the majority of customers successfully navigating the IVR, over a third never have to speak to an agent allowing you to focus on those who need complex support.
- Less than 0.6% of survey respondents stating they were dissatisfied identify the “phone system” as the reason for their dissatisfaction.

units.heading: Talking Points
units.text:
Talking Points:
- The IVR doesn’t accept my entry when I say it/doesn’t understand what I’m saying.
- “I’m sorry your experience wasn’t great. When making a selection in the IVR, make sure you are not on speaker phone and are limiting background noise (televisions, other people talking, etc.).”
- “I’m sorry your experience wasn’t great. The IVR listens for specific spoken commands that are provided. When making a selection, try to repeat the option you want exactly as spoken by the IVR. For example, if the IVR provides “Premium” as an option, you should state only “Premium”.”
- “I’m sorry your experience wasn’t great. Before making a selection in the IVR, allow the IVR to provide all options before making a selection.”
- How do I get through to a live agent faster?
- “I’m sorry you had trouble connecting with us. The quickest way to reach an agent is to listen to the IVR options and provide your selections in clear concise language.”
- “I’m sorry you had trouble connecting with us. The IVR is built to be as helpful as possible while providing options to self-service your needs and connect you with the right individual or group to assist you. I am happy to assist you now.”

units.heading: Important Considerations
units.text:
Important Considerations:
- Most options in the IVR will provide callers the ability to speak with an agent.
- IVR options for services outside of BENEFEDS include the ability to transfer callers to appropriate entities (e.g. Carriers, PSHB, FSA, FLTCIP, Login.gov etc.).
- The IVR, in many instances, provides information that will help callers before they reach an agent, or allows for self-service, 24/7, 365 days a year.
- For callers who authenticate in the IVR, the IVR provides customized responses based on their account information to better support their needs while reducing the number of calls routed to agents.
See page 2 & 3 for an outline of the IVR pathways.
conditions: Important Considerations:

units.heading: BENEFEDS IVR
units.text: The following charts show how a caller can proceed through the IVR. Some IVR options are only available to enrollees who’ve authenticated in the IVR.

units.heading: PROGRAM MENU
units.text:
Step 2: Program Menu (Caller must select one of the options listed below):
- FEDVIP - Asks if they are calling about FEDVIP dental or vision coverage. See step 5 on page 3 for Account Flag options that will present in the IVR for authenticated FEDVIP enrollees.
- PSHB - Provides the phone number for the appropriate PSHB Service Center and will offer to transfer the caller to PSHB directly.
- FEHB - States that BENEFEDS does not administer FEHB and that callers seeking information about FEHB should contact their FEHB insurance carrier or Agency Benefits Officer.
- FSA - Provides the phone number for an FSA Benefits Counselor, or if related to an FSA Allotment will transfer the caller to the BENEFEDS Research line.
- FLTCIP - Provides the option to transfer to the FLTCIP IVR or FLTCIP Billing, and routes to a FLTCIP Customer Service Representative.
- Other - States that BENEFEDS does not administer any other federal insurance benefits and that callers seeking information should contact their insurance carrier, Agency Benefits Officer or visit OPM.gov/insurance.

units.heading: AUTHENTICATION
units.text:
Step 3: Authentication
- The caller will be requested to provide their Social Security Number and Date of Birth (Partial Authentication).
- The IVR will also check to see if the caller is calling from the phone number listed on their account (Full Authentication).
- If three pieces of security information are obtained, you will not have to collect further security information as they are considered fully authenticated.
- Customers who don’t have an account or don’t enter their information skip this step and proceed as a non-authenticated caller (No Authentication).

units.heading: DENTAL OR VISION
units.text:
Step 4: FEDVIP Dental or Vision Selection
- If selecting FEDVIP from the Program Menu, the caller is asked to specify which program they want to discuss, Dental or Vision.

units.text: MAIN MENU OR ACCOUNT FLAGS

units.text:

- These menu options allow the caller to narrow down the reason for their call.
- ID Card, Claims, Provider Networks (Insurance)
- Provides information on current carrier or a carrier of their choosing (IVR provides a list of carriers).
- Offers to transfer the caller to carrier(s) but not an agent.
- Enroll in FEDVIP Plan (Enroll)
- Offers to compare plans and rates.
- Offers to connect the caller with an agent to process their QLE or enrollment (or OS enrollment depending on the date).
- Retirement Inquiries (Retirement)
- Provides information on the transition to retirement and explains how to make payment on BENEFEDS.gov.
- Offers to connect the caller with an agent.
- Premiums or Billing (Premium)
- Offers to compare plans and rates.
- Offers to connect the caller with a billing agent.
- Assistance with BENEFEDS Website (Web help)
- Can transfer callers to Login.gov, update a BENEFEDS phone number, or provide BENEFEDS.gov navigational support.
- Offers to connect the caller with an agent.

units.text:
Account Flags (Authenticated Enrollees Only)
- Some FEDVIP accounts may contain “flags” that provide customized responses, while accounts without these flags will be sent to the Main Menu.
- Recent Enrollment
- Offers to summarize the enrollee’s recent enrollment and advises when ID cards can be expected.
- Recent Change
- Offers to recap the account’s recent changes and provides the effective date.
- Recent Disenrollment
- Asks the enrollee if they are calling to enroll in the same plan.
- If during Open Season, the IVR will allow them to enroll.
- Recent Retirement

- Direct Billing
- Advises of any Termination Warning Letters sent, the date payment is due, and how to make payment.

units.heading: BENEFEDS Login.gov Support
units.text:
Even after customers have linked their accounts, they may still experience issues accessing their My BENEFEDS account and reach out to us for help. While our ability to assist with Login.gov related access issues is limited, we want to ensure every caller receives excellent service. ​
Below is a general script that can be used for a majority of calls we need to defer to login.gov for assistance. Understanding that this may not suit all calls, on the subsequent pages of this job aid are more specific scenario-based options.

units.heading: Deferring Customers to Login.gov with care (General Response)
units.text:
Deferring Customers to Login.gov with care (General Response):
"It looks like you're having trouble signing in through Login.gov. Since we don’t have access to their system, the best next step is to visit login.gov/help for assistance. I can assist you with FEDVIP enrollments, profile updates or billing questions. Do you need any assistance with those while I have you on the phone?”
What is Login.gov? ​“Login.gov is a secure sign-in used by many government websites. You’ll use it instead of your old username and password to access you’re My BENEFEDS Account.”​
​Why is this change happening? ​“OPM is switching to Login.gov to improve security and make it easier to access multiple federal services with one login.”​
​How do I sign-in?​ "The next time you sign in to your My BENEFEDS account, you will see a button labeled 'Sign in with Login.gov.' Clicking it will guide you through the steps to either connect or create your Login.gov account to your My BENEFEDS Account." ​
For additional talking points on specific scenarios, such as sign in issues or authentication challenges, please refer to page two of this Job Aid.
❓ Before You Assist the Caller Know Where They’re At. Here are some key questions to guide you. ​
- Is this their first time signing in to Login.gov? Or are they trying to sign in after already linking their accounts?​
- Do they already have a Login.gov account? If not, they’ll need to create one before linking. Reference the appropriate Job Aid to support them.​
- Do they already have a My BENEFEDS account?

units.heading: Transferring Callers to Login.gov
units.text:
Transferring Callers to Login.gov:
Callers who need to speak with a Login.gov representative can be transferred to them using the address book entry with the toll-free number in CXone (similar to how we handle carrier transfers).
Linking Their Login.gov and My BENEFEDS Accounts
If customers need assistance initially linking their Login.gov and My BENEFEDS accounts, there are separate job aids that can assist you in walking the customer through the initial linking process.
- BENEFEDS.gov: Create Account
- BENEFEDS.gov: Linked Account Sign In
- BENEFEDS.gov: Unlinked Account Sign In

units.heading: Fixing Incorrect Login.gov Account Connections
units.text:
| Initial Account Linking Issues | General Talking Points/Instructions |
| Fixing Incorrect Login.gov Account Connections | What Happens / - Login.gov connects to BENEFEDS accounts using a unique 36-character UUID (Universally Unique Identifier). / - Once linked, a UUID cannot be removed, only overwritten by linking a different Login.gov account. / - If an enrollee used a spouse’s or family member’s Login.gov account, the wrong UUID is stored. / How to resolve / To fix this, the spouse or family member must link their BENEFEDS account to their own Login.gov account first. / - This will overwrite the UUID linked to their BENEFEDS account. / - Once overwritten, the enrollee can then link their own account to their Login.gov account. / Quick Fix Steps (Login.gov Users) / - Have the incorrect account owner sign in: / - They must sign in using their own Login.gov account. / - If they don’t have one, they must create one using a unique email address (their own email, cannot match any other Login.gov users). / - Locate their account by using one of the following: / - BENEFEDS User ID / - Last Name + SSN + DOB / - Request the one-time passcode (OTP): / - OTP must go to the email or phone already established on their BENEFEDS account. / - Entering the OTP links Login.gov and overwrites the old UUID. / - The enrollee can now link their own Login.gov account. / - Once the wrong UUID is replaced, the enrollee can successfully link their own Login.gov account. / Alternate Process (Profile Only BENEFEDS Accounts) / If the spouse or family member’s account is a profile only (no enrollment history): / - Delete the profile, which will remove the stored UUID. / - Follow all HIPAA and security procedures to delete the profile. / - After deletion, the enrollee can recreate their account and link their Login.gov account. |

units.text: 5. Customer Experience

units.heading: BENEFEDS Open Season QA Companion Guide
units.text:
Goal: Provide a positive experience for the caller by incorporating the following behaviors into your communication and call handling.
- Active Listening: Provide undivided attention to caller. Avoid interrupting or talking over the caller. Avoid having the caller repeat the same information. Actively listen to ensure understanding of the customer’s issue.
- Efficiency: Keep conversation business related and avoid prolonging conversation more than necessary. Avoid long pauses and excessive dead air. Utilize the hold procedure when more time is needed to research the account or take an action. Check back in with the customer after having them on hold for 4 minutes. Follow the appropriate transfer/escalation procedure when necessary.
- Genuine Tone: Establish a sincere and positive tone throughout the call. Convey a true desire to understand and help the caller.
- Match Pace: Do not rush the call, and slow down or pick up the pace to match the needs of the customer as necessary.
- Professionalism: Be confident with the information provided and use courtesies such as “please” and “thank you”. Avoid sounding busy/distracted and avoid slipping into an overly casual manner of speaking. Use proper grammar, speak clearly, and avoid filler words such as excessive “yeahs”, “yeps”, “um’s” etc.
- Empathy/Diffusion (When applicable): Acknowledge customer’s frustration and apologize for any errors made. Demonstrate genuine empathy
when a caller is upset. Attempt to diffuse any negative feelings by providing options or alternatives when appropriate.

units.heading: BENEFEDS Role in FLTCIP
units.text: FLTCIP (Federal Long Term Care Insurance Program) provides long term care insurance for the Federal family (including active and retired family). It assists in paying for care when someone in a nursing home or can no longer perform certain activities of daily living.

units.heading: BENEFEDS administer the following aspects of the FLTCIP program:
units.text:
- BENEFEDS administer the following aspects of the FLTCIP program:
- Coordinates FLTCIP Premium deductions from the enrollee’s paycheck

units.heading: Customer Experience
units.text: Goal: Provide a positive experience for the caller by incorporating the following behaviors into your communication and call handling.

units.heading: Customer Experience Score · 5.1 Active Listening
units.text: | 5.1 Active Listening | • Provide undivided attention to caller • Avoid interrupting or talking over the caller • Avoid having the caller repeat the same information |

units.heading: Customer Experience Score · 5.2 Clear/Simple Language
units.text: | 5.2 Clear/Simple Language | • Use proper grammar and avoid filler words such as excessive “yeah”, “yep”, “um” etc. • Avoid any internal jargon or acronyms the caller will not understand |

units.heading: Customer Experience Score · 5.3 Efficiency
units.text: | 5.3 Efficiency | • Keep conversation business related and avoid prolonging conversation more than necessary • Avoid long pauses and excessive dead air • Utilize the hold procedure when more time is needed to research the account or taking an action • Check back in with the customer after having them on hold for 2 minutes • Follow the appropriate transfer/escalation procedure when necessary |

units.heading: Customer Experience Score · 5.4 Genuine Tone
units.text: | 5.4 Genuine Tone | • Establish a sincere and positive tone throughout the call • Convey a true desire to understand and help the caller |

units.heading: Customer Experience Score · 5.5 Match Pace
units.text: | 5.5 Match Pace | • Do not rush the call • Slow down or pick up the pace to match the needs of the customer as necessary |

units.heading: Customer Experience Score · 5.6 Professionalism
units.text: | 5.6 Professionalism | • Be confident with the information provided, and use courtesies such as please and thank you • Avoid sounding busy/distracted • Avoid slipping into an overly casual manner of speaking |

units.heading: Customer Experience Score · 5.7 Empathy/Diffusion
units.text: | 5.7 Empathy/Diffusion | • Acknowledge customer’s frustration and apologize for any errors made • Demonstrate genuine empathy when a caller is upset • Attempt to diffuse any negative feelings by providing options or alternatives when appropriate • Apologize for any errors made |

units.heading: Critical Errors
units.text:
IMPORTANT:
• Below are the behaviors that are not tolerated on any call
• Any of the below behaviors will result in a critical error for the call
conditions: IMPORTANT:

units.heading: Critical Errors
units.text:
Failure To Correctly Verify Security Information
1. Failure to confirm the caller’s name and verify it matches the account will result in a critical error.
2. In the event that adequate security information is not verified (2 pieces for basic security; 3 pieces for high security), or in the event that account specific information is disclosed to an unauthorized third party, this will result in a critical error.

units.heading: Critical Errors
units.text:
Clear Unprofessionalism
In the event of an intentional disconnect (different from an inappropriate caller); argumentative or defamatory language; malicious intent; or failure to escalate to a supervisor when available, these behaviors will result in a critical error.

sources.file: L1 Job Aids/BENEFEDS.gov Create Account.pptx

units.heading: BENEFEDS.gov: Create Account (1/2)
units.text:
This resource demonstrates how enrollees will create a BENEFEDS.gov account. This flow is also what enrollees will see if they attempt to sign into or retrieve an account but are unsuccessful (don’t have an existing account).
- If they already have a My BENEFEDS account but have just not linked it to their Login.gov account, see the BENEFEDS.gov: Unlinked Account Sign In Job Aid.
- If the customer tried to locate their account but it wasn't found and they still believe they have one, check the system. If an account exists, confirm that their information is accurate.

units.heading: BENEFEDS.gov: Create Account (1/2)
units.text:
Once you have confirmed the customer needs to create a My BENEFEDS account, provide a brief overview of the process.
“If you have not done so already you will start by creating a Login.gov account. Then you will go to BENEFEDS.gov to create your My BENEFEDS account by selecting "Get Started." You we be asked to authenticate your Login.gov account at this time before entering in your information for your BENEFEDS account. Once these steps are complete, they’ll be linked automatically. Would you like me to stay on the phone while you go through this process?”
If the customer would like you to stay on the phone. Use the below steps for guidance.

units.heading: BENEFEDS.gov: Create Account (1/2)
units.text:
To begin the create account process:
- Get Started. From the Sign In page on BENEFEDS.gov, select the Get Started button.
- This is located under Don’t have a My BENEFEDS account?

units.heading: BENEFEDS.gov: Create Account (1/2)
units.text:
- Authenticate their Login.gov Account. The customer will be redirected to Login.gov to sign in and verify their identity.
- They will enter their Login.gov email address and password to begin the process.
- They will be required to authenticate by entering the one-time code they will receive in the authentication app they set up when they created their Login.gov account, or
- They may also authenticate by receiving a code via text or voice call. To do this, click Choose another authentication method under the Having Trouble? text.

units.heading: BENEFEDS.gov: Create Account (2/2)
units.text: - Create a MY BENEFEDS Account. After authenticating on Login.gov, users will be redirected back to BENEFEDS.gov and will proceed through the Create Account flow as normal.

units.heading: BENEFEDS.gov Unauthorized Login Attempt
units.text: BENEFEDS.GOV: Unauthorized Login Attempt

units.heading: Customer Reports Unauthorized Login Attempt
units.text: If a customer calls to report that their BENEFEDS.gov account may have been compromised, follow these steps

units.heading: Customer Reports Unauthorized Login Attempt
units.text:
- Secure the account.
- Recommend the customer review or update their security information on Login.gov.
- RECOMMENDATION: Customers should consider changing their biometric or other multi-factor authentication method on Login.gov.
- Suggest they change their password online and set up a bio key, if they’ve not done so already.
- REMINDER: BENEFEDS is unable to assist customers with setting up or changing passwords on Login.gov. For assistance, they will need to contact Login.gov.
- Account Remediation
- Review the account for any unauthorized changes to the enrollment or PII.
- Update any invalid information.
- REQUIRED ACTION: Consult with a Team Lead if there are any unauthorized enrollment changes.
- Review Login.gov History
- Suggest they navigate to their account page on Login.gov and review History for recently used devices and sign-ins.
conditions: REMINDER: BENEFEDS is unable to assist customers with setting up or changing passwords on Login.gov. For assistance, they will need to contact Login.gov.

units.heading: Escalated Concerns
units.text: For customers who escalate their concerns, you may advise that Login.gov uses advanced fraud detection and secure authentication methods to safeguard their account. If the customer continues to escalate the issue, advise that BENEFEDS will follow up if more information is needed.

units.heading: Belated Action Request Form
units.text:
If a customer missed their enrollment window, they have a potential opportunity to enroll outside the window based on a belated action.
There are two main situations that customers would miss enrollment:
- They missed a QLE, such as newly hired, marriage , loss of insurance, acquiring an eligible family member and return from active duty.
- They missed the Open Season enrollment period.
Time Frames: 3 months after the missed opportunity.
Providing a Belated Action Request Form:
Belated Action Request Forms are provided to customers who meet specific criteria (see below reasons) and have 1 of 3 of the valid reasons for not enrolling or making changes within their 60-day window.
- You did not have a phone, or computer during the entire duration.
- Experienced an immediate death in the family.
- You had a significant medical emergency for yourself, or an immediate family member and you were unable to perform your requested action.
Note: If none if these reasons apply do not offer a Belated Action Request Form
Criteria Verification:
- Representatives should review the first Talking Point in this document to assess eligibility for a Belated Action Request Form.
- If eligible and within the three-month period for requesting belated actions, the form can be provided by the following methods:
Distribution Methods:
- Over the Phone: Direct callers to go to BENEFEDS.gov and click on the Review Your Options button on the site’s landing page. They will be able to download the BAR form on their own.
- Via Email: Inform the caller that the link will be sent to their email through a Correspondence AWD Work Item.
- Mail or Fax: For customers without internet access, mail or fax the form after creating a Correspondence AWD Work Item.
Note: A registration must be on file to provide the form. If the caller has not registered with BENEFEDS and is unwilling to do so, approval from a Team Lead is required to proceed with the request.

units.heading: Belated Open Season Actions (L1)
units.text: Use the scripting below when a customer requests an Open Season action, after Open Season has ended.

units.heading: Belated Open Season Actions (L1)
units.text:
“FEDVIP regulations do not allow for enrollments or changes outside of Open Season unless the action is due to a new hire event or a valid qualifying life event. However, there are some rare circumstances in which your enrollment in the program at the appropriate time was not possible for reasons outside of your control. For these instances, BENEFEDS may allow a belated action. Keep in mind, you must supply a detailed description of your situation and BENEFEDS has the right to request documentation from you to confirm the reason provided. If you are no more than 3 months outside of Open Season AND you fall into one of the following circumstances, you may be eligible for a belated action:
- You had no access to a telephone or Internet for the entire duration of the Federal Benefits Open Season.
- You had a significant medical emergency for yourself or an immediate family member for a significant portion of the Federal Benefits Open Season and you were unable to perform your requested action during that time.
- A member of your immediate family passed away during the Federal Benefits Open Season, and you were unable to perform your requested action during that time.”
”Do you fall into one of the categories I just read?”

units.heading: If above criteria is met…
units.text:
If above criteria is met…
- Confirm the caller is registered in the CS System. If the caller is not registered, complete the registration. -Direct the caller to download the form off BENEFEDS.gov from the Review Your Options button on the main page.
- If they have no access to the internet, escalate the call to a Senior Rep. to have the form mailed.
- Advise that the form must be returned to BENEFEDS by March 8th, 2026.

units.heading: If above criteria is NOT met…
units.text:
If above criteria is NOT met…
- Let the customer know…
- “In order to submit a form, you must fall into one of the categories I previously stated. If you do not fall into one of the categories it is extremely unlikely that your request for a belated action will be approved.”
- If the customer continues to request a form, you may provide them with the link to the form.

units.heading: If a belated action is approved…
units.text:
If a belated action is approved…
- Escalate to a Senior Rep.
Note: Customer will receive a letter indicating whether they were approved or denied by mail.
If approved, the customer will need to contact Customer Service to process their belated action. They CANNOT do so on BENEFEDS.gov
conditions: Note: Customer will receive a letter indicating whether they were approved or denied by mail.

sources.title: CXone Call Storage and Retrieval
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/CXone Call Storage and Retrieval.pptx

units.heading: CXone: Call Storage and Retrieval
units.text:
Why do we need to keep these call recordings? We have a contractual obligation to maintain storage of call recordings for a rolling 24-month period for all business lines.
What happens to the calls after 24 months? As each recording meets the 24-month storage period, it will be deleted by the system.
As business needs warrant, it may be necessary to access a recording stored in the CxOne environment. This job aid will outline the process for accessing these call recordings.
How are calls in CXone retained?
- Call recordings will be kept in short-term storage for no more than 180 days from the date of the call. After this time, the recording will be moved into long-term storage.
- Once the call is migrated into the long-term storage it will remain there until it reaches the 24-month retention requirement at Noon ET. After this, the call will be systematically purged from the long-term storage buckets.
If you use the Interactions module to listen to call recordings, it is very easy to discern whether a recording is in short-vs-long term storage.
Using the screen shot below, you can see the channel type icon is bold, as is the playback button to the right:

units.heading: CXone: Call Storage and Retrieval
units.text: If the recording has been moved to long-term storage, the channel and playback icons will be grayed out:

units.heading: CXone: Call Storage and Retrieval
units.text: In addition, if you hover one of the channel icons, you will see the following pop-up message:

units.heading: CXone: Call Storage and Retrieval
units.text: How to identify the master contact ID:

units.heading: CXone: Call Storage and Retrieval
units.text:
What to do if you require access to a recording in long-term storage:
- Submit a ServiceNow request with the following information:
- Indicate in the request that you need to retrieve a call recording that is currently in long-term storage.
- Provide the Master contact ID. See screen shot on previous page on how to properly identify the Master contact ID.
- Provide date of call.
- Provide the agent's name who received the first leg of the call.
- Advise how long the call recording will be needed. Please provide a specific date (example: May 20, 2023).
- If a time span is given, rather than an end date, the contact center support team will apply an approximate end date to the order, based on the timeline provided.
- If no end date or time span is given, the contact center support team will place the end date as one week from the receipt of the help desk ticket.
- Once the contact center support team receives the ticket, an online retrieval order will be placed through CXone to retrieve the recording. The retrieval time can take up to 6 hours to complete.
- Once the contact center support team has confirmed completion of the request, they will give the requestor an update advising the order has been completed.
- The file will be available for playback in the short-term environment until the end date noted in the retrieval order. After which time, the recording will be returned to long-term storage.

- If later: “I’m sorry, but we’re not able to reschedule callbacks. Our Contact Center is available Monday – Friday (current season operating hours). Please call us back when it’s convenient for you.”
Caller calls in because they never got called back: “

units.heading: CXone: Disconnected Calls
units.text:
If a customer disconnects during an active call, you are required to call them back immediately.
Exceptions: Upset or abusive callers, or they hang up because they don’t like or disagree with the information you’ve provided.

units.heading: CXone: Disconnected Calls
units.text:
Consider the following:
- If a customer disconnects an active call on their end, the agent will see an immediate status of ACW.
- Confirm the status of Held Party Abandoned (if the call was disconnected while on hold).
- If a caller disconnects during a call, the agent is to follow the process for an outbound call and call them back immediately.
- Follow all outbound call procedures; the call will be treated as unauthenticated.
- After the call, comment the account noting that you placed an outbound call to the customer due the call dropping.

units.heading: CXone: Disconnected Calls
units.text:
Agent Actions for Disconnected Calls:
- Confirm you have a status of ACW.
- Confirm the Held Party Abandoned status (if dropped while on hold).
- Place yourself in Unavailable – Outbound Call status in softphone.
- Dial the number the customer called from or the phone number(s) on their account and follow standard outbound call procedures:
- Use the appropriate greeting. Provide your name and that you are calling on behalf of BENEFEDS.
“Hello, my name is ___; I am calling from BENEFEDS. BENEFEDS administers the Federal Employee Dental and Vision Insurance Program.”
- Advise that you are on a recorded line.
- Confirm the customer’s first and last name.
- Verify three pieces of security. All outbound calls are treated as unauthenticated calls.
- If a third-party answers, follow all outbound call procedures for third parties. Do not provide account specifics unless the third party is authorized, or you obtain verbal authorization from the primary enrollee.
- If the primary account holder is unavailable and leaving a voicemail is possible, do not provide account specifics:
“Hello, this message is for ____. I’m calling from BENEFEDS; BENEFEDS administers the Federal Employee Dental and Vision Insurance Program. It is important we speak to ____. Please contact our office at 877-888-3337. We are available Monday – Friday, 9AM – 7PM Eastern time. Thank you, have a nice day.”

units.heading: CXone: Escalation Procedures
units.text: This job aid will instruct you on how to refer an escalated call or request for a manager to a supervisor.

units.heading: CXone: Escalation Procedures
units.text:
- Reach out to your Supervisor via Microsoft Teams with the following information about the caller:
- Customer’s Name
- Customer’s Member ID
- A brief description of the reason for the escalation
- Assure the customer you have contacted a supervisor:
Say, “(Mr./Ms. Customer’s name), I have reached out to my supervisor, and they will be joining us shortly. Thank you for your patience.”
3. Wait for your supervisor to join the call and allow them to introduce themselves.
- Once they have established themselves, they will take over the call.
- Do not disconnect the call, the supervisor will take the call over when ready.
- Before the takeover, copy and paste the Contact ID and write “Supervisor Takeover” in the account comments.
- You will not use AutoSummary for the takeover.
- You will be placed into Available status once the supervisor takes over the call.
*Note: Escalated calls cannot be transferred, and you must wait for your supervisor to join the call in order for it to be handled correctly.
conditions: Do not disconnect the call, the supervisor will take the call over when ready.

units.heading: CXone: Handling Escalated Calls (Supervisor)
units.text:

Note: You must be connected to the Agent Leg in softphone and the Supervisor dashboard to access these features. To sync the dashboard and softphone, log out of softphone, connect to the supervisor dashboard, then log into the softphone again.
conditions: Note: You must be connected to the Agent Leg in softphone and the Supervisor dashboard to access these features. To sync the dashboard and softphone, log out of softphone, connect to the supervisor dashboard, then log into the softphone again.

units.heading: CXone: Handling Escalated Calls (Supervisor)
units.text:
- After joining the call say, “Hello (customer’s name), this is (your name) and I will be handling your call.”
- Thank the agent and assume the call by selecting the Takeover option in your CXone Supervisor application.
- During the Takeover, the agent will be forced back into Available with no ACW.
- The agent will be required to copy and paste the Contact ID as well as manually comment “Supervisor Takeover”.
- The TL/Sup must also copy and paste the Contact ID and recap the call with a manual comment of anything discussed on the Sup level, (Requests, outcomes/directions provided).
Note: The Takeover option will be available after successfully joining a call and is accessible in the Supervisor Application only. You will not have the Takeover option in the softphone Panel.
conditions: Note: The Takeover option will be available after successfully joining a call and is accessible in the Supervisor Application only. You will not have the Takeover option in the softphone Panel.

units.heading: CXone: Troubleshooting Audio
units.text: When you have experienced audio issues, attempt the troubleshooting steps below.

units.heading: CXone: Troubleshooting Audio
units.text:
Caller Reports Background Noise: May occur when working in-office due to the proximity of our cubicles.
- Advise the caller, “Thank you for letting me know. I apologize for the background noise. Our agents are currently speaking with multiple callers, but I’m here to make sure you are fully taken care of.”
- Do not report the complaint to IT.
conditions: Do not report the complaint to IT.

units.heading: CXone: Troubleshooting Audio
units.text:
Caller Reports they Cannot Hear You:
- Check the mute button on your headset.
- Check that your system’s sound is not muted.
- Follow additional troubleshoot steps below if issue persists.

units.heading: CXone: Troubleshooting Audio
units.text: Agent Leg Continues to Disconnect During Call: Check your browser settings to ensure CXone is set to never fall asleep.

units.heading: CXone: Troubleshooting Audio
units.text:
- Select the Settings and more button.
- Select Setting.
- Go to System and performance.
- Select Performance.
- Scroll down to the section labeled "Never put these sites to sleep”.
- Ensure CXone is listed (https://cxagent.nicecxone-gov.com). If not, copy and paste the URL (available in the job aid description box) to the Add site button.

units.heading: CXone: Troubleshooting Audio
units.text:
Adjusting Headset Sound Settings:
- Type Sound Settings in the Search Window.
- Click Sound Settings.
Input (Microphone):
- Microphone Array (is the laptop microphone).
- Click the radial button for the External Microphone (it may say headset).
- Click the arrow to the right of Microphone Array.
- Click Don’t Allow (disables the laptop microphone).
- Click Sound (brings you back to previous screen).
Output (Hearing Sound)
- Current sound setting will be selected (laptop or monitor).
- Click the radial button for your headset.
- Click the arrow on the right-hand side for the previous setting. (May have multiple options displaying. Complete this step until only your headset remains.)
- Click Don’t Allow this will disable this sound option.
- Click Sound (brings you back to previous screen).
Final Steps: Close your CXone Agent by selecting the Log Out status > Log Out. Log back into your CXone Agent, connect your Agent Leg and go Available.

units.heading: CXone: Troubleshooting Audio
units.text:
Additional Audio Troubleshoot Steps: Finish your call and comment the account first.
- Inform your TL/SME/Admin and set your status to “Unavailable System Down”.
- Clear cache. Fully close the browser. Restart your computer.
- Check CXone Extension is installed. Use CXone Softphone: Installing Browser Extension job aid.
- Check browser permissions for Microphone and Pop-ups/Redirects. Use CXone Softphone: Initial Preferences and Setup job aid.
- Double check your system, or headset, is not muted.
- Submit an Employee Center Ticket (POR Agents only) or the TL/SME/Admin will submit a Vendor Help Ticket to report the issue, even if resolved for tracking purposes.

units.heading: CXone: Troubleshooting Audio
units.text:
Steps to Report Audio Issues (PORS agents only):
- In the Employee Service Center, select Report an IT issue.
- Select Telephony.
- Choose the appropriate incident topic. Options include Call Quality, I cannot hear the caller, or The caller cannot hear me.
- Select the appropriate urgency level.
- Identify if you are remote or in office.
- Include the following details in the ticket:
- Browser name.
- Interaction ID, if applicable (you may need to go into All Interactions to copy the last ID provided).
- Specific timestamp if the caller states they can barely hear you or you are coming up choppy.
- If you did a full restart of your system.
- If you switched browsers (e.g., Edge to Chrome).
- If you switched headsets or the USB port that your headset is plugged into.
- If you were able to resolve the issue.
- If you resolved the audio issues, click the Action button in the upper right-hand corner and select Resolve. If the issues are not resolved, leave the ticket open.
- If you resolved the issue but continue to experience problems, you can comment and reopen the ticket by clicking the Actions button in the upper right-hand corner and select Reopen.

sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Call Closing Process - Inbound Calls.pptx

units.heading: Call Closing Process – Inbound Calls
units.text: This Job Aid walks you through the steps for closing a call.

units.heading: Call Closing Process – Inbound Calls
units.text:
STEP 1: Say the appropriate closing script before offering the survey.
Below are some examples of effective ways to stay in control of closing the call.

units.heading: Call Closing Process – Inbound Calls
units.text:
Standard Closing Script:
This script is the standard required statement when closing your call.
Offering Condolences:
When notified of a death, the CSR should sincerely express condolences and thank the caller.
Redirecting the caller:
- Acknowledge the customers comment with warmth
- Smoothly redirect the conversation back to the purpose of the call
- Open the door for conclusion without sounding abrupt
Polite Interruption:
Politely interrupt the customer and let them know that you need to end the call.

units.heading: Call Closing Process – Inbound Calls
units.text:
- “Have I answered all your questions?” “Is there anything else I may assist you with?”
- “Once again, please accept my sincere condolences for your loss, and thank you for taking the time to notify us.”
- “That sounds interesting. I’ve never been deep sea fishing myself! Just to make sure I’ve answered everything you need today, do you have any other questions about [insert topic].”
- “I apologize for interrupting; however, I do want to ensure I have answered all your questions pertaining to [insert topic]. “Is there anything else I may assist you with?”

units.heading: Call Closing Process – Inbound Calls
units.text:
STEP 2: Offer survey and thank them for calling using the following script:
“There is a brief survey at the end of the call; we appreciate your feedback.
Thank you for calling.”
- Select Launch Icon from the softphone panel.
- Select End Call to disconnect the call and send
the caller to the after-call survey.
Remember, you must disconnect the call first for the
customer to be able to answer the survey questions.

units.heading: Call Closing Process – Inbound Calls
units.text:
STEP 3: Comment the account with Autosummary
- After your call has ended, AutoSummary will pop open, but the IVR details will close
- Select the ScreenPop icon to pop up the IVR details. (this will close the disposition window)
- Select the Outcome button to open/close the AutoSummary tool.
- Click the Disposition dropdown and select Complete.
- Complete will be the only option to select.
- Copy and paste both the Contact ID and the generated comment.
- Paste the Contact ID and generated comment into customer’s account comments field and save your comment in the system.
- Return to CXone and in the AutoSummary pop up click Save & Close before returning to available status.
Scenarios Requiring Manual Comments:
- Spanish Speaking Calls (When only Spanish was spoken on the call) – Spanish only calls require comments to be entered manually until AutoSummary is built to handle them.
- CXone Issues (Steady State only) – If there is an issue with CXone and AutoSummary is not available, manually comment “No AutoSummary”.
- Comment Contains PII/PHI - Alert your Team Lead if you see PHI/PII in the comment. Only copy and paste the valid data and omit the PII/PHI.
Important Reminders:
- Short calls may generate a response such as “No Summarization – Short Interaction”. In these instances, paste exactly what AutoSummary has generated.
- QA will no longer scores the content of comments, rather they will check to ensure there is a comment.
- This change will allow QA to assist in refining the AutoSummary technology.
- They will continue to check that a comment was placed on the account (all comments should be written by AutoSummary except for Spanish only calls.)
conditions: Important Reminders:

sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Carrier Concerns.pptx

units.heading: Carrier Concerns
units.text: This job aid is to assist agents in addressing customer issues related to their carriers.

units.heading: Dealing with Predeterminations and Pending Claims:
units.text:
Dealing with Predeterminations and Pending Claims:
- If an enrollee cannot get predetermination authorized by United Concordia or if a provider is withholding services due to unpaid claims, initiate an Enrollment Verification AWD work item.
- For ongoing issues with carrier representatives, consult your team lead for guidance.
- Advise enrollees on pending claims using the appropriate talking points found in the United Concordia section of the Job Aid FEDVIP Carriers, Coverage, Cost & Claims.

units.heading: Dealing with Predeterminations and Pending Claims · Requests for Evidence of Insurance (EOI) or Certificates of Coverage
units.text:
Requests for Evidence of Insurance (EOI) or Certificates of Coverage:
- If carriers push back on providing these documents, use the talking point below to address the issue with the carrier representative.
- If a carrier representative advises that they do not provide Evidence of Insurance (EOI)/Certificate of Coverage: "BENEFEDS is the administrator of enrollment and premium payment processes for the FEDVIP. In this capacity, we do not provide proof of coverage. FEDVIP carriers have the responsibility of providing such documentation."
- Continue to consult your team lead if resistance persists.

units.heading: Dealing with Predeterminations and Pending Claims · Coordination of Benefits
units.text:
Coordination of Benefits:
- Callers with questions about coordination of benefits should contact their FEDVIP carrier. BENEFEDS collects other insurance details (e.g., FEHB/PSHB, Medicare, Medicaid) and Other Insurance to help FEDVIP carriers coordinate benefits. While BENEFEDS updates this information to keep it accurate, any questions about the coordination process itself should be directed to the FEDVIP carrier.

units.heading: Dealing with Predeterminations and Pending Claims · Support for Low Income Housing Applications
units.text:
Support for Low Income Housing Applications:
- Direct enrollees requesting assistance for low-income housing applications to carriers@fedpointusa.com.
Underserved Areas:
- In some instances, enrollees may have difficulty finding a Provider within their Carrier’s network.
- In any area where a FEDVIP dental or vision plan does not meet OPM access standards, including underserved areas, enrollees may receive services from non-network providers.
- If this is the case, advise the customer to communicate with their carrier about potentially being in an Underserved Area.
Note: Carriers may require documentation to verify a dependent’s student status and can hold claim payments until such documentation is provided.
conditions: Note: Carriers may require documentation to verify a dependent’s student status and can hold claim payments until such documentation is provided.

units.heading: Carrier Information
units.text: Carrier Information (when information is available at Carrier and what actions generate new cards)
conditions: Note: GEHA provides EyeMed, a vision benefit as part of their FEDVIP Dental program.

units.heading: When is information sent to the Carrier?
units.text:
When is information sent to the Carrier?
- New Hire and QLE enrollments:
Information is sent to the Carrier and loaded to their system up to 5 business days before the effective date. ID cards or other information sent by the Carrier is mailed out within 15 days of the effective date.
- Updating Contact Information:
Address, phone, email, etc. These changes are sent to the Carrier the next business day and it takes 3-5 business days for the Carrier to load the change to their systems. So, if a customer calls the Carrier before the Carrier loads the information in their system, the Carrier won’t reflect any changes made. If the dependent’s address is different from the primary’s address, GEHA requires the update in writing and GEHA will retain the address in their files.
- Open Season Enrollments, Changes, Cancellations, & Re-enrollments:
BENEFEDS sends all the Open Season information (enrollments, changes, cancellations, etc.) to the Carriers after Open Season ends. It takes the Carriers some time to load all this information into their systems. If the customer calls their Carrier prior to the Carrier loading that information, then it is likely the Carrier won’t reflect any of the updated information. ID cards or other information will be received by January 1st for most new enrollees but should be received by all (when applicable) within 15 business days of January 1st.
Note: Enrollees are able to print their ID cards from the Carriers' websites.

slides.title: Changing Your Time Zone in IEX

units.heading: Changing Your Time Zone in IEX
units.text: IEX Webstation allows agents to change their time zones to accurately reflect where they are working from. In previous versions, Webstation would show agent schedules and time zone information in the time zone of their Management Unit (MU). For agents working outside of their MU’s time zone, their schedules would not reflect the time zone they’re currently in. To set your time zone in IEX:

units.heading: Changing Your Time Zone in IEX
units.text:
- Access your Homepage of IEX Webstation.
- Select Manage My Account by clicking the drop down under your name.
- Under Webstation Time Zone, select the time zone you wish to view your schedule in. Your time zone will be preset to your MU’s Time Zone.

slides.title: Changing Your Time Zone in IEX

units.heading: Changing Your Time Zone in IEX
units.text: While all date and time combinations appear in your preferred time zone, some data may not be converted to your time zone.

units.heading: Information converted to your preferred time zone:
units.text:
Information converted to your preferred time zone:
- Today Is link and Calendar selection
- Schedules including schedule details
- Reminders and Alerts
- Timestamps

units.heading: Information NOT converted to your preferred time zone includes:
units.text:
Information NOT converted to your preferred time zone includes:
- Stats Viewer Data
- Work Journal Data

units.heading: Changing Your Time Zone in IEX
units.text:
Note: The difference between your preferred time zone and your MU’s time zone may cause more than one schedule to be displayed.
When trading your schedule, the schedules display for the dates you have selected to give away and will be shown in your preferred time zone.
conditions: Note: The difference between your preferred time zone and your MU’s time zone may cause more than one schedule to be displayed.

units.heading: Chorus – Agent Workaround
units.text: When Chorus is experiencing technical issues and you’re unable to submit tickets in the system, please utilize the Chorus Log on SharePoint. See below for instructions.

units.heading: Chorus – Agent Workaround
units.text:
Agent Actions:
If an AWD ticket is required, please do the following:
- Locate Chorus Log from the CCC Workspace on the left-hand side.
- Click Add New Item.
- Enter the enrollee’s information.
- Member ID
- First and Last Name
- Action Required
- Enter the necessary information in the appropriate fields within the form.
- Complete the ticket.
- Leave your AWD comments
- Click Save

units.heading: Chorus – Agent Workaround
units.text:
Note:
- Agents need to type a brief explanation for the purpose of the AWD ticket in the SharePoint comments field.
- The Action Needed field in the SharePoint log has been updated to have a correspondence option.
- Correspondence fields are at the bottom of the log.
- Note: Once you are advised AWD (Chorus) is functional again, complete and submit any ticket requests you have logged in SharePoint.
