units.heading: Chorus – Process Steps Explained
units.text:
When checking the status of a ticket in Chorus, be sure you’re looking at any tickets that may have been created to complete the original request.
- On the right, a Primary – Inactivation ticket was originally created to inactivate an account.
- After receipt of the Primary ticket, a new inactivation ticket was created to process the inactivation.
- This is important because the original ticket may be marked as “End” or completed, while the second ticket may still be in processing.

sources.title: Clearing MS Edge Cache
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Clearing MS Edge Cache.pptx

units.heading: Clearing MS Edge Cache
units.text: Microsoft Edge is the recommended browser for all FedPoint systems. At times, you may notice errors with your systems or webpages. Clearing cache can often resolve these issues. Cache is used by a browser to save webpage information, which typically speeds up the browser. However, this information can become outdated or display incorrectly over time..

units.heading: Clear Cache in MS Edge | After Clearing Cache, Agent Checks Microphone
units.text:
- From the MS Edge browser, go to the far right of the top menu (ellipses), and click Settings
- Under Settings, click Privacy, search and services
- Under Clear Browsing Data, select Choose what to clear
- Select All time and check off browsing history, download history, cookies and cached imaged and files
- Scroll down and select Site Permissions, then click Clear Now

units.heading: Clear Cache in MS Edge | After Clearing Cache, Agent Checks Microphone
units.text:
After cache has been cleared, agents must check that MS Edge is connected to their headset. Often clearing cache resets the browser settings, and agents experience microphone issues. Follow the steps below to check that MS Edge can access the microphone.
Check Browser Settings:
- Open Agent in Edge and click on the Lock icon in the web browser (directly to the left of the URL bar)
- Select Allow for the Microphone under the Permissions for this site
Check Desktop Settings:

units.heading: Clear Cache in MS Edge | After Clearing Cache, Agent Checks Microphone
units.text:
- Click the windows button, then click the Settings icon
- Select System
- Select Sound
- Ensure the input device is your headset (Headset names will vary. They may include the name of the brands.)

sources.title: Commenting with AutoSummary
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Commenting with AutoSummary.pptx

units.heading: Steps to Comment an Account Using AutoSummary:
units.text:
Steps to Comment an Account Using AutoSummary:
- After your call has ended, AutoSummary will pop open, but the IVR details will close
- If necessary, select the ScreenPop icon to pop up to locate the Contact ID.
- If the AutoSummary closes, select the Outcome button to reopen the screen.
- Click the Disposition dropdown and select Complete.
- Copy and paste the Contact ID and the generated comment into the customer’s account comments field.
- Return to CXone and in the AutoSummary pop up, click Save & Close.

units.heading: Important Reminders:
units.text:
Important Reminders:
- Verbalize important details and questions (Chorus ticket numbers, Medicare/Medicaid questions, event dates, premium amounts, etc.) to ensure AutoSummary captures those details.
- Calls limited in duration or content may generate a response such as “No Summarization – Short Interaction”. In these instances, paste exactly what AutoSummary has generated.
- For AutoSummary errors, report them via a ticket in the Employee Service Center or other appointed channels.
- QA will not score comment content. They will check that the Contact ID was included, and the AutoSummary was used or the manual comment process on page 2 was followed.
- Calls where a supervisor takeover occurs require the following:
- Copy and paste the Contact ID while on the call with the Supervisor/TL.
- Manually comment the account with “Supervisor Takeover”.
- TLs/Supervisors: See the CXone Handling Escalated Calls (Supervisor) resource for information on takeovers.
- If action is taken on multiple accounts (Ex. Survivor Annuitant calls) follow the steps below:
- Paste the AutoSummary comment and Contact ID on both accounts.
- Paste the Member IDs of the related account to each other.
- AutoSummary is for Customer Service comments only. You are still required to write a comment for Chorus tickets and various SharePoint logs (e.g. Carrier Escalation Log, Escalation Notification Log, VA Benefits Inactivation Log).
conditions: Important Reminders:

units.heading: Manual Commenting Instructions for Agents:
units.text:
Manual Commenting Instructions for Agents:
When AutoSummary cannot be generated due to a CXone or AutoSummary error, when the AutoSummary contains PII or PHI, or when the call is received through the designated Non‑English line, manually comment following the requirements below.
- Copy and paste the Contact ID.
- Document the reason why the caller contacted BENEFEDS in one sentence, using the caller’s own stated reason(s). Include:
- The caller’s explicit reason for calling.
- Any additional issues the caller mentioned.
- Key event dates provided by the caller.
Example: “Caller asked about dental plan premiums and requested help updating their address.”
- Document actions you completed during the call in 2–3 concise sentences, written from your perspective. Include:
- All confirmed actions (e.g., reviewing enrollment details, explaining premiums, updating information, submitting a ticket).
- Specific details about what you reviewed or updated.
- Ticket numbers.
- Any guidance or information you provided that addressed the caller’s issue.
Do NOT include:
- System navigation or procedural steps (e.g., holds, internal checks, system movement).
- Closing call details (e.g. educating on survey).
- Timeframes provided (e.g. 3-5 business day window for updates).
Example: “I verified coverage, explained dental premiums, updated the address, and confirmed the changes.”
Do not include any PII or PHI (such as DOB, SSN, address, phone number, email, or medical information).

sources.title: Communication Options for the Deaf
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Communication Options for the Deaf.pptx

units.heading: Communication Options for the Deaf
units.text:
Customers who are hard of hearing or Deaf can use the 711 Relay Service, BENEFEDS.gov, or email BENEFEDS directly.
711 Relay Service
The 711 Relay Service is a telecommunication service that allows individuals with hearing or speech disabilities to place and receive telephone calls. To access this service, customers will dial 711 and will be connected to a relay service operator who can assist in communicating their message. This service is available across the United States and is free of charge.
Customers will use an operator via a relay service such as 711. The call will come into BENEFEDS as normal. Follow the steps below when handling a relay call.
Relay Calls
- If the customer calling using the relay service already has an account with BENEFEDS, then security information must be verified with the enrollee through the relay operator.
- During a relay call, each statement/question should be delivered in natural conversational tone with the customer.
- The relay operator will assist by communicating between the agent and customer.
Some relay customers may prefer to use "Go Ahead" when communicating via relay services. Agents should follow the relay operators lead whether to use it or not.
- If using the “Go Ahead” approach, the CSR should state “Go ahead” and pause after each message/question(s).
- The “Go ahead” phrase will be the relay operator cue to deliver the message/question(s) to the customer.
- The CSR should wait until the relay operator receives a response back from the customer and delivers a question(s)/answer(s) back.

sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Customers with Multiple ABW Reversals.pptx

units.heading: Customers with Multiple ABW Reversals
units.text: Multiple ABW reversals occur when there are several instances of failed automatic bank withdrawals, typically due to issues like insufficient funds or bank errors, leading to the need for manual intervention or alternative billing methods. Follow the step-by-step process for working with multiple ABW reversals.

units.heading: 1) Check Agency Status in Payroll UI Deduction Tab:
units.text:
1) Check Agency Status in Payroll UI Deduction Tab:
- Verify if the customer’s agency name is listed under Internal POI. (normal customers will display their poi number)
- If present, check their billing status, which should be changed from C – Confirmed to J-Code due to ABW reversals. The J-Code will trigger a letter letting the customer know they will be switched to direct bill, and they can update new banking information to return to ABW.

units.heading: 2) Review Freeze Code:
units.text:
2) Review Freeze Code:
- Look for any entries in the Freeze Code field. A P-Code will display and will not trigger a letter to the customer. Customers with a freeze due to multiple ABWs will not be able to switch back to ABW until the freeze is lifted. (this means bringing their account to current).

units.heading: 3) Examine ABW Transactions in Cash Flow Tab:
units.text:
3) Examine ABW Transactions in Cash Flow Tab:
- Inspect the Action and Amounts columns for patterns of ACH payments followed by reversals.
- Check for Reversal Codes in the Remarks section to understand the reasons behind the ABW reversals.

units.heading: 4) Analyze Billing and Payments Tab for Annuity Issues:
units.text:
4) Analyze Billing and Payments Tab for Annuity Issues:
- Focus on the Annuity row to determine if ABW reversals occurred due to insufficient funds.
- Note any discrepancies in the Payment Amount and YTD columns, which may indicate unresolved payments or further reversals.
conditions: Note any discrepancies in the Payment Amount and YTD columns, which may indicate unresolved payments or further reversals.

units.heading: 5) Consult Comments Tab for Customer History:
units.text:
5) Consult Comments Tab for Customer History:
- Review comments related to past ABW issues, particularly those mentioning insufficient funds.
- Use the Transaction Log to review ABW history over specified date ranges for better clarity.

units.heading: Customers with Multiple ABW Reversals
units.text: Please Note: Customers with accounts frozen due to ABW reversals must bring their accounts current before returning to ABW billing. This means that agents should not be putting in requests to return to ABW if the account isn’t current. Agents should not be submitting Agency Name Change tickets unless the account has been paid in full.

units.heading: Database Reduction
units.text:
Database Reduction enhances daily transaction processing and resource utilization within FedPoint by reducing the volume of online data in the BENEFEDS Customer Service System (CSS), thereby minimizing risks, saving storage space, and reducing overall costs.
Note: Fully archived accounts should NOT be retrieved. A new account should be created.
Data Retention Overview:
- Active Data: Includes information from the current calendar year minus the two previous years.
- Archived Data: Data older than the current year minus two years is archived and not directly accessible in the CSS.
Data Visibility:
- All Data Available: If a customer account has all data within the active timeframe, the message All Data Available will appear in the CSS.
Archived Accounts in the CSS:
- When viewing accounts in the CS System, only accounts with archived data will have a message.
conditions: Note: Fully archived accounts should NOT be retrieved. A new account should be created.

units.heading: Handling Comments:
units.text:
Handling Comments:
- Viewable Comments: All comments, regardless of the year they were made, remain viewable in descending order (most recent first).
- Archived Comments: To view comments from years that have been archived, use the Filters button in the Comment Log and select All Time to adjust the timeframe.

units.heading: Purpose:
units.text:
Purpose:
This initiative supports efficient management of the growing number of DVC & FSA enrollments, aligns with regulatory and data retention policies, and controls the total ownership costs related to data storage.

sources.title: De-escalation Techniques
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/De-escalation Techniques.pptx

units.heading: High Level De-Escalation Techniques
units.text: De-escalation is the process of calming down a caller so that a resolution can be met.

units.heading: High Level De-Escalation Techniques
units.text:
De-escalation techniques often feel unnatural because when we are faced with an intense confrontation, we are naturally driven to fight, flight or freeze. The key to avoiding these pitfalls, though it seems unnatural, is to remain centered and calm, keeping an even tone, a normal volume and neutral pace.
Below is a list of de-escalation techniques that will help facilitate an effective conversation with an angry caller and allow for a satisfactory outcome.

units.heading: High Level De-Escalation Techniques
units.text:
- Remain calm & professional
- Actively listen
- Show empathy

units.heading: High Level De-Escalation Techniques
units.text:
- Repeat back the caller’s issue
- Be sincere & apologize when needed
- Explain the path to resolution

units.heading: High Level De-Escalation Techniques
units.text:
- Don’t take is personally
- Let the caller vent
- Avoid the hold button

units.heading: High Level De-Escalation Techniques
units.text: See the Dealing With Unhappy Callers job aid for more detail.

units.heading: High Level De-Escalation Techniques
units.text:
De-escalation Scripting:
1. “I understand you are upset; I am attempting to assist you; however, in order to do so I will need you to remain professional. If you are unable to do so I will need to disconnect the call”
Once you have given the warning and the caller continues to be abusive, state the following
“Unfortunately, I can not continue the call in an unprofessional manner. I am ending the call now. Once you feel you are able to continue in a professional manner, please feel free to call us back at 1-877-888-3337.”
2. “I am sorry you feel this way, unfortunately we are bound by the rules and regulations set forth by OPM. If you continue to yell or be abusive, I will need to end this call.”
Once you have given the warning and the caller continues to be abusive, state the following
“I apologize, I can not continue the call in an unprofessional manner. I am ending the call now. Once you feel you are able to continue in a professional manner, please feel free to call us back at 1-877-888-3337.”
When a supervisor call back has been logged and the caller is refusing to end the call
3. “Unfortunately I do not have a supervisor available to take your call at this time. I have submitted a request for someone to return your call by the end of the next business day.”
If the enrollee does not allow you to disconnect, please continue with the following
“I do apologize I do not have a supervisor available at this time, but I will need to end this call now. Thank you for your understanding and I hope you have a nice day.”
When a caller is hesitant to provide their personal information in the IVR
“I understand your cause of concern, please be assured our IVR (phone routing system) is fully encrypted for your privacy.” (If they ask what that means you may explain that a third party is not able to listen in and steal their information)
Please remember to log all agent disconnected calls on the Abusive Callers log in CCC Workspace.

sources.title: Deferred vs. Postponed Annuitants
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Deferred vs. Postponed Annuitants.pptx

units.heading: Background:
units.text:
Background:
You may receive calls from annuitants that have either deferred or postponed annuities.
- There are differences between these two; recognize that not all annuitants are eligible for the FEDVIP
- More information on deferred and postponed annuitants can be found in the Transition to Retirement resource in LEARN
- Deferred Annuitants:
- A deferred annuitant is a former federal employee who was covered under the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS) and has completed at least 5 years of creditable civilian service
- Annuitants with a deferred annuity are NOT eligible for the FEDVIP because they did not meet the specific criteria required for continued coverage under OPM
- Postponed Annuitants:
- A postponed annuitant is former federal employee who's eligible for immediate retirement benefits but decides to delay receiving them to avoid the early retirement reduction

units.heading: Steps to complete a Dependent AWD ticket:
units.text:

- Date of Birth
- Sex
- Relation

units.heading: Exceptions:

sources.title: Dependent Eligibility Age 21 or 23 – USM
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Dependent Eligibility Age 21 or 23 – USM.pptx

units.heading: Dependent Eligibility Age 21 or 23 – USM
units.text:
Uniformed Service Members may cover their dependent children until age 21. BENEFEDS will send a coverage‑expiration warning letter to the enrollee 60 days before a dependent’s coverage ends. This includes dependents approaching their:​
- 21st birthday​.
- 23rd birthday (If enrolled as approved student)​.
- Approved expiration date for dependents who are temporarily incapable of self‑support​.
The letter outlines the self certifying process for Student status or ISS status. See Page 2 for self certification process.​
A TEI dependent must be fully registered and approved in DEERS as a student or ISS or the sponsor is in the process of updating their status in DEERS before FEDVIP coverage can be restored.​
- TRICARE does not grant coverage while DEERS registration is still “in process.”​
- FEDVIP cannot retain or restore coverage until TRICARE eligibility is active in DEERS or the sponsor certifies they are in the process of updating their status in DEERS.​
- If the enrollee does not respond to the letter by the dependent’s age out/temporary ISS expiration date, the dependent will be removed from the coverage. Reinstatements can be made within 60 days from the dependent’s age out/temporary ISS expiration date if the enrollee certifies eligibility.
If BENEFEDS receives certification within 60 days of their removal: ​
- The dependent is added back to the FEDVIP plan.​
- Coverage is retroactive to the drop date, with no lapse in coverage.​
If approval is received after the 60‑day reinstatement window:​
- Because this is self certification and the customer only needs to be in the process of updating DEERS, there is no appeals process. ​
- Some Exceptions may apply and allow BENEFEDS to reinstate a dependent more than 60 days after removal. See Page 3 for Exceptions​.

units.heading: Dependent Eligibility Age 21 or 23 – USM
units.text:
Both Incapable of Self‑Support (ISS) status and Full‑Time Student status require the sponsor/enrollee’s self‑certification.​
A. Incapable of Self‑Support (ISS)​
The sponsor/enrollee must email BENEFEDS at fedvipadministration@benefeds.gov with:​
- Sponsor/enrollee full name​.
- TEI dependent’s full name​.
- Confirmation the dependent is permanently or temporarily ISS​.
- If temporary, include the end date of ISS status.​
If removed, once satisfied:​
- The dependent is added back to the FEDVIP plan.​
- Coverage is retroactive to the drop date, with no lapse in coverage.​
B. Full‑Time Student Status​
The sponsor/enrollee must contact BENEFEDS to confirm:​
- The dependent is a full‑time student.​
- Full-time status began prior to their age off. ​
- The dependent is updated and approved in DEERS as TRICARE‑eligible or the sponsor is in the process of updating their status.​
Once confirmed:​
- Reach out to your TL/Floor Support to reactivate the dependent or, in they are not available, agents will submit a dependent ticket.​
- The dependent is added back to the FEDVIP plan if removed.​
- Coverage is retroactive to the drop date, with no lapse in coverage.​
A TEI dependent remains eligible:​
- Until age 23, or​
- Until graduation, whichever comes first.​
If the dependent graduates before age 23:​
- Sponsor/enrollee must contact BENEFEDS to remove the dependent​ or inactivate the FEDVIP enrollment if the dependent was the primary enrollee.
NOTE: The FEDVIP dental and/or vision carrier may request documentation to confirm full-time student status.​
conditions: NOTE: The FEDVIP dental and/or vision carrier may request documentation to confirm full-time student status.​

units.heading: EXCEPTIONS:​
units.text:
EXCEPTIONS:​
Dependents may be reinstated greater than 60 days via Dependent Ticket in the following situations:​
A. If the enrollment is a Self and Family plan, the dependent may be reinstated greater than 60 days.​
The sponsor or enrollee must certify the dependent is fully updated and approved in DEERS as TRICARE‑eligible or in the process of updating their status in DEERS. ​
If the sponsor or enrollee certifies the dependents eligibility:​
- The dependent is added back to the FEDVIP plan.​
- Coverage is retroactive to the drop date, with no lapse in coverage.​
- Only listed dependents in a Self & Family plan are eligible to use the coverage.​
B. If the DV17, 18, or 54 letter was mailed to an incorrect Address, BENEFEDS can reinstate the dependent greater than 60. ​
The address must be updated after the date of removal​
BENEFEDS must have the ISS approval on file (CIV), or the dependent is fully updated and approved in DEERS as TRICARE‑eligible or the sponsor is in the process of updating their status in DEERS. (USM/TEI)​
If the request to reactivate due to incorrect address is after December 31st of the same year they were removed, they must have a QLE or wait for the next OS.​
If the customer meets these requirements:​
- The dependent is added back to the FEDVIP plan.​
- Coverage is retroactive to the drop date, with no lapse in coverage.​
Additional talking points: ​
If the dependent had services after being removed and prior to reactivation, direct the customer to the carrier to discuss claims processing.
NOTES:
- Carriers may choose not to process claims for services that occurred greater than 12 months in the past. ​
- If the dependent does not meet the above exceptions, they would need to be added during Open Season
- If a member wants to update their affiliation to maintain dependent eligibility, they must act during Open Season.

units.text: Dependent Eligibility Age 22 – Civ. Employee or USPS

units.heading: Dependent Eligibility Age 22 – CIV Employee or USPS
units.text:
Federal Civilian and USPS employees and annuitants or survivor annuitants may cover their dependent children until age 22. BENEFEDS will send a coverage‑expiration warning letter to the enrollee 60 days before a dependent’s coverage ends. This includes dependents approaching their:​
- 22nd birthday​.
- Approved expiration date for dependents who are temporarily incapable of self‑support​.
The letter explains how to submit documentation to the employing agency or retirement system if the dependent is, or continues to be, incapable of self‑support.​
- The enrollee must contact their employing agency or retirement system to submit ISS documentation.​
- The agency/retirement system must make their determination and return the decision to BENEFEDS within 60‑days of the dependent turning 22 to maintain their coverage.​ Documentation is sent to: FEDVIPadminstration@benefeds.gov
- If approval is not received by the dependent’s age out/temporary ISS expiration date, the dependent will be removed from the coverage. Reinstatements can be made within 60 days from the dependent’s age out/temporary ISS expiration date if the dependent meets the applicable qualifying eligibility criteria and approval is received. ​
If BENEFEDS receives the approval from the employing agency or retirement system within 60 days of their removal: ​
- The dependent is added back to the FEDVIP plan.​
- Coverage is retroactive to the drop date, with no lapse in coverage.​
If approval is received after the 60‑day reinstatement window:​
- When the delay is due to administrative reasons outside the customer’s control, they may appeal the decision not to reinstate the dependent. ​
- If the customer is ineligible to appeal, exceptions to reinstate the dependent may apply.​
- See Page 2 for Appeals and page 3 for Exceptions​.
If the exceptions or appeals do not apply:​
- Educate the enrollee or sponsor regarding Qualifying Life Events (QLEs).​
- If there is no valid QLE, inform them they must wait until the next Federal Benefits Open Season to add or re‑enroll the dependent​.

units.heading: Dependent Eligibility Age 22 – Appeals
units.text:
Employee Appeals:​
The Enrollee may reach out to their HR or ABO for an appeal.​
- The HR or ABO must email OPM at benefedsportal@opm.gov and explain that they have submitted ISS authorization outside the 60-day timeframe.​
- OPM will request additional information from the HR or ABO​.
- OPM will notify BENEFEDS if the reinstatement of the ISS dependent is approved. ​
- Once approval is received BENEFEDS reinstates coverage retroactive to the drop date, no lapse in coverage.​

units.heading: Employee Appeals:​ · Annuitants/Survivor Annuitants Appeals:​
units.text:
Annuitants/Survivor Annuitants Appeals:​
While still on the phone with the customer, the agent will reach out to a team lead and provide them with:​
- The member ID.​
- Dependent name.​
- That the ISS documentation was delayed​.
- If the RI 75-5 form was sent​.
- The date the customer contacted OPM and submitted the “Disabled Dependent Questionnaire”.​
Supporting Documentation (Not required for appeal): ISS Approval Form (RI 75-5)
If the dependent is age 26 or older and has received the ISS Approval form (RI 75-5) for FEHB from OPM which includes the ISS dependent information, the annuitant information, and whether the ISS dependent is permanently or temporarily ISS, they can email it to fedvipadministration@benefeds.gov. This replaces the need for an email from their OPM caseworker.
The email must include:​
- The Primary Enrollees full name​.
- The Dependents full name​.
- The date they contacted OPM and submitted the “Disabled Dependent Questionnaire”​.

units.heading: Employee Appeals:​ · Actions and Expectations (Annuitants/Survivor Annuitants):​
units.text:
Actions and Expectations (Annuitants/Survivor Annuitants):​
- Advise the customer that we will call them back once the appeals process is complete.​
- The team lead will email the OPM Customer Advocate providing all the details of the appeals. ​
- The OPM Customer Advocate will reach out to OPM for approval to reinstate the dependent.​
- If approved, BENEFEDS reinstates coverage retroactive to the drop date, no lapse in coverage.​
- The TL will request the agent to call out to the enrollee to inform them of the outcome.​
Additional talking points: ​
If the dependent had services after being removed and prior to reactivation, direct the customer to the carrier to discuss claims processing.
NOTE: Carriers may choose not to process claims for services that occurred greater than 12 months in the past. ​
conditions: NOTE: Carriers may choose not to process claims for services that occurred greater than 12 months in the past. ​

units.heading: Dependent Eligibility Age 22 – Exceptions
units.text:
EXCEPTIONS:​
Dependents may be reinstated greater than 60 days via Dependent Ticket without an appeal in the following situations:​
A. If the enrollment is a Self and Family plan, the dependent may be reinstated greater than 60 days without an appeal.​
BENEFEDS must have the ISS approval on file (CIV), or the dependent is fully updated and approved in DEERS as TRICARE‑eligible. (USM/TEI)​
If the customer meets these requirements:​
- The dependent is added back to the FEDVIP plan.​
- Coverage is retroactive to the drop date, with no lapse in coverage.​
- Only listed dependents in a Self & Family plan are eligible to use the coverage.​
B. If the DV17, 18, or 54 letter was mailed to an incorrect Address, BENEFEDS can reinstate the dependent greater than 60. ​
The address must be updated after the date of removal​
BENEFEDS must have the ISS approval on file (CIV), or the dependent is fully updated and approved in DEERS as TRICARE‑eligible or the sponsor is in the process of updating their status in DEERS (USM/TEI)​.
If the request to reactivate due to incorrect address is after December 31st of the same year they were removed, they must have a QLE or wait for the next OS.​
If the customer meets these requirements:​
- The dependent is added back to the FEDVIP plan.​
- Coverage is retroactive to the drop date, with no lapse in coverage.​
Additional talking points: ​
If the dependent had services after being removed and prior to reactivation, direct the customer to the carrier to discuss claims processing.
NOTES:
- Carriers may choose not to process claims for services that occurred greater than 12 months in the past. ​
- If the dependent does not meet the above exceptions, they would need to be added during Open Season.
- If a member wants to update their affiliation to maintain dependent eligibility, they must act during Open Season.

slides.title: Dependent Eligibility – Incapable of Self Support (1/2)

units.heading: Dependent Eligibility – Incapable of Self Support (1/2)
units.text: Under certain circumstances, civilians may continue coverage for a child 22 years of age or older who is incapable of self-support and for USM TRICARE-eligible dependent child over age 21 or 23 who meets the Department of Defense's standard for incapacity and support or for incapacity and dependency.

units.heading: Dependent Eligibility – Incapable of Self Support (1/2)
units.text:
Federal Civilian:
The civilian employing/retirement office must make the incapable of self-support determination and submit the approval to BENEFEDS within 60 days of the initial enrollment or the dependent’s 22 birthday for the dependent to be included on the enrollment. BENEFEDS will send a letter informing them their employing/retirement office must send an approval to fedvipadministration@benefeds.gov. The approval must be received within 60 days from the date of the letter for the dependent to maintain coverage. *OPM annuitants are required to complete a form for ISS approval. This form can be found on OPM.gov by searching “RI 30-10 Disabled Dependent Questionnaire".
- If the dependent was already on the plan BENEFEDS will send a letter 60 Days prior to their 22 birthday. If the approval is not received within 60 days of the letter, they will be removed. If BENEFEDS receives the approval within 60 days after their 22 birthday, the dependents coverage will be reinstated.
- If the dependent was already 22 at the time of the enrollment or being added to the plan, BENEFEDS will immediately send a letter, and the approval must be received within 60 from the date of the letter for the dependent to maintain coverage.
NOTE: If the approval is not received within 60 days of the initial enrollment or the dependent’s 22 birthday, the dependent will not be added back to the plan, and the enrollee will need to wait for a valid QLE or Open Season period to add their dependent.
- If the member feels they have done their due diligence to process their dependent’s required documentation ( within 60 days) and their HR office or OPM delayed the process, Continue to Page two (2).
conditions: NOTE: If the approval is not received within 60 days of the initial enrollment or the dependent’s 22 birthday, the dependent will not be added back to the plan, and the enrollee will need to wait for a valid QLE or Open Season period to add their dependent.

units.heading: Dependent Eligibility – Incapable of Self Support (1/2)
units.text:
Uniformed Service Members:
Uniformed services personnel dependents over age 21 or 23 must meet the Department of Defense's standard specified in DoD law at 10 U.S.C. 1072(2)(D)(iii) for incapacity and support or for incapacity and dependency at 10 U.S.C.1072(2)(I)(ii)(III), (iii), (iv) and (v).
BENEFEDS will send a letter informing the enrollee that their dependent must be approved in DEERS and the enrollee must email a statement that the child is ISS to fedvipadministration@benefeds.gov. The statement should include members full name, dependents full name, and whether they are permanently or temporarily incapable of self-support. If temporarily incapable of self-support, they must include the temporary expiration date. The email must be received within 60 days from the date of the letter for the dependent to maintain coverage.
- If the dependent was already on the plan BENEFEDS will send a letter 60 Days prior to their 21 or 23 birthday. If the email is not received by within 60 days of the letter, they will be removed. If BENEFEDS receives the email within 60 days after their 21 or 23 birthday, the dependents coverage will be reinstated.
- If the dependent was already 21 or 23 at the time of the enrollment or being added to the plan, BENEFEDS will immediately send a letter requesting an email and the enrollee will have 60 days for BENEFEDS to receive the approval.
NOTE: If the approval is not received within 60 days of the initial enrollment or the dependent’s 21 or 23 birthday, the dependent will not be added back to the plan, and the enrollee will need to wait for a valid QLE or Open Season period to add their dependent.
conditions: NOTE: If the approval is not received within 60 days of the initial enrollment or the dependent’s 21 or 23 birthday, the dependent will not be added back to the plan, and the enrollee will need to wait for a valid QLE or Open Season period to add their dependent.

units.heading: Dependent Eligibility – Incapable of Self Support (1/2)
units.text: Once approval has been received BENEFEDS will send a DV56 letter to the Member. This letter is automatic but does not necessary mean they are being added. Refer to the time frame above. Exception: In the case that an enrollee has a self and family plan already, the dependent can be reinstated outside of these time frames.

Federal Civilian Employee:
Determine if the dependent has been removed.
- If the dependent is still on the plan and they are checking the status of their request, Educate them on the timeframe and direct them back to their HR Agent/Specialist
- If the dependent has been removed:
- Direct the customer back to their HR or ABO.
- The HR Agent/Specialist or ABO must email OPM at benefedsportal@opm.gov and explain that they have submitted ISS Authorization outside the 60-day timeframe.
- OPM will request answers to specific questions directed to the HR.
- OPM will notify BENEFEDS if reinstatement of the ISS dependent is approved.
- If Approved, BENEFEDS will reactivate the dependent.
- Confirm if adding the dependent back on will cause a change in premiums. Discuss premium changes and adjustments if applicable.
- If not approved, the customer must add the dependent back to the plan with a QLE or during the next Federal Benefits Open Season.

units.heading: Dependent Eligibility – Incapable of Self Support (2/2)
units.text:
Federal Civilian Annuitant:
Determine if the dependent has been removed.
- If the dependent is still on the plan and they are checking the status of their request:
- Direct them to OPM. The customer can request the name, phone number, and/or email of their caseworker to inquire on the process.
- IF the ISS dependent has been approved for FEHB, Do they have the RI 75-5 form from OPM?
- If they have the RI 75-5 form from OPM, they can email it to fedvipadministration@benefeds.gov
- BENEFES will Validate the information and add the dependent if it is still within the 60-day timeframe.
- If the dependent has been removed:
- If they have the RI 75-5 form, they can email it to fedvipadministration@benefeds.gov
- Ask for the date they contacted OPM and submitted the “Disabled Dependent Questionnaire”
- Confirm if adding the dependent back on will cause a change in premiums. Discuss premium changes and adjustments if applicable.
- While the customer is still on the phone, reach out to a Team Lead. Your Team Lead provide expectations.

units.text: ISS and Student status is self certifying for USM affiliations and cannot be disputed. Exception: If the DV 17, 18, or 54 letter was mailed to an incorrect Address, BENEFEDS can add the dependent outside the 60-day timeframe. Address must be updated after the date listed on the letter for the dependent to be reactivated. If the request to reactivate the dependent is after December 31 (Post Open Season) of the same year they were removed, they must have a QLE or wait for the next OS.

sources.title: Determining FEDVIP Reinstatement
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Determining FEDVIP Reinstatement.pptx

units.heading: General Criteria for Reinstatement:
units.text:
General Criteria for Reinstatement:
Reinstatement may be considered if inactivation was due to:
- Address discrepancies or BENEFEDS communication errors.
- Incorrect inactivation codes (E-Exhausted, I-Ineligible, X-Transferred).
- Payment issues where posted payments did not prevent inactivation.
- Restoration of employment or annuity after wrongful termination.
- Natural disasters impacting the enrollee's ability to maintain coverage.
- Hospitalization during the entire period from the first direct bill to account inactivation.
Important Notes:
- Reinstatement leads to coverage being retroactive to the date of inactivation with no break in coverage.
- Enrollees must pay all retroactive premiums unless specific exceptions apply (e.g., hospitalization, administrative error with no requirement for immediate payment).
- Reinstatement is based on an enrollee’s employment status at the time of inactivation.
- If the APO is not sending L codes when the account termed for non-pay, the ACH reinstatement option will be provided.
- Customers may make the reinstatement payment, and they will be reinstated if payment is received by the due date regardless of their current employment status. In these instances, if the customer is calling to make a payment and the option to do so exists in the system, process the payment.
Exceptions:
- For USM (Uniformed Service Members) or certain specific employment cases, reinstatement might follow different protocols or require less stringent conditions for approval.
Additional Resources:
- Reinstatement for Non-Pay Request
- The above resource includes information about Workers’ Compensation and LWOP reinstatements.
- Leave Without Pay (LWOP)
- 5-Day Grace Period for Non-Pay Inactivation
- Primary Reinstate Enrollment AWD Ticket
See page 2 for steps on determining a FEDVIP reinstatement.
conditions: Important Notes:

units.heading: Specific Steps to Process Reinstatement:
units.text:
Specific Steps to Process Reinstatement:
- Verify Inactivation Reason:
- Ensure the inactivation code matches one of the accepted reasons for reinstatement (e.g., Non-Payment, Exhausted, Ineligible).
- Check Timing and Conditions:
- Confirm that the Inactivation code = Non-Payment
- Confirm that their mailing address is incorrect and they never received the direct bills sent to them.
- Did the enrollment inactivate before the first day of the previous Open Season?
- If NO, then continue with Step 3 below.
- If YES, is the timing of the request for reinstatement during Open Season/Post Open Season? (Note: Post Open Season ends December 31st.)
- If NO, then the reinstatement request may not be processed.
- Update Necessary Information:
- Correct mailing addresses or contact information as required.
- Edit member’s information if they provide new or corrected information.
- When an account needs to be reinstated but also needs other updates that cannot be completed in the CS System, please include the updates needed in the comments of the Reinstatement ticket. Do not submit multiple tickets.
- Authorization and Documentation:
- Obtain authorization from a Team Lead if the inactivation was due to administrative errors.
- For members and 3rd parties (authorized and unauthorized), if the option to process an ACH payment is available, you may take the ACH payment to reinstate the coverage.
- If the member is located at a new agency, create a Primary Agency Name Change Ticket to have the agency updated.
- If the ACH payment option is not available (due to the account being inactivated), create a Reinstatement AWD (Automated Work Distribution) Work Item.
- If they are located at a new agency, update the new agency name on the ticket.
- If the enrollee has received a Past Due Reinstatement Letter, but their account is inactivated:
- This will prevent an ACH payment from being made on BENEFEDS.gov and in the Customer Service System.
- If this is the case, please request that the enrollee remit the payment in the amount written in their Past Due Reinstatement Letter via check to the following address by the date specified in the letter:
- BENEFEDS-FEDVIP
- P.O. Box 414095
- Boston, MA 02241-4095
- Note: Reinstatement is within 3 days, unless there has been a reversal in the last 6 months. If there has been a reversal, we will hold the reinstatement for 10 days to ensure the payment is good before reinstating.
- Communicate with the Enrollee:
- Explain that if they were enrolled in both dental and vision, they do not have to pay on both programs. They can make payment of either one.
- Inform about the potential for double deductions to cover past due premiums if reinstatement is approved.
conditions: Note: Reinstatement is within 3 days, unless there has been a reversal in the last 6 months. If there has been a reversal, we will hold the reinstatement for 10 days to ensure the payment is good before reinstating.

sources.title: Discontinued Service Retirement (DSR)
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Discontinued Service Retirement (DSR).pptx

units.heading: Discontinued Service Retirement
units.text:
What is a Discontinued Service Retirement (DSR)?
- A DSR provides an immediate annuity for employees who are separated from federal service involuntarily.
- The term “involuntary separation” means any separation against the will and without the consent of the employee, other than “for cause” for misconduct or delinquency (most common example being a reduction in federal workforce).
- Provided this person will receive an immediate annuity via a Discontinued Service Retirement (DSR), this situation fits a continuation of coverage, and they are eligible to continue their FEDVIP enrollment.

units.heading: What is a Discontinued Service Retirement (DSR)? · Agent Action
units.text:
Agent Action:
- Action codes for a DSR entered by an agency often translate to a T code, or a termination code (viewable in CSS Billing).
- The T code will instruct BENEFEDS to inactivate the enrollee’s account.
- Enrollees will be responsible for contacting BENEFEDS to state they have retired.
Agents will initiate a reinstatement:
- Create a Primary Reinstatement AWD ticket to reinstate the enrollee:
- Select the agency the enrollee is retiring from and comment that they are retired in the AWD comments field.
- Explain the reinstatement rules to the member:
- Must reinstate both dental and vision if both dental and vision were inactivated.
- Explain you are submitting a request for reinstatement, which may or may not be approved depending upon further research into the account.
- If before 30 days: enrollees will not be required to remit past due payment.

units.heading: Dual Eligibility
units.text: Is Your Caller a Federal Civilian or a Uniformed Services Member?

units.heading: Dual Eligibility
units.text:
Dual eligibility is when a customer is eligible for FEDVIP as both a Federal Civilian and a Uniform Service Member. It's up to the enrollee to decide what affiliation to use when enrolling.
Customers may change their affiliation mid-year if they meet one of the following exceptions:
Exceptions for Changing Affiliation Mid-Year:
- A Uniform Service Member becomes Newly Hired as a Federal Civilian employee may process a new enrollment and make changes to their existing enrollment within 60 days of their hire date. (see Allowable Changes) To make changes, you must first update their affiliation to FEDCIV.
- If a Federal Employee is separating/ terminating from their Federal Civilian job, or part of the Deferred Resignation Program, and is a Uniformed Service Member, we can update their affiliation to USM to continue coverage. (if inactivated prior to the affiliation change, submit a reinstatement ticket with the affiliation information in the ticket) Must keep the same coverage.
- A rehired OPM Annuitant may enroll as a new Federal civilian employee and make changes within 60 days of their hire date. (see Allowable Changes) If they want to remain a retiree, they will retain what they currently have for coverage, with no changes.
- If a Survivor annuitant gets remarried and wants to add their new spouse, you may update their affiliation within 60 days of the marriage to allow the change. (See the ACED Chart for allowable QLE Changes)
Allowable changes (AWD Ticket required):
- Enrollment
- Plan changes
- Enrollment Type Change
NOTE: If a member wants to update their affiliation to maintain dependent eligibility, they must take action during open season

units.heading: Edit Other Insurances – Medicare and Medicaid (3/3)
units.text:
As a reminder, we have been asked to collect information regarding customer’s enrollment in Medicare and Medicaid.
- IMPORTANT: BENEFEDS is required to indicate if someone is enrolled in FEHB per OPM. This is even when their FEHB does not cover any dental or vision. Agents may receive calls from BCBS to change enrollees’ indications. Agents should follow the prompts on the other insurance page and ask if they are enrolled in FEHB for health benefits. If they are, they should not make any changes and direct the customer back to the carrier for coordination of benefit questions.
- These questions need to be asked on all accounts where the pop-up is present, unless the caller is requesting cancellation or disenrollment and do not have an existing enrollment.
- You are required to get three pieces of security when asking the Medicare and Medicaid questions.
- Don’t ask these questions to customers who are calling to cancel coverage with a valid QLE or are reporting the death of an enrollee unless they have an existing plan year enrollment.
What is Medicare/Medicaid?
- Medicare is a federal health insurance program primarily for people aged 65 and older, as well as some younger individuals with disabilities or certain medical conditions. It has different parts that cover hospital stays, medical services, prescription drugs, and more.
- Medicaid is a joint federal and state program that provides health coverage for individuals and families with low income. Eligibility and benefits vary by state, but it generally covers essential health services like doctor visits, hospital care, and long-term care.

sources.title: Effective Dates
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Effective Dates.pptx

units.heading: Effective Dates
units.text:
The coverage effective date is one of the most important pieces of information that BENEFEDS provides to enrollees. Providing incorrect coverage effective dates could possibly mean large out-of-pocket expenses for FEDVIP enrollees. In addition to understanding coverage effective dates, it is important to note that the BENEFEDS portal stores other types of effective dates.
- Premium Effective Date is the date that a certain premium AMOUNT becomes effective
- Coverage Effective Date is the date that the enrollee's coverage will begin
- Carrier Effective Date is the date that an enrollee first signed up for a plan with a NEW CARRIER
Talking Points:
Customer asks when their coverage will become effective for a new enrollment during the current plan year:
“Your coverage will become effective on the first day of the following pay period.”
Customer asks when their coverage will become effective for a new Open Season enrollment:
“Your coverage will become effective on January 1st next year.”
Customer asks when they can expect to see their premium deductions begin for their new Open Season enrollment:
“You will see your first premium deductions begin in the first full pay period of January. This may mean that you will see the deduction in your late-January paycheck.”

units.heading: To determine the correct effective dates, see the following resources:
units.text:
To determine the correct effective dates, see the following resources:
- ‌Allowable Changes and Effective Dates (ACED Chart)
- ‌FEDVIP Payroll Schedule

After that, you’re eligible to enroll in FEDVIP. However, in most cases you cannot add surviving children or dependents to your coverage (see below). / - Surviving children and dependents: You’re eligible for TDP and considered a transitional survivor until you become ineligible by turning 21 (non-student), turning 23 (full-time student), or getting married. These same events also make a child or dependent ineligible for FEDVIP. / Eligibility for Vision: Yes. You and eligible family members are eligible if you are enrolled in a TRICARE health plan (the three-year transitional period does not apply to vision. |  |  |

units.heading: I.T. Incident
units.text:
I.T. Incident
Something is broken or goes wrong
A problem needs to be fixed
This situation disrupts your normal use of technology, and the goal of an Incident is to fix the problem quickly so you can get back to work.
Examples
- Your computer crashes
- You can’t connect to the internet
- You can’t power on your computer
- You can’t log into your computer
I.T. Incidents are reported through the Report an Issue button from the Employee Service Center homepage.

units.heading: I.T. Request
units.text:
I.T. Request
You need something new or different
A want needs to be fulfilled
This situation is a want or permission for something that will help you complete your job efficiently.
Examples
- You need to be added to a distribution list
- You want a new SharePoint site
- You need access to create a new Teams Channel
- You need access to a shared drive
I.T. Requests are submitted through the Request Something button from the Employee Service Center homepage.

units.heading: Enrollment Terms and Conditions
units.text:
Enrollment Terms and Conditions
During the FEDVIP enrollment process you must agree to these terms and conditions to complete your FEDVIP dental and/or vision enrollment.
Eligibility
- I certify that:
- I am eligible to enroll in a dental plan and/or vision plan under the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP).
- Any family members I have added are eligible to enroll.
- I will not be covered under more than one FEDVIP dental and/or FEDVIP vision plan, nor will any of my eligible family members. If I am or any of the eligible family members in my enrollment are covered or will be covered under someone else's FEDVIP dental plan and/or FEDVIP vision plan, I will not proceed with this enrollment.
- All eligible family members are enrolled under one primary enrollment, regardless of their physical location or residence.
- I understand that if I am not eligible to enroll, or any of my family members are not eligible, my plan can change or the enrollment can be canceled immediately, as applicable. Any premiums paid prior to the effective date of the plan change or the cancelation, while covered, will be retained by the insurance carrier and I will not be responsible for repaying benefits received prior to that date.
- Exception Note: I also understand that if a family member loses eligibility due to divorce, my plan can be changed retroactively to the first day of the first pay period following the event date and that I may be responsible for repaying any benefits not covered after that date.
- I understand that if it is discovered that I am or any of my eligible family members is covered under more than one FEDVIP dental and/or FEDVIP vision plan, one of the enrollments will be canceled. Any premiums paid prior to the effective date of the plan change or cancelation, while covered, will be retained by the insurance carrier, and I will not be responsible for repaying benefits received prior to that date.
- I understand that my FEDVIP plan can ask me for documentation of my eligibility, as well as that of my family members, and I must provide this proof within 60 days of that request. If I do not, or if the documentation is deemed insufficient, my FEDVIP plan may change or my FEDVIP enrollment may be canceled immediately, as applicable. Any premiums paid prior to the effective date of the plan change or the cancelation, while covered, will be retained by the insurance carrier, and I will not be responsible for repaying benefits received prior to that date.
conditions: Exception Note: I also understand that if a family member loses eligibility due to divorce, my plan can be changed retroactively to the first day of the first pay period following the event date and that I may be responsible for repaying any benefits not covered after that date.

units.heading: Enrollment Terms and Conditions · Enrollment
units.text:
Enrollment
- I understand that:
- My enrollment automatically continues each year, unless I take action to cancel it during the Federal Benefits Open Season (open season).
- During open season, if I wish to cancel my coverage, I must take action by canceling my enrollment via BENEFEDS.gov or telephone. If I take no action during open season, my active coverage will continue automatically into the new plan year.
- The opportunities to change or cancel enrollment outside of open season are extremely limited.
- Financial hardship does not allow me to change or cancel my coverage.
- Retirement does not allow me to change or cancel my coverage, with one exception. Exception note: If a member of the uniformed services retires, his or her family's coverage will be inactivated. In order to have coverage, the sponsor will be required to submit a new enrollment covering the sponsor and his or her family, as applicable.
- I understand that:
- It is my responsibility to notify BENEFEDS via BENEFEDS.gov or telephone of any changes that are relevant to my enrollment, including home address and agency, branch, or retirement system changes. I further understand my agency, branch, or retirement system is not responsible for notifying BENEFEDS. Please note, notifications of changes sent with direct payments will not be processed.
- If my premium changes because my home address changes, the new premium rate will be effective the first pay period following the date upon which I notify BENEFEDS of my new address.
- There is no temporary extension of coverage when my FEDVIP coverage ends.
- If it is discovered that there are multiple primary enrollments for one family, all enrollments may be consolidated under one primary enrollment. Any premiums paid prior to the effective date of resulting plan changes or cancelations will be retained by the insurance carrier.
- I may be contacted about other federal benefits.
- You may opt-out of non-administrative communications at any time.
- In order to continuously improve services provided to federal employees, retirees, members of the uniformed services, and their family members, I may be asked periodically to provide my opinion and feedback regarding BENEFEDS, FEDVIP, or other program-related processes, systems, or services.

units.heading: Enrollment Terms and Conditions · Premium Payments
units.text:
Premium Payments
- I authorize premium payments to be deducted from my pay, annuity, retirement pay, or bank account, as applicable. I understand that an additional authorization is required to establish a recurring electronic funds transfer (EFT), which BENEFEDS refers to as an automatic bank withdrawal (ABW).
- I understand that plans and premiums are reviewed on an annual basis and I authorize future premium adjustments to my plan, when enrollment continues for the following plan year, to be deducted from my pay, annuity, retirement pay, or bank account, as applicable.
- If deductions cannot be made and BENEFEDS sends me a bill, I understand that I must pay that bill on time. If I do not, I understand that BENEFEDS maintains the right to terminate my enrollment.
- If deductions cannot be made, I understand that BENEFEDS will continue to attempt deductions and, if successful deductions are confirmed, my enrollment may continue and will result in BENEFEDS recouping any past premium due.

units.heading: Enrollment Terms and Conditions · FEHB Authorization
units.text:
FEHB Authorization
- I authorize BENEFEDS to receive information about my Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) Program enrollment, if any, from my agency, payroll provider, or retirement system, and give it to my FEDVIP plan since, when applicable, the FEHB Program is the first payor of benefits. The FEDVIP plan allowance is the prevailing charge. I am responsible for the difference between FEHB and FEDVIP benefit payments and the FEDVIP plan allowance.

units.heading: Enrollment or Inactivation Due to Divorce
units.text: This job aid outlines two distinct scenarios related to divorce where a former spouse remains listed on an active FEDVIP enrollment.

units.heading: Scenario 1: Former Spouse Calling to Enroll After Divorce
units.text:
Scenario 1: Former Spouse Calling to Enroll After Divorce
When a former spouse contacts BENEFEDS to enroll following a divorce but is still listed as a family member on their former spouse’s active account, they must be removed from that account before their enrollment can be completed.
Agent Actions:
- Create a profile for the caller.
- Locate the active account where the caller is still listed.
- Call out to the primary account holder of the active account to request removal of the former spouse.
- Do not conference the caller into this outreach.
- Work with each party independently unless either party specifically requests a conference.
- If the other party has multiple contact numbers and you are attempting to reach them using more than one number, you must check in with the held party between call outs. The 2-minute check in rule for holds does not apply in this scenario.
- If contact is made and the primary agrees, process the removal.
- After removal, return to the original caller to complete their enrollment.
- When the primary refuses to remove the former spouse or you are unable to reach them:
- If the primary is not reached, leave a voicemail and manually comment the active account.
conditions: Do not conference the caller into this outreach.

units.heading: Scenario 1: Former Spouse Calling to Enroll After Divorce · Voicemail Script
units.text:
Voicemail Script:
“This message is for [member name]. My name is [your name], and I’m calling on behalf of BENEFEDS. BENEFEDS administers the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program. We need to speak with you. Please call us back at 1 877 888 3337. Our office hours are Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–7 p.m. (ET).”
Manual Comment:
“Customer divorced [mm/dd/yyyy] and needs to remove former spouse or stepchildren.”
- Instruct the caller to email a copy of their divorce decree to service@benefeds.gov.
- The email subject should be: ATTN: Research.
- In the body of the email, the caller must include:
- Their full name
- Their new member ID
- A brief explanation of the situation
- Complete an Enrollment Ticket. Ticket comments must include:
- The related account’s member ID (do not provide this number to the caller)
- Confirmation that you attempted to contact the other party
- A note stating the customer is emailing their divorce decree to service@benefeds.gov, ATTN: Research
- Provide the following expectations to the customer:
- Once Research receives the divorce decree, they will remove the caller from the former spouse’s account.
- If Research receives the decree within 19 days, they will automatically process the caller’s enrollment and send a confirmation email.
- If the decree is not received within 19 days, or if the other party does not remove them by the end of the 19 days, the ticket will be closed without action.
- The removal will be retro to the date of divorce.
- If the removal results in a premium change, the account will be adjusted accordingly. Any overpayment will be refunded or applied as a credit. See FEDVIP Credits & Refunds Job Aid.

slides.title: Enrollment or Inactivation Due to Divorce

units.heading: Scenario 2: USM – Sponsor Requesting to Inactivate a FAD Account
units.text:
Scenario 2: USM – Sponsor Requesting to Inactivate a FAD Account
Sponsors may request inactivation of a FEDVIP (FAD) account without consent from the primary only if one of the following conditions applies:
(1) The sponsor is enrolling due to retirement, (2) The primary is a minor, (3) The sponsor submits a divorce decree.
Agent Actions:
- Create a profile for the caller if they intend to enroll.
- Locate the active account where the former spouse or minor child is still listed.
- If the primary on the active account is a minor:
- Create an inactivation ticket for the FAD account. Ticket comments must include:
- The caller’s new member ID
- A note indicating whether the sponsor intends to enroll
- If the primary on the active account is a former spouse, call out to the primary account holder.
- Do not conference the caller into this outreach.
- Work with each party independently unless either party specifically requests a conference.
- If the other party has multiple contact numbers and you are attempting to reach them using more than one number, you must check in with the held party between call outs. The 2-minute check in rule for holds does not apply in this scenario.
- If contact is made, determine eligibility (20/20/20, 20/20/15, or CIV).
- If eligible, update their affiliation.
- A ticket is required to change the affiliation to CIV.
- If not eligible, submit an inactivation ticket.
- After updating their affiliation or submitting the ticket, return to the original caller.
- If the primary refuses to provide eligibility information or cannot be reached — and the sponsor does NOT intend to enroll:
- Leave a voicemail and manually comment the active account.
Voicemail Script:
“This message is for [member name]. My name is [your name], and I’m calling on behalf of BENEFEDS. BENEFEDS administers the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program. We need to speak with you. Please call us back at 1 877 888 3337. Our office hours are Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–7 p.m. (ET).”
Continued on Page 3 
conditions: Do not conference the caller into this outreach.

units.heading: Manual Comment:
units.text:
Manual Comment:
“Customer divorced [mm/dd/yyyy] and needs affiliation updated or enrollment inactivated.”
- Instruct the caller to email a copy of their divorce decree to service@benefeds.gov.
- The email subject must be: ATTN: Research. The caller must include:

- Their new member ID
- A brief explanation of the situation
- Provide the following expectations to the customer:
- Once Research receives the divorce decree, they will inactivate the FAD account.
- The inactivation will be retroactive to the date of divorce.
- Applicable refunds will be returned to the primary account holder.
- If the account has a minor child who was covered (current or aged off) between the date of divorce and today’s date.
- Inactivation ticket submitted:
- The inactivation will be retro to the event date unless former spouse was never eligible (Enrolled after divorce as FAD)
- Applicable refunds will be sent to the primary of the FAD account
- Advise we will enroll the eligible family member(s) on their own account retroactively effectively based on the date of divorce.
- Advise the customer this action will result in past due premiums. Research will educate the customer on the past due amount and adjustment process.

- Unable to Reach Primary/ Inactivation ticket not submitted:
- Complete an enrollment ticket.
- If enrolling with ABW, you must read the ABW Authorization statement for each enrollment.
- Ticket comments must include:
- The related account’s member ID (do not provide this number to the caller)
- Confirm that you attempted to contact the other party
- That the sponsor is sending in the divorce decree
- If they agree to the ABW Authorization statement.
- Advise we will enroll the eligible family member(s) on their own account retroactively effectively based on the date of divorce.
- Advise the customer this action will result in past due premiums and educate on adjustment process. Past due premiums will be calculated once enrollment is processed.
- Provide the following expectations to the customer:
- Once research processes the inactivation ticket, they will process the enrollment.
- The inactivation will be retroactive if divorce, or prospective if primary is a minor.
- BENEFEDS will send a confirmation via email or letter once the enrollment is complete.

sources.title: FEDVIP Background
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/FEDVIP Background.pptx

units.heading: FEDVIP Background
units.text: BENEFEDS/FEDVIP Background

units.heading: Background:
units.text:
The Federal Employee Dental and Vision Benefits Enhancement Act of 2004 enabled the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to provide dental and vision benefits to Federal employees, retirees, and their dependents. These benefits are available through the Federal Employees Dental/Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP), which offers competitive group premiums without pre-existing condition limitations. Enrollees can choose from Self Only, Self Plus One, or Family coverage, with eligibility for enrollment extending to similar rules as the Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) Program, regardless of actual FEHB enrollment.
BENEFEDS, established by Long Term Care Partners in 2005, serves as a secure portal for managing FEDVIP enrollment and includes integrated payroll, billing systems, and customer service to handle premium administration. This platform also supported the transition of the TRICARE Retiree Dental Program (TRDP) to FEDVIP in 2019, allowing retired Uniformed Services members and their families to enroll in FEDVIP, expanding its reach and utility.

sources.title: FEDVIP Credits & Refunds
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/FEDVIP Credits & Refunds.pptx

units.heading: Account Credits & Premium Retention:
units.text:
Account Credits & Premium Retention:
- Do not provide any specific refund amounts or anticipated refund dates.
- Refund amounts or dates may only be provided after the refund has been issued.
- Account credits are funds collected by BENEFEDS that can apply to future premiums or, in specific cases, be refunded to the enrollee.
- BENEFEDS will retain credit amounts from the current year and the previous year as long as the total credit does not exceed three times the current annual premium amount.
- If the credit exceeds 3 times the annual premium amount or includes funds older than the current and previous year, BENEFEDS will issue a refund for the full credit amount, minus any premiums needed to cover pending payment files.
conditions: Do not provide any specific refund amounts or anticipated refund dates.

units.heading: Account Credits & Premium Retention · Submit a Refund Request for the following reasons
units.text:
Submit a Refund Request for the following reasons:
- The enrollee overpaid by direct payment (Check or ACH Payment)
- Overpayment made by check will be held for 10 business days, and over payment by ACH will be held for 5 business days before a refund can be processed.
- For Payroll/Annuity, we are not required to hold it. We will have 1 day to process the refund if due to a credit balance, or 3 days if due to a refund request.
- Refunds can take up to 15 business days to be fully processed.
- If premium deductions were not processed correctly.
Refunds on Deceased’s Account: If asked about potential refunds, say, “If it has been determined that overpayments exist on the account, they will be refunded via the original payment method, or to the estate of the deceased.”
Premium retention involves holding a portion of funds to ensure coverage of pending bills and accurate payment of future bills. Pending bills are when the APO for that account has a bill that has run but not yet posted payment. The account itself may or may not show a bill row, so that APO’s schedule shall be referenced.

units.heading: Account Credits & Premium Retention · PAT needs to determine if the account’s next bill file will be to a pre-tax or post-tax lo
units.text:
PAT needs to determine if the account’s next bill file will be to a pre-tax or post-tax location:
- If pre-tax location: PAT retains premiums for any pending bill row plus one pay period.
- If post-tax location: PAT retains premiums for any pending bill row. If there is no pending bill row, no premium retention is required.
Premium retention is required for pending bill rows to avoid creation of past due because a pending bill row’s payment is not guaranteed.
Note: if a refund results in both post-tax and pre-tax refunds, and the account is billing to a post-tax location next, the above post-tax direction is correct.
conditions: Note: if a refund results in both post-tax and pre-tax refunds, and the account is billing to a post-tax location next, the above post-tax direction is correct.

units.heading: Account Credits & Premium Retention · OPM Letters Regarding Premiums Not Being Withdrawn/Account Credits
units.text:
OPM Letters Regarding Premiums Not Being Withdrawn/Account Credits:
Enrollees receiving premium deductions through an OPM annuity may receive a letter indicating that OPM is no longer receiving premium deductions for their account. This is due to the enrollee having a credit on their account and does not impact their coverage.
Explain: "When there is a credit on the account, we temporarily stop billing OPM for your FEDVIP premiums so that the credit can be used first. After the credit is fully applied, your regular premium deductions through your annuity will start again automatically.
During the time we pause those premium requests, OPM may send a standard letter stating they are no longer receiving a request for your premium. The letter can sound like a change to your coverage, but it’s only informational. Your coverage remains active, and no action is required."

units.heading: Refund Processing
units.text:
Refund Processing
If it is determined that a refund is due, it can take an additional 10-12 business days after the refund has been processed by the Finance department to be mailed out to the enrollee.
- Refunds can take up to 15 business days before they are received.
- For payroll/annuity, we are not required to hold it. It will take 1 day to process the refund if it is due to a credit balance, and 3 days if it is due to a refund request.
- Once the customer cashes their refund check or the APO issues the refund payout, it is reported back to Premium Admin, and the cash-flow refund status is updated to “Recouped”.
- Exception: If the refund is sent to an APO due to a retroactive removal and the customer is no longer in their system, Premium Admin must issue a check, and the status will show “recouped” once the check is issued, even if the customer never cashes it.
conditions: Exception: If the refund is sent to an APO due to a retroactive removal and the customer is no longer in their system, Premium Admin must issue a check, and the status will show “recouped” once the check is issued, even if the customer never cashes it.

units.heading: Refund Processing · Refunds (Payroll/Pre-Tax)
units.text:
Refunds (Payroll/Pre-Tax)
If payment was collected through pre-tax dollars (Payroll), refunds will be routed back to Payroll when possible and issued as an after-tax refund.
- Only Federal Civilians and U.S. Postal Employees have their premiums deducted pre-tax.
- All refund requests are considered a “request” and must be approved before a refund/credit is applied to an account.
- All money that is overpaid will be credited back to the account.
- BENEFEDS Premium Administration Team will process the refund within 1-2 pay periods.
- Refunds are issued if requested (enrollee prefers a refund instead of an account credit), if the credit balance is greater than 3X the annual deduction, or if any of the credit balance is on a plan year that is more than 2 years before the current plan year.
Note: If a credit is on the account and a refund is requested, the refund may be issued if it doesn’t create a negative balance.
Refunds (Annuity/Post-Tax)
If payment was collected through post-tax dollars (Annuity), refunds will be sent from BENEFEDS.
- Post-tax deductions include Annuitants, Survivor Annuitants, Worker’s Compensation, ABW, Direct Bills, and Compensationers.
- BENEFEDS Premium Administration Team will hold payments for a specific number of days:
conditions: Note: If a credit is on the account and a refund is requested, the refund may be issued if it doesn’t create a negative balance.

units.text:

units.heading: FEDVIP Credits & Refunds
units.text:
- Refunds for post-tax payments (ACH/Direct) will be sent by check unless otherwise specified.
- Refunds for post-tax payments (ABW) will be sent to the bank account the payment was withdrawn from. (Many ABW credit balances are not refunded and are sent back to the customer’s bank account.)
- Refunds for accounts inactivated due to death will be sent via check payable to the estate. If the check needs to be reissued to an alternate payee, the payee must submit an Alternate Payee form.
- If the member who has passed is on ABW, any refund due will be returned to their bank account. If we are unable to return premiums via ABW, we will send a check to the estate.

units.heading: General Rules:
units.text:
General Rules:
If premiums were originally deducted before taxes (pretax), any refund will go back to the same APO (payroll office) the premiums came from—even if the customer no longer works with that APO.
It’s the customer’s responsibility to contact that APO to make sure they receive the refund.
- If it’s been more than 3 years since the customer was with their APO, the APO may not be able to process refunds.
- In that case, PAT will be notified, and the refund will be sent to the customer’s current APO instead.
- This 3-year limit is a general guideline—it’s usually around that time frame.
Expectations to leave with callers:
- There is a 10 day hold on money we receive from checks and ACH payments; and a 10 day hold of ABW payments.
- If it is determined that a refund is due, it can take an additional 10-12 business days after refund has been processed by our finance department to be mailed out to the enrollee. Refunds can take up to 15 business days before they are received.
- For payroll/annuity, we are not required to hold it. It will take 1 day to process the refund if it is due to a credit balance, and 3 days if it is due to a refund request.
- If it is determined that a refund/credit is not due or it was stated in the ticket that a callback is requested, Research will contact the customer within 3 business days of receipt of that ticket.
Talking Points:
Customer pays by ABW and was due a refund it has not received a check in the mail:
“Because you paid your premium deductions through ABW, BENEFEDS will not send a check in the mail, instead the refund will be sent back to the bank that was setup on your account for your Automatic Bank Withdrawal.”
Customer pays by ABW and states it has been over 10 business days, and they have not received their refund back into their bank account:
“I do apologize for the inconvenience; however, you will need to contact your bank for any additional questions regarding when you can expect to see your refund on your account.”

slides.title: FEDVIP Ineligible vs Never Eligible Dependents

units.heading: Ineligible Dependents
units.text:
Ineligible Dependents
Ineligible dependents are individuals who do not currently meet the requirements for FEDVIP coverage but may become eligible in the future if certain conditions change. Eligibility may depend on factors such as age, student status, or changes in family structure.
Examples:
- Children over 21 who are full-time students but haven't yet submitted the required paperwork to verify their status.
- Stepchildren who aren't living with the enrollee or don't have a parent-child relationship but may qualify if their living situation changes.
- Dependents under 22 who no longer qualify as students but could regain eligibility if they become incapacitated before turning 22.
- Dependents who were full time students who have since graduated.

units.heading: Ineligible Dependents · Removing Ineligible Dependents
units.text:
Removing Ineligible Dependents
- The dependent can be removed by performing a QLE of Lost Family. Enter the QLE event date as the last day of the current pay period.
- In the case of death or divorce, use the date of the event as the QLE.
- If the account has been archived and the event date occurs before the archival date, you must first retrieve the archived data before processing the QLE. If you are unable to retrieve the archived data, submit a dependent ticket and document that the data could not be retrieved.

units.heading: Ineligible Dependents · Never Eligible Dependents
units.text:
Never Eligible Dependents
Never eligible dependents are those who were not eligible at the time they were added as a dependent to a plan and are still ineligible at the time of accessing the account.
Examples:
- Former spouses or ex-stepchildren after a divorce.
- Children over the age of 22 who are not disabled.
- Siblings or parents, unless they qualify under special survivor annuitant rules.
- Grandchildren (unless the grandparents are foster parents and the child lives with them).
conditions: Never Eligible Dependents
Never eligible dependents are those who were not eligible at the time they were added as a dependent to a plan and are still ineligible at the time of accessing the account.

units.heading: Ineligible Dependents · Removing Never Eligible Dependents
units.text:
Removing Never Eligible Dependents
- The dependent can be removed by performing a QLE of Lost Family. Enter the QLE event date as the last day of the current pay period.
- This QLE date should be completed for all never eligible dependents.
- If the account has been archived and the event date occurs before the archival date, you must first retrieve the archived data before processing the QLE. If you are unable to retrieve the archived data, submit a dependent ticket and document that the data could not be retrieved.
