sources.title: FEDVIP Primary Enrollee Eligibility
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/FEDVIP Primary Enrollee Eligibility.pptx

units.heading: FEDVIP Primary Enrollee Eligibility
units.text: This document outlines the eligibility and enrollment guidelines for different customer types under the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP).

units.heading: Federal Employees
units.text:
Federal Employees
Federal employees, whether full-time, part-time, seasonal, intermittent, or temporary, are eligible for the FEDVIP provided they meet specific work criteria. These employees must generally expect to work at least 130 hours per month for 90 consecutive days, with exceptions for emergency personnel like wildland firefighters. Ineligibilities include those under the Temporary Continuation of Coverage (TCC), employees of certain designated organizations, and those in non-pay or inactive due to non-payment status.
- Eligibility: Full-time, part-time, seasonal, intermittent, or temporary federal civilian employees expected to work at least 130 hours per month for 90 consecutive days, excluding specific ineligible groups.

units.heading: USPS Employees
units.text:
USPS Employees
USPS employees who meet FEHB eligibility requirements can also enroll in FEDVIP. This includes seasonal, intermittent, and temporary employees expected to work at least 130 hours per month for 90 consecutive days.
- Eligibility: USPS employees meeting FEHB eligibility.
- Enrollment in a PSHB (Postal Service Health Benefits) plan will not disrupt or prevent enrollment in other insurance benefits programs including FEDVIP, FSAFEDS, FEGLI, and FLTCIP.

units.heading: Annuitants
units.text:
Annuitants
Federal annuitants are generally eligible for FEDVIP regardless of their FEHB status. This includes those who have retired under systems like the Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS) or the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS), including those who retire for disability. There is no requirement to have been enrolled in FEHB prior to retirement for continuing FEDVIP coverage, which differs from other federal programs.
- Eligibility: Federal retirees who receive an immediate annuity or retire due to disability, under any federal retirement system.

units.heading: Survivor Annuitants
units.text:
Survivor Annuitants
Survivor annuitants, typically surviving spouses or children, become eligible for FEDVIP following the death of a federal employee or retiree. They have a specific enrollment period of 60 days post-eligibility. However, a surviving spouse who remarries before age 55 and was not married to the deceased for at least 30 years loses eligibility. Enrollment processes for survivors must be escalated to a senior representative even during Open Season.
- Eligibility: Survivors receiving a Basic Survivor Death Benefit or a CSF Claim number, with conditions based on remarriage and length of the previous marriage.

units.heading: Compensationers
units.text:
Compensationers
Compensationers are individuals receiving workers' compensation and deemed unable to return to duty by the Department of Labor. These individuals, whether currently receiving compensation or survivors of a deceased compensationer, are eligible for FEDVIP without the necessity of being enrolled in FEHB. This status provides them with a unique pathway to FEDVIP enrollment.
- Eligibility: Employees or former employees entitled to workers' compensation and deemed unable to return to duty, along with their survivors.

units.heading: Uniformed Service Members
units.text:
Uniformed Service Members
Uniformed Service Members who are retired or certain reservists qualify for FEDVIP benefits following the end of the TRICARE Retiree Dental Program (TRDP). Retired members, their families, and select reservists are eligible for both FEDVIP dental and vision coverage if they were previously part of the TRDP and are enrolled in a TRICARE health plan. Importantly, active-duty Uniformed Service Members themselves are not eligible to enroll in FEDVIP; their dental and vision needs are covered through TRICARE. However, their families and dependents can access FEDVIP vision coverage, provided they are enrolled in a TRICARE health plan.
- Eligibility: Retired Uniformed Service Members, their dependents, and certain reservists qualify for FEDVIP. Family members of active-duty service members are eligible for vision coverage through FEDVIP, contingent upon enrollment in a TRICARE health plan

units.heading: FEDVIP Roles
units.text: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) contracts with FedPoint to be the administrator and marketplace operator of BENEFEDS.gov and manages the enrollment and premium payment processes on behalf of the FEDVIP carriers and OPM. The Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP) provides dental and vision coverage to active and retired Federal civilian employees, Uniformed Service Members and their families.

units.heading: Governs the FEDVIP
units.text:
- Governs the FEDVIP
- Determines eligibility and enrollment rules
- Wrote the FEDVIP law that outlines the policies and regulations
- Works with the carriers to determine premiums
- Contracts FedPoint to be the administrator of the BENEFEDS program

sources.title: Federal Benefits Open Season Overview
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Federal Benefits Open Season Overview.pptx

units.heading: Background:
units.text:
Background:
During Open Season, members of the Federal family can enroll in and/or make changes to their Federal benefits without restriction.
There are two methods Federal family members can use to enroll in the FEDVIP, make a change to existing FEDVIP enrollments, or cancel FEDVIP enrollments:
- Customers may visit www.BENEFEDS.gov to enroll, make changes, or cancel.
- Customers can call BENEFEDS Customer Service to enroll, make changes, or cancel.
Open Season should be referred to as the Federal Benefits Open Season, as other Federal benefits are holding open seasons during the same timeframe as the FEDVIP is.
All Open Season actions become effective January 1st.

units.heading: Background · Federal Benefits Open Season Dates
units.text:
Federal Benefits Open Season Dates
The Federal Benefits Open Season occurs annually. The event occurs during a 4–5-week period and is normally held from the Monday of the second full workweek in November through the Monday of the second full workweek in December. Once OPM has released the dates, BENEFEDS will make them available on BENEFEDS.gov, and the dates may also be provided by call center reps.

units.heading: Background · Federal Benefits Open Season Hours of Operation
units.text:
Federal Benefits Open Season Hours of Operation
Call Center Hours:
Monday–Friday: 8AM – 9PM EST
Last day of Open Season: 8AM – 12AM EST (midnight)
BENEFEDS.gov Hours:
Available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
Allowable Actions During Federal Benefits Open Season
Any eligible individual may call or access their account online during the Federal Benefits Open Season and submit any of the below allowable actions:
- Enrollment into a Dental and/or Vision plan (Coverage begins on January 1st)
- Changes to an existing Dental and/or Vision plan (Coverage begins on January 1st)
- Cancellations for a Dental and/or Vision plan (Coverage ends December 31st)
Talking Points:
Customer asks why enrollments and changes are only allowed during Open Season:
“The FEDVIP is an annual benefit offered to you by the Federal government. Because it is an annual benefit, you must be enrolled for the entire year and pay premium for the entire year, unless you have had a qualifying life event (QLE) that allows enrollment or changes outside of Open Season.”

sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Federal Civilian Transition to Retirement (L1).pptx

units.heading: Federal Civilian Transition to Retirement (L1)
units.text: Follow the steps below when advising callers about the transition to retirement process.

units.heading: Reminders about the Transition process:
units.text:
Reminders about the Transition process:
- FEDVIP Enrollments automatically continue into retirement.
- Enrollees cannot cancel due to retirement.
- Not all retirement systems allow premium deductions from pension/annuity.
- You must verify all the retiree’s demographic information. Update if necessary.

units.heading: Federal Civilian Transition to Retirement (L1)
units.text:
Step 1: When someone calls to advise they have retired or are retiring, determine if they have listened to the retirement info in the IVR:
Say, “Our automated system provides information on the retirement transition, have you had the opportunity to listen to that information?”
- If YES, say, “ Do you have any questions about the transition process?”
- If NO, continue to Step 2 below

units.heading: Federal Civilian Transition to Retirement (L1)
units.text:
Step 2: Verify All Demographic Information (asking the following questions assumes 3 pieces of security have been verified):
Say, “To ensure you’re able to receive correspondence from BENEFEDS during your transition to retirement, we will confirm your profile and contact information.”
- Email: “Is your email still ______?”
- Residential Address: “Is your residential address still _______?”
- Mailing Addresses: “And is that address also your mailing address?”
- Phone Number: “Is the phone number, _______, still the best number to reach you at?”

units.heading: Step 3: Review the following with the caller:
units.text:
Step 3: Review the following with the caller:
Say, “Let’s review some important information regarding your transition. If you have questions afterwards, I will be able to transfer you to an agent who can discuss this information with you further.”
- “Your FEDVIP coverage will automatically continue into retirement. After we receive notification of your retirement from your payroll office, we’ll work with your annuity system to set up premium deductions from your annuity.”
- “In some cases, it can take an extended period for your annuity to be finalized. During this time, BENEFEDS will send you direct bills for your premiums and you must pay these bills to maintain your FEDVIP enrollment.”
- “You may make payments online from your My BENEFEDS account at BENEFEDS.gov, or by mail. Please note - you can only make a payment after your bill has been generated. Once your annuity is finalized, BENEFEDS will automatically deduct directly from your annuity.”
- “Keep in mind, retirement is not a qualifying life event. You cannot enroll, cancel, or change your FEDVIP coverage outside of an open season because you have retired.”
Say, “Do you have any question about what I’ve just reviewed?” If Yes, transfer to an L2. If No, conclude the call as normal.

units.heading: Step 3: Determine their support needs:
units.text:
Step 3: Determine their support needs:
Ask: “Do you have specific questions about the retirement transition, or would you like me to walk you through the full process?”
- If they have specific questions, answer those questions.
- If they want the full transition process, read the transition script below.
Retirement Transition Script:
“Once you retire, your FEDVIP coverage continues automatically. Your payroll office will notify BENEFEDS, and we’ll move your account to monthly billing. While your annuity is being finalized, you’ll receive bills from us, and you must pay them to keep your coverage.
Once your annuity is finalized, your premiums will be deducted automatically. If your annuity isn’t enough to cover the premiums, you’ll stay on direct billing.
Some retirement systems don’t allow deductions. In those cases, you can choose to set up automatic bank withdrawals.
We’ll send you letters throughout the process and let you know if you need to take action.”
NOTE: Customers who are going through disability retirement will lose eligibility if they are terminated. They will have 60 days to re-enroll once they receive a CSA# and their annuity is finalized. Retirees who choose to continue their OWCP payments in lieu of a retirement will continue their eligibility. Not all OWCP claims are deductible.

units.heading: Financial Document Requests
units.text: Financial Document Requests

units.heading: Financial Document Requests
units.text: There may be times when enrollees call to request certain letters from BENEFEDS to assist with reimbursements or tax filing purposes. This is a condensed list of letter types and when they are to be used.

units.heading: Correspondence AWD Ticket:
units.text:
Correspondence AWD Ticket:
Post Tax Premium: Used when an enrollee requests record of annual premium amount paid with post tax funds. This is only submitted for tax purposes. To request this letter, submit a Correspondence AWD ticket and select “Post Tax Premium” from the drop down.
**Note: This should only be used for PRIOR plan years and not the current plan year.
Premium Statement: Used when an enrollee requests an account of what premiums were requested and that BENEFEDS has received premium payments for during a requested time period. To request this letter, submit a Correspondence AWD ticket and select “Premium Statement” from the drop down. NOTE: Team Lead approval is required.
Premium Inquiry AWD Ticket:
Account Statement: Account statements can only be sent for POST TAX payments. Used when an enrollee needs a statement of their Health Savings Account (HSA) Reimbursement. To request this letter, submit a Premium Inquiry AWD work item select “General Premium Inquiry” subcategory “New Account Statement”. Note: These requests are specific to the timeframe in which the customer provides. EX: Customer needs an account statement for premiums paid between 11/01/2022 through 02/01/2023.
**Note: This option should only be used for Military Affiliations. A USM member can request an HSA statement through the Premium Inquiry/Account Statement process for any premiums that have been received and posted to the account. These requests can be for any period of time.
Other:
Low Income Housing Forms: Used when an enrollee needs information from BENEFEDS to complete an application for Low Income Housing. BENEFEDS does not provide the needed information for these forms- but you can provide the enrollee this email address for assistance: benefedsadministration@benefeds.gov

units.heading: Foreign Blocked Countries
units.text:
As part of a standard review of our security and systems, LTCP identified certain countries that will be blocked from accessing our websites in an effort to protect against any potential malicious activity. This is effective immediately and may limit the customer’s ability to use BENEFEDS.gov.
Use the talking points below to help if a person in an affected country contacts you.

units.heading: Talking Points
units.text:
Will the entire site be blocked or will some functionality be available?
“To protect against any potential malicious activity, the entire LTCFEDS.gov site will be blocked. If you need assistance, Please contact the FLTCIP Customer Service Center at 1-800-LTC-FEDS (1-800-582-3337) TTY 1-800-843-3557 for all program-related inquiries or contact the BENEFEDS Customer Service Center at 1-877-888-FEDS (1-877-888-3337) TTY 1-877-889-5680 for premium-related inquiries. If you are calling from outside the United States, dial your country’s international access code, followed by +1-571-730-5942.”
How will I pay my premium if I currently use BENEFEDS.gov?
“BENEFEDS administers the premium payment processes on behalf of the FLTCIP. A BENEFEDS customer service representative will be happy to assist with your payment inquiry, contact BENEFEDS Customer Service Center at 1-877-888-FEDS (1-877-888-3337) TTY 1-877-889-5680. If you are calling from outside the United States, dial your country’s international access code, followed by +1-571-730-5942.”
Are the FLTCIP and BENEFEDS 800-numbers international toll-free numbers?
“The FLTCIP and BENEFEDS numbers are domestic 800-numbers. To contact us from outside the United States, dial your country’s international access code, followed by +1-571-730-5942.”
Will the site be restricted if I use an incognito browser?
“Yes, the site will be restricted if you live in one of the following countries: Ukraine, China, Russia or North Korea.”
Which countries are affected by this change?
“We are blocking access to our website for anyone residing in Ukraine, China, Russia, and North Korea.”
What is causing this change?
“Long Term Care Partners regularly monitors our systems to ensure they are secure. We have identified certain countries that we will block from accessing our website in an effort to protect against any potential malicious activity. All website activity will continue to be monitored on an ongoing basis.”

units.heading: Overview of GEHA
units.text:
Overview of GEHA
GEHA (Government Employees Health Association) Connection Dental Federal is a national/international dental carrier under the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP). It offers comprehensive dental services with additional vision and hearing benefits integrated into its plans.
Pronunciation and Contact Information:
- Pronunciation: GEHA can be pronounced as "Gee-Ha" (hard G as in 'Green') or spelled out as G-E-H-A.
- Phone: 1-877-434-2336
- Website: [www.gehadental.com](http://www.gehadental.com)
- Hours of Operation: Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. CST, year-round.

units.heading: Overview of GEHA · Integrated Benefits
units.text:
Integrated Benefits:
Vision Benefit: GEHA includes a vision benefit through EyeMed within its dental plan. Customers may receive an EyeMed ID card and inquire about its purpose, not realizing it is part of their dental plan enrollment.
Hearing Benefit: A hearing aid discount plan through TruHearing is also included, applicable to both dental and medical plan enrollees.
Common Customer Queries:
- Vision Benefit Inquiry:
- Customer Question: "Can you tell me more about the GEHA vision benefit I received?“

units.heading: Guidelines for VTO (Voluntary Time Off)
units.text: This guide is a quick reminder to help you understand how VTO works and what to expect when requesting it. Use it as an easy reference anytime you're planning your schedule.

units.heading: VTO Request Process
units.text:
VTO Request Process
- Employees submit VTO requests on a first-come, first-served basis but approval depends on staffing and operational needs.
Approval and Work Requirements
- Submitting VTO does not guarantee approval; employees must continue working unless explicitly approved to leave.
Impact on Breaks and Lunches
- Selecting VTO mid-shift may adjust or remove breaks depending on total paid hours remaining in the shift.
Monitoring VTO Confirmation
- Employees should wait for official approval confirmation before leaving to ensure operational fairness and accuracy.
Taking VTO Blocks Mid-Shift
- If your shift continues after your VTO block ends, you’re expected to return and work the remaining scheduled time.

units.heading: Background:
units.text:
Background:
FSAFEDS is a Flexible Spending Account (FSA) program available to Federal Employees in the Executive Branch and other agencies that have adopted the program. Aside from processing premium deductions for the FEDVIP, BENEFEDS also processes the FSAFEDS allotments for Federal Employees. BENEFEDS does NOT process enrollments, claims, or reimbursement for the program or have any other program details.
If you receive a call from an enrollee inquiring about FSAFEDS:
- Educate the customer on BENEFEDS role by explaining BENEFEDS manages allotments for FSAFEDS along with enrollments, changes, and premium deductions for FEDVIP.
- Ask if they have questions about their FSAFEDS Allotments or if they have questions about FSA reimbursements, claims, or enrollments.
- If they are asking about FSAFEDS Allotments, advise you must transfer them to our research department and then transfer the call to Research.
- If they are calling about FSA reimbursements, claims, enrollments, or have other program questions, advise they must contact FSAFEDS directly. Provide the contact information and offer to transfer them.
Demographic Updates:
Updates made to their BENEFEDS account do not transfer to FESAFEDS. If the customer needs to update their demographics and is enrolled in FSAFEDS, they must contact FSAFEDS directly. Provide the caller FSAFEDS contact information and offer to transfer the call.
FSAFEDS Contact Info:
Website: www.FSAFEDS.gov
Phone: 1-877-372-3337
TTY: 1-866-353-8058
International: 1-650-577-5294
Fax: 1-866-643-2245
Hours of operation: Monday – Friday 9AM – 9PM EST
NOTE: BENEFEDS Customer Service does not have access to FSA only accounts. BENEFEDS Customer service is not required to verify FSA accounts before transferring unless they have FEDVIP Questions.

units.text:
FedPoint Media Inquiry Policy
The following guidelines are to be referenced in the event that a call or email is received from an outside party seeking information regarding FedPoint’s contracts or potential business lines.
This includes, but is not limited to, any representative from a media outlet (newspaper, magazine, digital, television, radio), insurance professionals, or any individual from an outside healthcare, financial, legal, lobbying, or consulting firm, or consumer advocacy group.
Talking Points:
- I’m sorry, I don’t normally handle these types of questions. While I don’t have an answer for you, we do have a process in place to get you what you need.
- We request that all such inquiries be sent, in writing, to media@fedpointusa.com and we will respond in a timely manner.
- In your email, please include:
- Name
- Organization
- Best e-mail/phone number to reach you
- Specific question(s) you would like answered
- Deadline (if applicable)
If pressed for a contact or response, such as “Can you provide me with the contact information of the folks who have the information?”, please provide the following statement along with the contact information below:
- Just a moment, I’ll get that information for you. The contact is Matt Piper or Tim Cullity. However, our policy is to respond to these types of inquiries in writing via our media inbox.
PR Process
- Notify your Supervisor or TL of the inquiry.
- Unless otherwise instructed by your Supervisor or TL, Notify (via email only) Tim and Matt and CC your manager/director.
- The FedPoint team will coordinate a response with John Hancock and OPM as appropriate.
- If it is a FLTCIP/BENEFEDS matter, OPM will send the response unless requested otherwise.

sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Handling a Leave Without Pay Call.pptx

slides.title: Handling a Leave Without Pay Call

units.heading: Background:
units.text:
Background:
- Federal employees on Leave Without Pay (LWOP) may include those on military deployment, maternity leave, or other personal leaves.
- During LWOP, BENEFEDS issues direct bills as these employees are not receiving regular paychecks.
Key Points for Handling LWOP Calls:
- Notification of LWOP Status:
- BENEFEDS is informed of LWOP through a No Deduction Reason code 'L' sent by the employee's payroll office (APO).
- Direct billing starts after receiving at least two L-codes from consecutive pay periods.
- Direct Billing Process:
- A DV24 letter is sent to the enrollee’s registered address, informing them about the start of direct billing.
- Direct bills are issued every other pay period.
- Enrollees must pay all direct bills to maintain their FEDVIP coverage.
- While direct billing we will continue to bill the APO.
- Upon Return from LWOP:
- When an employee returns to work, BENEFEDS resumes premium deductions from their pay.
- If there are any past-due amounts, BENEFEDS may initiate double deductions until the backlog is cleared.
- Non-Payment during LWOP:
- If the account is inactive, the overnight address cannot be offered as an option to reinstate. The post mark date of the payment must be prior to the date of the inactivation.
- The 30-day timeframe for submission of payment for reinstatement on the (DV35) only applies if they are in active pay status receiving pay from the APO.
- Those who are in inactive pay status must wait until they return to work to re-enroll.
- Exceptions and Adjustments:
- If an enrollee’s address is incorrect and leads to missed correspondence, reinstatement may be considered.
- Overpayments identified will be adjusted as per the Adjustment Letter (DV58), and excess payments will be accounted for.

slides.title: Handling a Leave Without Pay Call

units.heading: Reinstatement Rules:
units.text:
Reinstatement Rules:
- Generally, enrollees cannot be reinstated after inactivation due to non-pay, except if caused by incorrect address issues. After the address has been updated in the CS system, an AWD Reinstatement ticket may be submitted. If not due to an invalid address issue, the customer will be ineligible for reinstatement regardless of their pay status. They must re-enroll within 60 days of returning to a paid status.
- Enrollees will need to have returned to an Active Pay status to be reinstated.
- If member inactivates for non-pay and enrolled in both dental and vision, they DO NOT have to pay on both programs, they can make payment on either or.
- If a customer was inactivated during Open Season and they are calling to reinstate after Open Season ends, PAT will not reinstate because they had the opportunity to address this during Open Season. Exception: This will be an exception only if they had an invalid address.
Option to Submit Payment in the BENEFEDS CSS:
- Reinstatement is based on an enrollee’s employment status at the time of inactivation.
- If the APO is not sending L codes when the account termed for non-pay, the ACH reinstatement option will be provided.
- Customers may make the reinstatement payment, and they will be reinstated if payment is received by the due date regardless of their current employment status.
- If the customer is calling to make a payment and the option to do so exists in the system, process the payment.
Talking Points for Agents:
- "Ensure your address with BENEFEDS is current to receive all billing and communication."
- "Please make arrangements to pay your direct bills on time to avoid disruption in your FEDVIP coverage."
Note:
If a member is currently on LWOP during Open Enrollment season they will not be able to enroll. Once they return to active pay status, they can enroll with a QLE return from being on LWOP.

units.heading: Hold and Transfer Procedures & Scripting
units.text: Follow the appropriate guidelines below when you need to place the caller on hold or transfer the call.

units.heading: Hold and Transfer Procedures & Scripting
units.text:
Placing the Caller on Hold:
- Politely let the caller know you will place them on a brief hold, that you appreciate their patience and will return promptly.
- Before two minutes (2)** of hold time lapses, check back with the caller. If more research is required, take the caller off hold and let them know that you are still researching the account and ask if they are alright holding for a few more minutes. Thank the customer for holding once you return to the lin
- ** Agents who are warm transferring the customer will follow the previous 4 minute timeframe.
Transferring the Call Internally:
- Let the caller know you will be transferring them to the appropriate department/person.
- Ask if you may place the caller on hold while you complete the transfer.
- Follow the appropriate transfer process within CXone Agent by either instant (cold) transferring, or warm transferring the call.
- Be sure to leave transfer notes for the receiving agent when placing a cold transfer.
Transferring to a Carrier:
Before offering to transfer a call to the carrier, briefly explain why you need to transfer them by clarifying that BENEFEDS manages enrollment and premium billing while carriers handle claims and coverage, only provide additional role details that are related to the reason for the call.

units.heading: Hold and Transfer Procedures & Scripting
units.text:
Suggested Scripting:
“May I place you on a brief hold while I look into this for you?”
“Do you mind if I place you on hold for a moment while I research this?”
“Thank you for holding, Mrs. Jones, I will need some more time to research your account. Are you alright with holding a little longer?”
“I'll need to place you on brief hold for a moment while I review you account / billing / etc. I appreciate your patience.”
“Thank you for holding, Mrs. Jones. I was able to locate that information for you.”
“Unfortunately, I am unable to assist you with ___, however I’d be glad to transfer you to someone who can help. Would you mind if I placed you on a brief hold while I transfer you?”

sources.title: Humana's Alternate Effective Date
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Humana's Alternate Effective Date.pptx

units.heading: Humana's Alternate Effective Date
units.text: This job aid explains the concept of the "Alternate Effective Date" used by Humana for FEDVIP enrollments and how it affects customer coverage and claims processing.

units.heading: Humana records FEDVIP coverage start dates in two ways:
units.text:
Humana records FEDVIP coverage start dates in two ways:
- Standard Display Date: This is the date shown on Humana’s website and used in general communication, typically the first day of the first full month following enrollment.
- Alternate Effective Date: This is the actual start date of coverage which may not fall on the first of the month. It is used internally for claims processing but is not visible on the website or mentioned in the Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system.
Example:
- If an enrollee’s actual coverage effective date is April 22, 2012.
- The date displayed on Humana’s website will be May 1, 2012.
- The "Alternate Effective Date" used for processing claims will be April 22, 2012.
Steps to Verify Coverage Effective Date:
Warm Transfer: If an enrollee has concerns about the accuracy of their coverage start date:
- Initiate a warm conference call with Humana.
- Request the Humana representative to confirm and explain the "Alternate Effective Date" to the enrollee.
Talking Points for Common Queries:
Query on Humana/CompBenefits:
"Yes, CompBenefits is now known as Humana/CompBenefits. All contact information remains the same. If you have any specific questions about your coverage, I can provide their contact details or transfer you directly to them for assistance."
Usage:
This information is crucial for customer service representatives handling inquiries about Humana’s FEDVIP plans, ensuring accurate information is provided regarding coverage dates and claims processing. It also aids in clarifying any confusion customers may have with the transition from CompBenefits to Humana/CompBenefits.
Note:
Representatives should be aware that while they cannot see the "Alternate Effective Date," they can assure enrollees that Humana uses this date for all claims related decisions, and it reflects the actual start of coverage as per the enrollment details.

sources.title: Incident vs Breach
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Incident vs Breach.pptx

units.heading: Background
units.text:
Background
FedPoint’s contracts with OPM require us to report incidents. A breach needs to be reported within 30 minutes of discovery by FedPoint. For an incident, we have to report within 2 hours of discovery. This is a performance metric that impacts our profit margin—and it is a metric that we often miss because the timeframes are tight. If someone discovers an issue but does not report it to Compliance until several hours or days later, it counts against our performance metric.

units.heading: Incident vs Breach
units.text: What is a Breach? | What is an Incident?

units.heading: Incident vs Breach
units.text:
Some incidents are also a breach of PII (personally identifiable information—such as a name + DOB, or an enrollee’s social security number) and/or PHI (protected health information—the fact that someone has long term care insurance or dental or vision insurance is an example of PHI).
FedPoint is bound by HIPAA to ensure the privacy and security of all our customers’ PII and PHI.
If this information is somehow divulged to a third party, we need to investigate what happened and analyze what and how we need to report to the government.
Examples Include:
• PHI or PII is disclosed without proper security information first being confirmed.
• Account information is disclosed to an unauthorized third party.

units.heading: Incident vs Breach
units.text:
Anything that adversely impacts customer service, enrollee satisfaction, or OPM constituencies (such as the payroll offices, FEDVIP carriers, etc.).
Examples Include:
• Misdirected communications (faxes, emails, letters that went to the wrong person or organization)
• System outages (externally facing websites, call center phones).

units.heading: Incident vs Breach
units.text: A breach is almost always an incident; an incident (such as a call center outage) is not always a breach.

units.heading: Updated Guidance: Workforce Changes – 2025 Impacts
units.text:
Updated Guidance: Workforce Changes – 2025 Impacts
We are no longer allowing reinstatements for customers who were impacted by the 2025 Workforce (WF) changes, as the Open Season (OS) has since passed.
Customers who:
- Remain eligible for FEDVIP, and
- were inactivated in 2025 due to WF changes,
Must now meet one of the following criteria to enroll:
- Experience a valid Qualifying Life Event (QLE) and submit an enrollment within the required timeframes, or
- Wait until the next Federal Benefits Open Season.
Reinstatements based on the original 2025 workforce changes are no longer permitted.
Additionally:
- Customers who elected Deferred Resignation are no longer able to close any gaps in their coverage.
- These customers must follow the standard enrollment rules and cannot retroactively correct or reinstate coverage for periods in which they were inactive.

sources.title: Insufficient Funds
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Insufficient Funds.pptx

units.heading: Insufficient Funds
units.text:
Sometimes an enrollee does not have enough money in their paycheck or annuity check to pay their FEDVIP premium. The Federal government refers to this as insufficient funds. Enrollees who have insufficient funds are still eligible for the FEDVIP and must continue their FEDVIP enrollment. There are many reasons why enrollees may not have enough money in their pay or annuity check to pay their premiums:
- They may have other deductions coming out of their paycheck.
- If they are employed, the Federal government only allows a certain percentage of their total deductions to be made on a pretax basis.
- If the amount allotted to have come out of their paycheck for pretax deductions exceeds the allowable amount set by the Federal government.
- Some annuitants or survivor annuitants receive a small monthly annuity.
- After BENEFEDS receives notification that an enrollee has insufficient funds in their paycheck or annuity check, the enrollee will be sent a direct bill.
- Annuitants and Survivor Annuitants will have an opportunity to pay by automatic bank withdrawal (ABW) deductions if the enrollee states their FEDVIP deductions are causing their annuity to be insufficient for FEHB premium deductions, or if BENEFEDS requests a double deduction and the annuity is insufficient.

units.heading: Enrollee has insufficient funds
units.text:
Enrollee has insufficient funds:
- BENEFEDS will receive an insufficient funds error code (I-Code) on the payment file from most APOs.
- Some APOs will send other codes such as S, B, F, or Z codes under the Error Code column. (Refer to Page 3 of the Premium Administration Codes Job Aid for Error Code Long Names from the specific APOs.)
- Enrollee's billing status will change to Direct after receiving two I-codes or an I-code and a null or $0.00 amount.
- BENEFEDS will send their first direct bill for the entire past due amount on the first odd pay sequence after the billing status was change to Direct.
- BENEFEDS will continue to send bill files to the enrollee's APO and send direct bills until a successful deduction is made from their paycheck/annuity check again.
- The enrollee must pay the direct bills to maintain their FEDVIP enrollment.
- If an Annuitant/SA receives and I-code on a single deduction we will send out a direct bill, but to have the option to switch to ABW we would need to have received a I-code on a double deduction.
- When being direct billed, if the enrollee is current and is not past due, there is no option to make an ACH payment.

units.heading: Insufficient Funds
units.text: - Increased FEHB Premiums can't be deducted due to not having enough in the annuity because of FEDVIP deductions. An Agency Name Change/Claim # ticket will need to be submitted. The customer can choose to be placed on Direct Bill or ABW with the new POI of (PENDB01 or PENAB01). If the customer chooses ABW, the banking information will need to be included on the ticket along with the new POI.

sources.title: Intermittent Payors
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Intermittent Payors.pptx

units.heading: Intermittent Payor Background Information:
units.text:
Intermittent Payor Background Information:
Some enrollees may encounter periods of time where they are paid intermittently.
- Deductions are considered intermittent (Federal Civilian only) if:
- A $0.00 payment is received, followed by a positive payment, and then another $0.00 payment in consecutive pay periods and there is a past due balance equal to or greater than 4x the current premium amount.
- The system logic would inactivate these accounts for non-payment of premium; however, the intermittent payroll deductions interrupt the non-pay termination process:
- This results is an accumulated past due.
- The Premium Admin Team works to identify these intermittent payees and will switch the accounts to the APO’s corresponding ABW location in order to collect premium payments.
- If the enrollee does not provide ABW information within 30 days of being switched to ABW, the account gets updated to Direct Bill status, and the direct bill location is changed to Direct Intermittent for PAYDB03 or PAYDB04.
- Note: Once an enrollee is no longer in a direct bill status, even if a direct bill was sent, the enrollee cannot make an ACH online payment.
conditions: Note: Once an enrollee is no longer in a direct bill status, even if a direct bill was sent, the enrollee cannot make an ACH online payment.

units.heading: Intermittent Payor Background Information · Example of Intermittent Pay
units.text:
Example of Intermittent Pay:
- Pay Period 1: $0.00 pay received (no premium deduction).
- Pay Period 2: Positive pay received (premium successfully deducted).
- Pay Period 3: $0.00 pay received (no premium deduction).
- Pay Period 4: Customer is changed to an ABW location and has 30 days to provide their ABW info.
- If after 30 days no ABW information is received, they are switched to a Direct Bill location. If they want to return to their APO location, they must have returned to a full-time status AND have no past due amount.

units.heading: Intermittent Payor Background Information · Handling Intermittent Payors
units.text:
Handling Intermittent Payors:
Once the account has been changed to an ABW/DB location, BENEFEDS will not be notified by their original APO if/when the enrollee returns to work.
The enrollee must notify BENEFEDS that they have returned to work if they wish to resume pre-tax payroll deductions.
- If the enrollee calls to request to be changed back to payroll and has returned to work:
- Submit an AWD Agency Name Change (refer to the FEDVIP AWD Processor-Primary AWD Work Item Job Aid for assistance) to return the enrollee to payroll deductions.
- Advise the enrollee they must send in a payment for the entire past due amount.
- If this is the first request to return to payroll deductions and a payment for the past due has not been received at the time of the request, PAT will honor the request and move the enrollee back to payroll.
- If the enrollee becomes intermittent again, PAT will not make the change to payroll unless the enrollee has returned to work and the past due amount is paid in full.

sources.title: Leave Without Pay (LWOP)
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Leave Without Pay (LWOP).pptx

units.heading: Who’s eligible
units.text:
Who’s eligible
Only Federal or U.S Postal employees may take a leave of absence from their job and not be paid. When these instances occur, the Federal government calls this “leave without pay” (LWOP). When an employee is on LWOP, they are still eligible for the FEDVIP because they still hold their Federal status.
Billing
- BENEFEDS is notified of an enrollee’s LWOP status via the L-code on the payment file.
- Direct bills will be sent after the first two L-codes on the payment file.
- When the employee has returned to their job or retired, BENEFEDS will automatically begin deducting premiums from their pay or annuity.
- If the employee terminates their Federal employment, BENEFEDS will inactivate their FEDVIP coverage.

units.heading: Who’s eligible · Reinstatement
units.text:
Reinstatement
- If an account is inactivated due to non-payment, reinstatements will not be granted unless;
- The account has the incorrect address that delayed billing, then an AWD Reinstatement ticket may be submitted after the mailing address is updated.
- If the account on LWOP is inactive, the overnight address can not be offered as an option to reinstate. The post mark date of the payment must be prior to the date of the inactivation.

units.heading: Who’s eligible · Option to Submit Payment in the BENEFEDS CSS
units.text:
Option to Submit Payment in the BENEFEDS CSS:
- Reinstatement is based on an enrollee’s employment status at the time of inactivation.
- If the APO is not sending L codes when the account termed for non-pay, the ACH reinstatement option will be provided.

sources.title: Managing Break in Federal Service
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Managing Break in Federal Service.pptx

units.heading: Definition of Break in Service:
units.text:
Definition of Break in Service:
A break in federal service occurs when there is a termination followed by a rehire, leading to a gap in employment and eligibility. This can result in a loss of coverage.
Reinstatement Overview:
Reinstatement applies when an employee is reactivated without a loss of eligibility, usually due to an error or oversight, allowing them to continue coverage without interruption.
Handling Enrollments:
- 3 Days or less:
- Reinstatement can only take place when the separation is 3 calendar days or less.
- Submit a Primary – Reinstatement AWD ticket.
- Short Break (4 days - 29 days):
- No changes to previous enrollment allowed unless due to a qualifying life event (QLE), like moving outside a carrier's service area or changes in family status.
- Long Break (30 days or more):
- Treat as a new hire; enrollee can make any desired changes to their enrollment.
- Update employment status to New Hire with the rehire date.
- Enrollment becomes effective the first day of the pay period following rehire.
Special Circumstances:
- Some roles detailed in FEDVIP regulations (e.g., emergency responders) may have unique rules affecting enrollment during breaks in service.
- If an employee returns after a break of less than 30 days without previous FEDVIP enrollment, they must wait for Open Season or another QLE to enroll.
Administrative Actions:
- Update the Department/Agency if needed.
- For approved changes, use the system to adjust enrollment details and communicate any changes through confirmation emails or letters.
Note: Always verify the specific circumstances of a break in service or reinstatement to ensure compliance with FEDVIP regulations and avoid processing errors that are time-consuming to correct.

sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Medicare & Medicaid Questions.pptx

units.heading: Medicare & Medicaid Questions
units.text:
As a reminder, we have been asked to collect information regarding customer’s enrollment in Medicare and Medicaid.
- These questions need to be asked on all accounts where the pop-up is present, unless the caller is requesting cancellation or disenrollment and do not have an existing enrollment.
- You are required to get three pieces of security when asking the Medicare and Medicaid questions.
- Don’t ask these questions to customers who are calling to cancel coverage with a valid QLE or are reporting the death of an enrollee unless they have an existing plan year enrollment.
What is Medicare/Medicaid?
- Medicare is a federal health insurance program primarily for people aged 65 and older, as well as some younger individuals with disabilities or certain medical conditions. It has different parts that cover hospital stays, medical services, prescription drugs, and more.
- Medicaid is a joint federal and state program that provides health coverage for individuals and families with low income. Eligibility and benefits vary by state, but it generally covers essential health services like doctor visits, hospital care, and long-term care.

units.heading: Medicare & Medicaid Questions
units.text:
- If given the Medicare & Medicaid questions, please provide the questions to the enrollee and allow them to answer.
- If the enrollee is unsure of their enrollment into Medicare or Medicaid, advise them that is no issue, and mark their enrollment as "No" in the CSS.
- If no pop-up occurs when the enrollee’s account is access, that indicates they have already provided an answer to the Medicare & Medicaid questions.

units.heading: If a caller asks why we are collecting this information, you may state the following:
units.text:
If a caller asks why we are collecting this information, you may state the following:
“We are asking for this information to assist your FEDVIP dental and/or vision plan with coordinating your benefits with those programs.”
“For additional information or further questions on the coordination of benefits, please reach out to your carrier.“
For L2 Agents Only:
If you are creating a Primary – Enrollment AWD ticket:
- Please include the answers to the Medicare and Medicaid questions, otherwise the customer’s enrollment cannot be processed.
- If the Tricare questions have not been answered, include those in the ticket as well. You will know if they have previously been answered if they do not appear in the enrollment flow.
- Only new accounts that were created after the Tricare questions were added will need these answered.

units.heading: Members with Multiple Accounts:
units.text:
Members with Multiple Accounts:
You may encounter members who have two different accounts. In some cases, one account will have a correct Social Security Number, whereas the other account will not. This often occurs when members accidentally enter their SSN incorrectly online, are unable to change it, and create a new account with the correct SSN.
Handling Members with Multiple Accounts:
L1 Agents: Transfer the member to a Senior Representative (L2)

- Add the correct SSN in the NEW SSN field
- Include the Member ID associated with the correct SSN in the AWD Comments
- If there is other enrollment information that needs to transfer to the correct account, enter that information into the AWD Comments
- Advise the caller their ticket will be processed in the order it is received, typically within 3-5 business days

units.heading: How do you know if a Survivor is a New Survivor?
units.text:
How do you know if a Survivor is a New Survivor?
Survivor Annuitants are considered new when they are calling to enroll within 60 days of:
- Date of death of the primary enrollee, OR
- Date they received their CSF Claim # from OPM OR
- Date of the letter (DV11) sent by BENEFEDS.
OPM Survivor Annuitants must have received their CSF Claim Number. If they have received their CSF# and are calling within one of the timeframes above, they are eligible to enroll.

units.heading: New Survivor Annuitant Create Account
units.text: If the Survivor is newly eligible, you must create the account. L1 reps then transfer the call to a Senior Representative to complete the enrollment.

units.heading: New Survivor Annuitant Create Account
units.text: If the Survivor is not newly eligible, and has a Qualifying Life Event, such as loss of coverage, you may proceed and submit a QLE enrollment.

units.heading: Survivor Annuitants Receiving an OPM Annuity
units.text:
Survivor Annuitants Receiving an OPM Annuity
Survivor Annuitants who answer no to receiving a Survivor Basic Employee Death Benefit from their spouse or if the deceased is a child, will be asked of they receive a survivor annuity from OPM.
- If they answer yes, they will need to provide their CSF claim number.
- They will also be required to provide the decedent (deceased’s) social security number
- If they cannot provide these pieces of information, the account cannot be created at this time.

units.heading: Lump Sum vs Coupon Program
units.text: The below information clarifies the 'Lump Sum or Coupon Program' question in the Customer Service System. The question appears after selecting a spouse and answering “yes” to whether the beneficiary has received a Survivor Basic Employee Death Benefit. The descriptions below will help in selecting the correct payment setup for new survivor annuitant accounts.

units.heading: Lump Sum vs Coupon Program
units.text:
Lump Sum Option:
A one-time payment received by the beneficiary. Deductions for FEDVIP premiums cannot be taken directly from this amount, so beneficiaries are set up with Automatic Bank Withdrawal (ABW) or direct billing for premium payments immediately.
Coupon Program:
The lump sum is divided into 36 monthly payments over three years. During this period, FEDVIP premiums can be deducted directly from these payments. After the three-year term, BENEFEDS coordinates with OPM to transition the beneficiary to ABW or direct billing for future payments.

units.heading: Lump Sum vs Coupon Program
units.text:
- Customers on lump sum or coupon program will not have a CSF#
- They will still need to provide the decedent social security number.

- “Do you have dependents that are currently receiving ongoing orthodontic services?”

- If no to both questions, the survivor may choose a Prospective Enrollment.
- Complete the enrollment in the CS System by entering the date of death when prompted. If it is outside the 60 days, enter the date of the DV11 letter.
- For OPM Survivor Annuitants Only:
- If they are calling outside of 60 days of the date of death or the date of the DV11, you may use the date they provide for receipt of their CSF Claim #. Enter this in the field for “Survivor Annuitant Letter”.
- OPM survivors must only have received their CSF# to enroll. The do not need to have it on hand to enroll and do not need to call back to provide it to us.
- After completing the enrollment, submit a Primary-Agency Name Change/Claim # AWD Work Item to provided the CSF# to PAT. CSF claim numbers are typically 7 digits, provide the full number to PAT.
- This ticket only needs to be submitted if the customer is submitting an enrollment. Please do not submit this ticket on a registration only as it will be NIGO’d.
- Paste the generated AutoSummary comment to both the survivor's and the deceased’s account.

units.heading: Child Survivor Enrollment (FEDCIV-Annuitant) Under Age 16
units.text:
Child Survivor Enrollment (FEDCIV-Annuitant) Under Age 16
Once you have confirmed the Primary is not receiving SSI benefits you may experience an error enrolling the dependent. When you receive a call from a Parent or guardian of a Survivor who is under 16 years of age there is a Defect preventing the enrollment. You will see an error message populate; this is due to the DOB making the primary less than 16 years of age. Follow these steps to complete the enrollment.
- As a rule, we should create the registration with the youngest child as the Primary. This ensures seamless coverage for all dependents until they age off.
- Edit the Profile: Change the Year of Birth so the child appears older than 16.
- After the profile has been completed and saved, go back into the profile and fix the DOB so that its correct.
- Proceed with the enrollment as normal. A Chorus ticket is not necessary.

units.heading: Removing an Ineligible Family Member from a Deceased’s Account:
units.text:
Removing an Ineligible Family Member from a Deceased’s Account:
Removing an ineligible family member from a deceased account before inactivation through a third party is considered part of closing out the deceased's affairs and will not require documentation. This is not considered a HIPAA matter.
- EX: I’m an Adult child of a member who passed 7/01/2025. I call BENEFEDS to inactivate his account. During the interaction it was discovered my mother who passed in Sept 2023 was never removed.
- BENEFEDS CS can act by removing the family member through the third party as part of closing the deceased's affairs. No legal documentation is required.
- CSR can escalate concerns to a supervisor, and we can consult compliance before acting.

units.heading: Background: New Survivor Enrollment
units.text:
Background: New Survivor Enrollment
If a previously covered family member had services under the decedent's enrollment after the paid through date, but before the last day of the pay period in which the deceased passed, then they may send in payment for that pay period(s) and have their claims covered.
- Payments submitted for this reason must be applied to the Deceased’s account, not the Survivor’s account.
To be certain on the amount to send in, please submit a Premium Inquiry ticket, requesting the amounts needed to get the paid thru date to the last day of the Pay Period when deceased passed.
Once this has been calculated the Research department will call out to give the survivor the amounts to send in.

Survivor Annuitants are considered new when they are calling to enroll within 60 days of:

units.heading: Lump Sum vs Coupon Program
units.text: The below information clarifies the 'Lump Sum or Coupon Program' question in the Customer Service System. The question appears after selecting a spouse and answering “yes” to whether the beneficiary has received a Survivor Basic Employee Death Benefit. The descriptions below will help in selecting the correct payment setup for new survivor annuitant accounts.

units.heading: Lump Sum vs Coupon Program
units.text:
Lump Sum Option:
A one-time payment received by the beneficiary. Deductions for FEDVIP premiums cannot be taken directly from this amount, so beneficiaries are set up with Automatic Bank Withdrawal (ABW) or direct billing for premium payments immediately.
Coupon Program:
The lump sum is divided into 36 monthly payments over three years. During this period, FEDVIP premiums can be deducted directly from these payments. After the three-year term, BENEFEDS coordinates with OPM to transition the beneficiary to ABW or direct billing for future payments.

units.heading: Non-FEDVIP Program Information (1/2)
units.text:
This job aid provides information, tips and talking points for FEHB, Tricare, and PSHB programs for situations where callers are confused about the differences between those programs and FEDVIP.
FEHB Information
- Identify it’s an FEHB Call:
- When the customer refers to health insurance or medical insurance.
- If they are a Federal employee or Federal Annuitant (for USPS employees and annuitants, refer to the PSHB Talking Points job aid).
- Use other ways to describe FEHB.
- Federal Employees Health Benefit
- Medical or health insurance
- There are no search results for your customer.
- Explain the difference between FEHB and FEDVIP:
- Explain that FEHB is for Federal medical coverage and FEDVIP is for dental and vision coverage.
- FEHB and FEDVIP are completely different federal benefits.
- Explain that the customer can contact their FEHB by:
- Going to www.opm.gov/insure and clicking on Healthcare (see image on the right).
- Speaking to HR or Benefits Officer at work.
- Locating their health insurance ID card and looking for a phone number on the card.
Loss of the Tricare Retiree Dental Program
During Open Season 2018, BENEFEDS welcomed the Retired Uniformed Services Members and their families to FEDVIP. Over 850,000 people were enrolled in the Tricare Retiree Dental Program (TRDP) which came to an end on December 31, 2018.
Due to the loss of TRDP, retirees and their families were encouraged to enroll in FEDVIP. Therefore, a Retired uniform service members and their families who were eligible for the TRICARE Retiree Dental Program (TRDP) are eligible for FEDVIP dental coverage.
As a result of this transition from TRDP to FEDVIP for Uniformed Service Members and their eligible dependents, a Newly Eligible USM is “someone who has recently retired from active- duty military service”.
- Note: If they are enrolled in a TRICARE health plan, then they are also eligible for vision.
conditions: Note: If they are enrolled in a TRICARE health plan, then they are also eligible for vision.

units.heading: Non-FEDVIP Program Information (2/2)
units.text:
PSHB Information
- Identify it’s a PSHB call:
- When the customer refers to health insurance or medical insurance
- If they are a USPS employee or USPS annuitant (for all other affiliation types, refer to the FEHB Call Tips job aid)
- Use other ways to describe PSHB
- Postal Service Health Benefit
- Medical or health insurance
- There are no search results for your customer
- Explain the difference between PSHB and FEDVIP:
- Explain that PSHB is for USPS medical coverage and FEDVIP is for dental and vision coverage
- PSHB and FEDVIP are completely different federal benefits
- What is the Postal Service Health Benefits Program (PSHB)?
- The Postal Service Health Benefits (PSHB) program is a new health insurance program for Postal Service employees, retirees, and their families. It is part of the Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) program and is administered by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM).
- When does coverage under the PSHB begin?
- Coverage for the PSHB starts the new year after open season. Enrollment in the PSHB program will be available during the Open Season period that typically runs from the 2nd week of November through the 2nd week of December..
- What role does BENEFEDS play in PSHB?
- The PSHB program is not managed by BENEFEDS. We have no additional information about the program.
- Who should I speak to regarding PSHB?
- Postal Workers and Annuitants wanting to speak to PSHB to the following phone number: 877-477-3273 (Option 5)
- Hours of Operation: 7:00 AM – 8:45 PM EST, Monday – Friday
- Will PSHB affect my other federal benefits?
- Your FEDVIP dental and/or vison plan may coordinate benefits with your PSHB plan if your PSHB plan has dental or vison coverage.
- Enrolling in PSHB will not affect your other benefits, such as:
- Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP)
- Federal Flexible Spending Account Program (FSAFEDS)
- Federal Long Term Care Insurance Program (FLTCIP)

units.text: Non-Appropriated Funds, is revenue made from a business, and not government funds. For example, if there is a gas station on base, the cashier’s paycheck is pulled from the revenue of that gas station (non-appropriated funds) and not from government funds.
conditions: Note: The NAF agency option on the Payroll Schedule is only for Federal Civilian employees who have a NAF annuity.

units.heading: NAF Employees:
units.text:
NAF Employees:
- Are being paid with non-appropriated funds.
- Typically, they establish a NAF Annuity for their retirement.
- NAF Employees are not Federal Civilian employees, and therefore not eligible for FEDVIP, in active employment or retirement.
conditions: Note: The NAF agency option on the Payroll Schedule is only for Federal Civilian employees who have a NAF annuity.

units.heading: If a NAF employee becomes a Federal Civilian employee, they can either:
units.text:
If a NAF employee becomes a Federal Civilian employee, they can either:

- Switch to OPM retirement
If they choose to keep their NAF annuity, they will collect a NAF annuity instead of an OPM annuity when they retire.

units.heading: BENEFEDS Open Season/Post Open Season QA Appeal Process
units.text:
If it is believed that there may be a discrepancy with the way a call was scored, please follow the directions below.
**Please Note: A full audit of the QA in question will be performed by a Senior QA Coordinator. This may result in scoring changes in other sections of the form which may cause the score to be higher or lower than the original score. All scoring reconsiderations are final.
- The agent should first seek out assistance from their Admin, SME, or Floor Supervisor.
- The Admin, SME, or Floor Supervisor will listen to the call and review the QA for discrepancies.
- If the Admin, SME, or Floor Supervisor feels a QA review is needed, they will select "Request Review" and leave detailed comments in the next screen as to why the QA evaluation needs to be reviewed for reconsideration. The evaluation will then go to a Senior QA Coordinator for review.
- Within 2 business days, the Senior QA Coordinator will do a full review of the evaluation in question and will update the form (if needed). All reviews completed by Senior QA will be considered final.
Please Note: Review requests will not be considered if the above process isn’t followed as described. If an agent selects “Appeal” without proper approval, their request will be denied.

units.heading: OS/Current Plan Year Call
units.text:
Below are common talking points to use when speaking with callers
before or during Open Season.
Open Season Dates: The Monday of the second full week in November to the Monday of the second full week in December. (EX: 11/10/25 – 12/08/25)
Plan Year Dates: January 1st to the beginning of Open Season the same year. (EX: 01/01/2026 – 11/09/2026)
Reminder: Open Season Coverage Effective Dates
With Open Season approaching, you may be getting callers inquiring about their existing enrollment or even new callers asking about our programs. Nevertheless, we should always advise these callers that the changes, cancellations or enrollments will only be effective the following plan year.
Caller: I’m starting to prepare for open season and I’m looking to change my plan from the High Option to the Standard Option, do I need to call BENEFEDS, or can I go online to make the change myself?
Agent: You can either go online to make the change or call BENEFEDS Customer Service. Once you make the change it won’t be effective until 1-1-2026. As a reminder open season starts on November 10th, runs through December 8th.
Caller: I'm looking to cancel my coverage; I don't need it anymore.
Agent: Unfortunately, unless you have a QLE, (agents refer to ACED chart), you would not be able to cancel your plan until Open Season. At that time, if you do decide to cancel, your last day of coverage is 12/31/2025. As a reminder open season starts on November 10th and runs through December 8th.
You must provide the above information on changes, enrollments, or cancellations for Plan Year calls if a QLE does not exist. Continue to follow normal expectation guidelines during the Open Season.
conditions: Reminder: Open Season Coverage Effective Dates

units.heading: OS/Current Plan Year Call
units.text:

Agent: "Thank you for reaching out. I understand your interest in enrollment. As of December 8th, 2025, the open enrollment period has concluded for this year. However, individuals may still be eligible for enrollment or plan changes if they've experienced a Qualifying Life Event**. Have you experienced a qualifying life event?”
Caller: I forgot to make a change to my Dental plan. Do I still have time to do that?
Agent: "The open enrollment window closed on December 08, 2025. Don't worry though – you may still qualify for enrollment or plan adjustments if you've experienced a Qualifying Life Event**. Have you experienced a qualifying life event?”
**If the customer explains that their reason for missing Open Season enrollment was due to lack of phone and internet access, a serious illness or death in the immediate family, you can refer to the Belated Open Season Actions job aid to assist them.
Concluding the Call:
Agent: "Thank you for your time today. After this call, there is a brief survey. Your feedback is incredibly valuable to us, as it helps us improve our services. We appreciate your input and look forward to serving you in the future. Have a wonderful day! and thank you for calling Benefeds"

sources.title: Past Due and Retroactive Payments
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Past Due and Retroactive Payments.pptx

units.heading: Past Due and Retroactive Payments
units.text:
Past-due premiums are those premiums that should have been collected but were not for some reason. For example, perhaps a person went on leave without pay and we were unable to deduct from their pay, or we received an insufficient funds code. In these cases, we should have collected premiums but were not able to. These premiums are past-due and must be collected.
Retroactive premiums result from changes in effective dates or other such actions that result in back-dating effective dates.

units.heading: There are two methods for collecting past-due and retroactive premiums:
units.text:
There are two methods for collecting past-due and retroactive premiums:
- Double deductions
- Direct bill/Direct payments
Double deductions occur when we double the amount of the payroll or annuity deduction to collect past-due or retroactive premiums. We will double deduct until the owed amount is collected and never deduct more than double the normal deduction amount.
Some things we may double deduct for are:
- A belated action/enrollment has been submitted and the effective date is NOT January 1st
- Back-dated changes that result in retroactive premium increases (e.g., QLE to add a child after the event date)
- Single missed deductions
- Workers’ compensation cases with a past-due amount
- Reinstated accounts with a past-due amount
Direct bills to collect past-due or retroactive premiums will be sent to a participant if we are unable to double deduct from their payroll or annuity. Direct bills will be for the full past-due amount.
Some things we may send a direct bill for are:
- A belated action/enrollment has been submitted and the effective date is January 1st
- An S-code was received, which may indicate that the enrollee is either in special pay status or seasonal teacher/teacher’s recess status
- BENEFEDS received information that the enrollee is in leave without pay status
- Returned ABW items (e.g., if an enrollee’s ABW is returned by the bank, BENEFEDS would change them to direct billing)
- Workers’ compensation claim status that does not allow deductions from workers’ compensation benefits
- Insufficient funds code was received
- Missed deductions (no code)

units.heading: Past Due and Retroactive Payments
units.text:
Direct payments occur when a customer calls BENEFEDS to ask if they can send in a payment to pay the past-due or retroactive premiums on their account.
Factors to consider when sending in a direct payment:
- Customers can do this, but it is important to note that their normal method of payment is via pretax payroll deduction.
- By sending in a direct payment, they will not be realizing the tax savings if they paid their past-due or retroactive premiums by double deduction.
- If a customer wishes to send in a direct payment, they must include their user ID and/or member ID on the check and note which enrollment the payment applies to (dental, vision, or both).

units.heading: Calculating Past Due Premium
units.text:
Calculating Past Due Premium
In most cases, you should rely on the past-due amount located on the deduction info tab in Payroll UI.
If the past-due amount on the account seems incorrect, use the following simple formula to recalculate
the customer’s past-due amount.
- Determine the number of pay sequences that should have been paid YTD.
- Multiply by the premium deduction amount found on the deduction info tab.
- The result will be the amount that the enrollee should have paid YTD.
- # of pay sequences YTD x premium deduction amount = amount owed YTD
4. Determine how much was received YTD by looking at the cash flow tab.
5. Subtract #4 above from #3 above to determine the amount owed in past-due premium.
- amount owed YTD - amount received YTD = past-due amount

units.heading: To determine if there are back premiums owed for a previous year, please follow the below
units.text:
To determine if there are back premiums owed for a previous year, please follow the below steps:
- On the payments tab, select the year for which past-due premiums are still owed.
- Get the annual deduction amount and move to the cash flow tab.
- Select the year that you are researching back premium amounts for.
- View the top line under the column YTD.
- If the annual deduction amount and the YTD amount match, the enrollee has paid their full annual premium for that plan year.
- If the annual deduction amount and the YTD amount do not match, subtract the YTD amount from the annual deduction amount and this is how much the enrollee still owes for that plan year.

units.heading: Postdated ACH Payments
units.text:
When a customer is making an ACH payment with a CSR or on BENEFEDS.gov they have the option to select a payment date that is in the future; this is known as a postdated payment.
The below confirmations are provided to the customer after postdating an ACH payment.
- The customer will receive an email outlining the date the payment was requested and the date the payment will be processed. This will take place on the date the payment was requested AND the date the payment is processed. *NOTE- There will be no way to tell in CSS if a payment was postdated after the original request. The email is not captured in Image.
- There will also be an on-screen confirmation in CSS for the CSR processing the postdated payment or in the BENEFEDS.gov for the customer processing the postdated payment.

sources.title: Potential Dual Enrollment Scenarios
sources.file: SME Job Aids/Potential Dual Enrollment Scenarios.pptx

units.heading: Potential Dual Enrollment Scenarios
units.text:
Dual enrollment is when an individual is covered under more than one FEDVIP dental enrollment or more than one FEDVIP vision enrollment. FEDVIP regulations do not allow dual enrollments in a FEDVIP plan. In order to prevent a dual enrollment situation, we must follow the guidelines for combining the accounts of enrollees who are married.
Examples: Marriage
- If one person has Self Only and the other has a Self and Family and they get married, it results in a dual coverage situation since all eligible family members in a Self and Family plan are covered. To prevent the dual enrollment, we need to inactivate one account and perform a QLE-Acquiring an Eligible Family member on the other.
- If one person has Self Only and the other has Self Only and they simply want to combine into a Self Plus One but tell you after the 60-day timeframe for submitting the QLE-Acquiring an Eligible Family Member, they cannot combine until Open Season. They don’t have dual coverage; they each have Self Only.
- If one person is enrolled in dental and the other is enrolled in vision, they cannot combine accounts. In this case, each person could be added as a dependent on the other’s plan, with no inactivation.

units.heading: Agent Actions
units.text:
Agent Actions:
- You should have both primary enrollees on the phone for you to complete this request.
- The participant must be within the timeline for submitting an Acquiring a Family Member QLE.
- If both parties are on the phone, warm transfer to Research to complete the combination. If a Research Representative is not available, you must submit a Combine Accounts Primary AWD Work Item.
- If both parties are not available, then advise them to call back when both parties are available and remind them that there is a timeframe associated with this action.

units.heading: Example: Dependent
units.text:
Example: Dependent
- A dependent under a FEDVIP enrollment becomes a New Hire and wishes to enroll as the primary on their own plan.
Agent Actions:
- Ensure both the dependent and the current primary are on the line.
- Ensure the participant is within the timeframe for enrolling as a new hire.
- Transfer the call to Research. Research will remove the dependent and process a new enrollment for the dependent.

units.heading: Talking Points:
units.text:
Talking Points:
Customer asks if he can be enrolled with his spouse as a dependent and if his spouse can be enrolled with him as a dependent creating two FEDVIP enrollments with dual coverage:
“I’m sorry, the FEDVIP regulations do not allow dual enrollments. You will have to decide which spouse will be the primary enrollee and the other spouse can be listed as a dependent on that plan, or each spouse can have a Self Only enrollment.”
Customer would like to cancel their FEDVIP enrollment because they have just gotten married and would like to enroll in their new spouse’s coverage, which is also a FEDVIP plan (MUST be a FEDVIP plan):
“Congratulations on your marriage. I would be happy to assist you with this change. I do need to speak to your spouse to have this request processed. Also, I need to know the date of your marriage; it must be either in the next 31 days or in the past 60 days for this request to be processed.”

sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Prenoting USM New Retirees.pptx

units.heading: Prenoting USM New Retirees
units.text:
You may have received some calls from recent retirees who have completed their FEDVIP enrollment, inquiring as to why they are receiving ABW/DB offer, when they previously elected to have premiums deducted from their annuity.
- While waiting for confirmation on our pre-noting, if we receive a 2nd B code, this will automatically switch these enrollees to ABW, even though we may receive the first premium deduction from their annuity.
- This is due to the timing of the pre-noting and when the allotment finalizes.
- These error codes can be found in either the Billing and Payments tab in BUI, and in the transaction log.
- If the enrollee wants their premiums to come from their annuity, create an Agency Name Change AWD ticket.
Payments Tab
Transaction Log
Changing USM Retiree to ABW
We will allow USM retirees to switch having deductions taken from their annuity to their bank account. However, this is not our preference, and we should not offer to do this.
If the USM retiree requests to have premiums deducted from their bank account and not their retirement:
- Create an Agency Name Change AWD ticket.
- PAT will process this request and will switch the enrollee to ABW status.
- Advise the enrollee that once their request is processed, they will receive a letter/email advising of the change.
- Enrollees can go online to BENEFEDS.gov to add their banking information to their account.
- If they do not add their banking information, they may be switched to direct bill.
Note: All tickets will be processed in the order they’re received, so it is important for the enrollee to update their information online once they receive confirmation that the switch to ABW has been completed.

units.heading: Primary Enrollee vs Sponsor
units.text: Primary Enrollee vs Sponsor

units.heading: Primary Enrollee vs Sponsor
units.text: It is important to understand the difference between a primary enrollee and a sponsor when enrolling customers in the FEDVIP. Use the definitions below to communicate the difference between a primary enrollee and sponsor to customers.

units.heading: Primary Enrollee vs Sponsor
units.text: Who is considered the Primary Enrollee?

units.heading: Primary Enrollee vs Sponsor
units.text: The Federal employee, retiree or Survivor Annuitant enrolled in the FEDVIP. Primary enrollees can add eligible family members to their plans as dependents. Dependents are not eligible to enroll in the FEDVIP without the primary enrollee.

units.heading: Primary Enrollee vs Sponsor
units.text: Who is considered the Sponsor?

units.heading: Primary Enrollee vs Sponsor
units.text:
An enrollee who is eligible for TRICARE benefits because of their own military service and not the status of another person.
Retired Uniformed Service Member
A retired Uniformed Service Member is considered the sponsor and can enroll themselves and their family members in a FEDVIP dental and/or vision plan.
NOTE: Family members of a Retired USM who has one or more of the following dental exceptions are eligible to enroll in FEDVIP Dental only, without the Sponsor having to enroll:
- Sponsor is receiving VA Dental Services, or
- Has dental insurance from their employer that does not cover their family, or
- Unable to receive dental services due to a pre-existing condition.
Active Duty Uniformed Service Member
An active duty Uniformed Service Member is not eligible for the FEDVIP, but can “sponsor” his/her family. The eligible family member can enroll themselves and their family members in a FEDVIP vision plan. The eligible family member is considered the primary enrollee.

units.heading: Instructions on submitting a Primary Inactivation AWD Ticket:
units.text:

- Select Inactivation for Action Needed.
- Choose plan(s) requiring inactivation.
- Select Inactivation Reason.
- Enter Event Date.
- Enter AWD comments explaining the reason for inactivation and include all applicable details.

For directions on inactivating a FAD account due to divorce, see Enrollment or Inactivation Due to Divorce.
Customer Expectations: The account will be inactivated on the last day of the pay period following submission or the last day for which we receive premium.
- Do not provide specific inactivation dates until the inactivation has taken place because we may or may not receive additional premium.
Provide the customer with the following script:
"I have submitted a request on your behalf. Your ticket will be processed in the order in which it was received. Once processed, you will receive a confirmation letter and may check your online account to validate the changes.“
