units.heading: A Primary Reinstate Enrollment AWD ticket should be created for the following reasons:
units.text:
A Primary Reinstate Enrollment AWD ticket should be created for the following reasons:
- Address discrepancies.
- BENEFEDS communication errors.
- Enrollment inactivated due to:
- Reason code marked as "Exhausted."
- Incorrect ineligible, termination, or deceased code.
- Payment posted but still inactive for non-payment.
- Restoration of employment.
- Non-payment inactivation caused by:
- Retirement (incorrect No Deduction Reason Code).
- Agency transfer (incorrect No Deduction Reason Code).
- Incorrect agency on file (correct agency now provided).
- Incorrect employment status on file (correct status now provided)

units.heading: Steps to complete a Reinstate Enrollment ticket:
units.text:
Steps to complete a Reinstate Enrollment ticket:
- Before submitting ticket, ensure all account information in the CS system is updated
- Enter Member ID
- Select Plan(s) requiring change
- Enter New Agency/Sub Agency if wrong in CS system
- Select Reinstatement Reason
- Enter AWD comment with applicable detail and External POI

units.heading: Customer Expectations:
units.text:
Customer Expectations:
- Restoration of Employment/Annuity: Full payment is not required. Account reinstatement occurs within 3–5 business days, a Reinstatement Confirmation Letter (DV21) is issued, and past due premiums are collected via double deductions.
- When Payment is Required Before Reinstatement: A Past Due Reinstatement Letter (FDVPA04) is sent within 3–5 business days, requesting full payment in cases involving:
- Address discrepancies (exception below does not apply).
- BENEFEDS communication errors.
- Inactivation reason code = "Exhausted."
- Incorrect ineligible, termination, or deceased code.
- Payment posted but still inactive due to non-payment.
- Important Exception: If the member contacts BENEFEDS within 30 days of inactivation (e.g., inactivated 2/3, call before 3/3), no FDVPA04 letter is sent, and no direct payment is needed. BENEFEDS will reinstate the enrollment and collect past dues through double deductions.

units.heading: Processing ACH payments with an unauthorized third party:
units.text:
Processing ACH payments with an unauthorized third party:
ACH payment information may be provided by an unauthorized third party to:
- Make a payment
- Reinstate coverage
To provide ANY billing information to an unauthorized third party, you must first confirm that the intent of the call is to make an ACH payment. Otherwise, you must follow normal third-party guidelines for speaking to an unauthorized third party.

units.heading: Processing ACH payments with an unauthorized third party · You may discuss with the 3rd party the following
units.text:
You may discuss with the 3rd party the following:
- Paid-thru Date
- Future Paid-thru date
- Current Past due vs Bill amount (if there is a difference)
- If the account has termed for non-pay and reinstatement is offered.
- If reinstatement is not being offered, we would not discuss the termination with the 3rd party.
- In these cases, advise the 3rd party we are unable to take the payment at this time and that the primary account holder should call is back.
You may not speak about any other aspect of the account (such as enrollment details) with the third party.

units.heading: Processing ACH payments with an unauthorized third party · Important Considerations
units.text:
Important Considerations:
- Attempt to gather proper security information for the primary’s account with the third party.
- If there are no other transactions occurring during the call, and the 3rd party is only calling to make a payment or reinstate the account by making a payment, no security is required other than confirming the account holder’s name matches the account in the CSS ("May I have the bank account holder's name?“).
- BENEFEDS will only accept a payment from the unauthorized third party's account.
- The primary enrollee's banking information cannot be used in this instance, even if saved to the account.
- Do not save the 3rd parties bank information to the account.
- The ACH confirmation number may be provided to the unauthorized 3rd party.
- If the enrollee also has an outstanding balance(s) on another account (dental, vision, FLTCIP):
- You can explain that we administer the premium payment processing for FEDVIP & FLTCIP.
- You may provide information (premium amount due, due date, etc.) about those other outstanding balances to help keep the account(s) active.
conditions: Important Considerations:
Do not save the 3rd parties bank information to the account.

units.heading: Processing ACH payments with an unauthorized third party · If obtaining verbal authorization
units.text:
If obtaining verbal authorization:
- Request to speak with the primary enrollee.
- Verify security with the primary enrollee (three pieces).
- Banking information for the primary enrollee may be provided by the authorized individual.
- The primary enrollee at the time verbal authorization is obtained should subsequently authorize BENEFEDS to deduct premium from the enrollee's account.
- Please use the following script when obtaining verbal authorization:
- "Do you authorize the third party to discuss and make changes to your account, including providing banking information for the purpose of submitting a payment? And do you allow BENEFEDS to deduct the payment from your account?“
- If the primary says yes, you may now continue with the third party.

units.heading: QA Call Checks
units.text: Quality Assurance: Call Checks

units.heading: QA Call Checks
units.text: What Are Call Checks?

units.heading: QA Call Checks
units.text:
- Call checks are “spot checks” of calls to ensure quality standards are still being met, except there is no numerical
score or pass/fail attached. These reviews are for coaching and agent development purposes only.
- Call checks are meant to be supplemental listening, meaning they should only be done once official QA scoring
has been completed for the day.
- Call checks should provide a brief and high-level overview of how the agent handled the call. It is not a measure of whether or not they achieved each metric on the call check Form. (For example, feedback may include: “You
took all necessary steps to process the enrollment for the customer. Just be sure to offer the carrier contact info.
Keep up the great work!”)
- Call checks should have a friendly “FYI” tone when delivering the feedback.

units.heading: Call Check Process
units.text:
- Call checks should be completed using the OS Call Check Form in CXone. NOTE: This form is identical to the
BENEFEDS OS form, with the exception that there is no numerical score attached.
- Call checks should be processed through CXone just like official QA. Critical error behaviors that are identified, should follow the normal process and be emailed to the agent’s site admins/floor supervisors, and CC: BENEFEDSQACoordinators@fedpointusa.com
- There is no limit to how many call checks can be completed for an agent within a day, as there is no official scoring attached, and this is only supplemental listening.
- The exception to the above is critical error behaviors. When the first critical error is identified from a call check,
no further call checks should be completed for that agent for the rest of the day. This allows time for the Site OM and/or Floor Supervisor to address the issue with the agent and correct the behavior.

sources.title: Reasons Direct Bills are Sent
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Reasons Direct Bills are Sent.pptx

units.heading: Reasons Direct Bills are Sent
units.text:
There are three high-level reasons Direct Bills are generated for FEDVIP customers.
- Enrolled with a Direct Bill location/APO*:
- The APO is not setup to deduct and pass premiums (agencies/annuity offices with double asterisk).
- Agency Payroll Offices
- Civilian Marksmanship Program
- District of Columbia government
- District of Columbia Housing Authority
- U.S. Capitol Police (USCP)
- Annuity Offices
- District of Columbia - Office of Pay and Retirement Systems
- District of Columbia Judges
- District of Columbia Retirement Board
- NAF – Marine Corps Community Service
- NAF – Navy
- Navy Exchange Service Command
- Office of Thrift Supervision
- Survivor with Basic Employee Death Benefit
- USUHS – TIAA – CREF
- Enrolled with USM status that requires ABW
- Eligible for Retirement Pay (REP) if insufficient funds/allotments or paid by VA
- Gray Area Reservist (GAR)
- Eligible for Retirement Pay - Without Sponsor - Family of Retired USM (RPN)
- Family of Gray Area Reservist (FGR)
- Medal of Honor Recipient (MOH)
- USM Survivors (SRP, STR, SRR, SMO, SAC)
- Family of Active Duty (FAD)*
- National Guard/Reserve Member (TRS)*
- Un-remarried Former Spouse (UFS)
- Eligible as Own Sponsor (OES)
- *In these instances, enrollees must set up ABW when they enroll. They can then revoke their ABW authorization and be sent direct bills instead.
- APO unable to deduct
- The enrollee has insufficient funds - In these instances we receive an I-code on the payment file.
- The enrollee is on leave without pay - In these instances we receive an L-code, and the APO sends $0.00 or null on the payment file.
- The enrollee is on leave without pay from their Federal Civilian position due to Active-Duty orders.
- The enrollee retired and their annuity has not been adjudicated yet - In these instances we receive an S-code.
- Analysts manually change someone to Direct Bill based on other codes or no deduction reasons.
- Enrollment flagged with Belated Past Due
- Enrollee is paying FEDVIP premiums pre-tax due to a belated enrollment.

units.heading: Receiving a Transferred Call
units.text:
Seasonal/Level 1 Representatives may transfer customers to Senior Representatives to ensure efficient handling of complex issues and quick resolutions.
Handling the Escalated Call:
- Check the Transfer Notes in CXone for:
- The full name of the transferring Representative.
- Member ID (if not included in Case Information).
- A brief description of the issue.
- Answer the call with the following greeting:
- “Hello, my name is [Your Name]. I see that you were transferred to me, so I do have your account up. How can I help you today?”
- Complete the call with the customer.
Verifying Security Information:
- Assume security information was confirmed by the transferring Representative.
- Confirm the caller's name matches the account information provided.
- For third-party callers:
- Ensure verbal authorization from the enrollee was noted by the Seasonal/Level 1 Representative.
- Confirm the third-party caller’s name matches the information noted in the BENEFEDS CSS.
- Complete the call with the customer.

sources.title: Refund Request Premium AWD Ticket
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Refund Request Premium AWD Ticket.pptx

units.heading: Premium Refund Request AWD Ticket
units.text:
When to Submit a Refund Request AWD Ticket
Use this ticket only if any of the following are true:
- The enrollee directly requests a refund.
- Credit balance is greater than 3X the Annual Deduction Amount.
- Any part of the credit balance is tied to a plan year more than 2 years prior to the current plan year.
- There is an overpayment on a deceased account.
Payment-Type Routing (What Happens to the Refund)
- Pre-tax (Payroll): Refunds routed back to Payroll as after-tax refunds.
- Post-tax (Annuity): Refunds issued by FedPoint.
- Post-tax (ACH/Direct): Refunds sent by check unless specified otherwise.
- Post-tax (ABW): Refunds sent to the originating bank account (many ABW credits are returned to the bank).
- Inactive accounts (due to death): Refunds sent to the estate; alternate payees must submit an Alternate Payee Form for reissued checks.

units.heading: Premium Refund Request AWD Ticket
units.text:
Steps to complete a Refund Request ticket:
- Enter Member ID
- Select Plan(s) requiring change
- Enter External POI, Next Pay Period Start Date
- Select Yes or No for Post Tax Payment
- Enter AWD comment with all applicable details
Customer Expectations:
- 10-day hold for checks, ACH payments, and ABW payments.
- Refunds, once processed, are mailed within 10-12 business days and received within 15 business days.
- Payroll/annuity refunds: No hold; 1 day to process for credit balances, 3 days for refund requests.
- If no refund/credit is due or a callback is requested, Research contacts the customer within 3 business days.

sources.title: Reinstatement for Non Pay
sources.file: Senior Rep Job Aids/Reinstatement for Non Pay.pptx

units.heading: Reinstatement for Non Pay
units.text: Reinstatement For Non-Pay Requests

units.heading: Background:
units.text:
Background:
Uniformed Service Members (USM) and Federal Civilian (FEDCIV) Enrollees who are in an active pay status have the option of being reinstated within 30 days from the termination date under the following circumstances:

units.heading: Reinstatement for Non Pay
units.text: Non-Pay Inactivation (ALL): If we receive payment within 5 days of inactivation PAT will automatically reinstate.

units.heading: Reinstatement for Non Pay
units.text: Non-Pay Inactivation (USM): Upon termination a DV82 letter is generated providing amount needed to be received within 30 days in order to reinstate.

units.heading: Reinstatement for Non Pay
units.text:
Non-Pay (FEDCIV): Upon termination a DV35 letter is generated providing amount needed to be received within 30 days in order to reinstate.
- Members who were inactivated for non-pay and are receiving pay from Worker’s Compensation can only be reinstated if their claim is FEDVIP eligible.
- To address this scenario, submit a Reinstatement AWD ticket and provide their Worker’s Compensation claim number in the ticket.
- We will send direct bills if there are not enough funds and they will need to pay their bills to maintain their coverage.
- Once a reinstatement ticket is submitted, PAT will reach out to Worker’s Comp to verify.
- If we determine their claim is FEDVIP eligible, the account will be reinstated.
- If their claim is not FEDVIP eligible, the account won’t be reinstated.
- You will find statuses for both “FEDVIP Eligible” and “Non-FEDVIP Eligible” in the ticket as well as the account comments.
The above rules apply for past-due premiums.
- If it has been less than 31 days for this request, we will automatically reinstate the account.
- If it surpassed 31 days, a Past Due Reinstatement Letter (PDRL) will be mailed out requesting the past due premiums prior to reinstatement.
Note: Reinstatement is within 3 days, unless there has been a reversal in the last 6 months. If there has been a reversal, we will hold the reinstatement for 10 business days to ensure the payment is good before reinstating.
conditions: Note: Reinstatement is within 3 days, unless there has been a reversal in the last 6 months. If there has been a reversal, we will hold the reinstatement for 10 business days to ensure the payment is good before reinstating.

units.heading: Reinstatement for Non Pay
units.text:
Non-Pay (FEDCIV on LWOP): PAT will not reinstate outside the 5-day grace period which allows for delays in mailing/processing time. If an enrollee in this category has an incorrect mailing address on file an AWD Reinstatement ticket may be submitted after the mailing address has been updated in the CS System.
- If the account is inactive, the overnight address cannot be offered as an option to reinstate. The post mark date of the payment must be prior to the date of the inactivation.
- The 30-day timeframe for submission of payment for reinstatement on the (DV35) only applies if they are in active pay status receiving their pay from the APO.
- Those who are in inactive pay status must wait until they return to work to re-enroll.
- Note: If the account inactivated for non-payment while on LWOP, they are ineligible for reinstatement regardless of their current pay status. They must re-enroll within 60 days of returning to a paid status (The only exception would be if the customer had an invalid address).
If member inactivates for non-pay and enrolled in both dental and vision, they DO NOT have to pay on both programs, they can make payment on either or.
If a customer was inactivated during Open Season and they are calling to reinstate after Open Season ends, PAT will not reinstate because they had the opportunity to address this during Open Season.
conditions: Note: If the account inactivated for non-payment while on LWOP, they are ineligible for reinstatement regardless of their current pay status. They must re-enroll within 60 days of returning to a paid status (The only exception would be if the customer had an invalid address).

units.heading: Option to Submit Payment in the BENEFEDS CSS:
units.text:
Option to Submit Payment in the BENEFEDS CSS:
- Reinstatement is based on an enrollee’s employment status at the time of inactivation.
- If the APO is not sending L codes when the account termed for non-pay, the ACH reinstatement option will be provided.
- Customers may make the reinstatement payment, and they will be reinstated if payment is received by the due date regardless of their current employment status.
Agent Actions:
- If the option to make and ACH payment exists and the customer is calling to pay, process the payment.
- You do not need to discuss their LWOP status (if applicable) with them in these instances.
Talking Points:
Customer calls stating they mailed their payment but just received a letter indicating they’ve been inactivated:
“If you mailed in the amount requested on your termination letter prior to the due date stated on that notice, and we received the payment in time, we’ll reinstate your account.”
Customer asks if they can overnight a premium payment (prior to the inactivation date) to avoid being inactivated:
“Yes, you'll have to use the US Postal Service's Express Mail service and send it to BENEFEDS-FEDVIP P.O Box 414095 Boston, MA 02241-4095. Make checks payable to FEDVIP and include your Member ID and whether it is for Vision or Dental.”
Customer Reinstatement:
- If the customer’s account was terminated due to non-payment, you will be redirected to the page as shown below when attempting to enroll.
- Customers can make a payment and bring their account due to continue with a regular enrollment.
- CS Agents will have ability to continue with the enrollment without a customer payment, but agents must inform the customer that the enrollment will be considered prospective.
- Both options will continue to the normal process flow of bill payment or enrollment, which has not changed with this update.

units.heading: Notes:
units.text:
Notes:
- This is mirrored on the Enrollee Portal, but customers do not have the Continue with Enrollment option.
- The customer will be required to make a payment for the account to be reinstated.

sources.title: Reporting Suspected Fraud
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Reporting Suspected Fraud.pptx

units.heading: Did You Know?
units.text:
Did You Know?
FedPoint staff have multiple channels available to them for reporting possible fraud.
- Contact Manager/Team Lead or Human Resources
- Contact Compliance
- Employee Ethics, Conduct, Fraud Reporting Form, located on The Hub
- BENEFEDS Fraud Reporting Hotline 1-603-433-3815
When you suspect fraud, or a customer has contacted BENEFEDS to report potential fraud and does not wish to call the hotline themselves, gather relevant information and report to the BENEFEDS fraud hotline at 1-603-433-3815.

units.heading: Did You Know? · What Information Will You Need To Gather?
units.text:
What Information Will You Need To Gather?
- A description of the alleged impropriety.
- Relevant and specific details of the situation, including the identity of the person or entity alleged to have engaged in wrongdoing and the BENEFEDS.gov account in question.
- The date of the alleged wrongdoing and how you or the customer is aware of the alleged impropriety.
- Remember that the customer may want to remain anonymous.

units.heading: Did You Know? · What Does Possible Fraud Look Like?
units.text:
What Does Possible Fraud Look Like?
- Someone misrepresenting themselves or their dependents as eligible for coverage.
- A caller may tell you that they suspect someone of misrepresentation.
How Will You Know?
You will see indicators of suspicious activity, potential fraud and/or misrepresentation. These indicators are unusual circumstances, that vary from normal activity. These could look like:
- Birthdates of dependents that are close in age. For example, 4 months apart.
- Large age gap between spouses. For example, possibly enrolled parent instead of spouse.
- Being aggressive or combative, yelling, making demands.
- FedPoint is unable to validate employment, but customer keeps calling in to obtain coverage.
Remember, these are only indicators, and do not necessarily mean that fraud has been committed. It does mean that the issue should be referred for further review.

units.heading: Did You Know? · Whistleblower Protection Information
units.text:
Whistleblower Protection Information
- We recognize that whistleblowers help root out fraud, waste, and abuse, and, as such, help preserve the integrity of the programs on the BENEFEDS platform.
- Federal laws strongly encourage Federal employees, as well as employees of Federal contractors, to disclose wrongdoing.
- Whistleblowers are critical to combatting waste, fraud, and abuse, and Federal laws protect whistleblowers from retaliation of any kind.

units.heading: Suspicious Toll-Free Phone Numbers
units.text:
Suspicious Toll-Free Phone Numbers
We have received reports of toll-free numbers that closely mimic our official contact number, differing by just one digit. If a caller mentions they were connected to a different company while trying to reach us, please follow the instructions provided below.
When a caller states they reached another company when trying to contact us, do the following:
- Verify the number that they were attempting to call.
- Ask the caller to look at the call history on their phone to provide the phone number they dialed.
- Provide this website to the caller to report the fraudulent activity: ReportFraud.ftc.gov

units.heading: Suspicious Toll-Free Phone Numbers · Inform the Caller
units.text:
Inform the Caller:
- “We are aware that there are phone numbers that closely resemble ours.”
- “To protect your personal information, only use the official telephone numbers published within the Contact Us section of our website - https://benefeds.gov/contact.”
- “If you believe you may have disclosed your credit card details, banking information or any other sensitive personal information to a fraudulent individual you spoke to or in response to an automated prompt:
- Freeze your credit by contacting the three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion) to prevent scammers from opening accounts in your name.
- Monitor your accounts by keeping a close eye on your bank accounts and credit card statements for unauthorized charges.
- Report the fraud by filing a report with the Federal Trade Commission.”

units.heading: Suspicious Toll-Free Phone Numbers · Best Practices to Provide the Caller
units.text:
Best Practices to Provide the Caller:
- Verify the prefix and whether the number you wish to call requires 800, 866, 877, or 888.
- Verify the numbers you have typed on your phone or device.
- Verify the correct number to call in advance by visiting the company's website to look up account details rather than relying on search engine results for contact telephone numbers.
- Never give sensitive details to an automated prompt. Genuine customer service lines will not demand your full Social Security number or credit card information right away via an unsolicited automated menu just to "verify a reward."
conditions: Never give sensitive details to an automated prompt. Genuine customer service lines will not demand your full Social Security number or credit card information right away via an unsolicited automated menu just to "verify a reward."

units.heading: Important daily activities to keep in mind when managing agent schedules:

Important daily activities to keep in mind when managing agent schedules:
- Schedules are coded for attendance deviations greater than 1 minute (+1).
- Unplanned Time Off is used when an agent is absent or if there is time during the shift where an agent logs off for a period of time.
- Agents are considered late if not available to take calls at scheduled start time and are not experiencing system issues.
- Leave Early is used when an agent is unable to continue their scheduled shift time.
- System Down is used for agents who cannot perform scheduled tasks due to system issues.
- Previous workday schedule adjustments are due by 10:30 AM EST of the following business day.
- All agent time off is considered unplanned.
- Agents are allowed 10 minutes of setup time prior to the scheduled start of their shift.
- Schedule updates should be made in real-time whenever possible to allow for accurate WFM planning.
- Lunch/break times should never be adjusted at the agent’s request or to modify adherence.
- If an agent has an 8 hour or longer shift (8.5 or more with a lunch) and they log in to Available status 1-14 minutes after their scheduled start time, update their schedule with the Late code. Do not remove their first break.

sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Security Verification Direct Hit.pptx

units.heading: Security Verification: Direct Hit
units.text:
During IVR authentication, when users enter their SSN and Date of Birth, the system checks to see if they are calling from the phone number on their account. If the phone numbers match, the system will determine the call to be fully authenticated.
If the caller does not authenticate in the IVR with SSN and Date of Birth, but still calls from the number on their account, the system will determine the call to be not authenticated. However, we may use the phone number matching the number on the account as a piece of security.
This piece of approved security information is known as a Direct Hit.

units.heading: Security Verification: Direct Hit
units.text:
How does it work?
In the Agent panel, the number the customer is calling from will be displayed. If this number matches the number located on the customer’s profile, it is considered a Direct Hit and will satisfy one piece of security.
- Identify the number the customer is calling from. In this example, the caller’s phone number is (978) 476-9239.
- After locating the caller’s profile in the BENEFEDS Customer Service System, determine if the phone number on the profile matches the caller’s phone number.

units.heading: Security Verification: Direct Hit
units.text:
IMPORTANT:
You are not able to ask the customer for their phone number as a piece of approved security information.
*Actions to be taken on an account require three pieces of security each time the account is accessed. A Direct Hit may count as one piece of security.
conditions: IMPORTANT:

units.heading: Security Verification: Direct Hit
units.text:
- 3. Verbalize the direct hit by reading the following script:.
“Thank you, Mr./Ms. ____ , I can see the number you are calling from today is listed on your account, I can use that as an additional piece of security to authenticate your account.”

sources.title: Security Verification
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Security Verification.pptx

units.heading: Security Verification
units.text: Representatives are expected to identify the caller by confirming their full name. Ask “May I have your full name?”. If the caller identifies as primary and you suspect they are a third party, you must ask a second time “May I have your full name please?”. If the caller again identifies as the primary enrollee, you may continue assisting the caller. Once their identity is determined, verify if they have authenticated in the IVR and to what level of authentication. There are three levels of authentication displayed when a call is received.

units.heading: Security Verification
units.text:
This displays when the customer has not authenticated through the IVR. You must verify a minimum of two (2) pieces of approved security for the following actions:
- Discuss account details
- Close out Deceased’s affairs
- Mail out Plan/Rates, ADI forms, and Revoke ABW forms
- All ACH Payments
A third piece of approved security will be required to process a transaction. (See the ‘Transaction list’ for examples) Direct hits must be verbally acknowledged.
Calls from outside entities (Carriers, Veteran’s Service Officers, Agency Benefits Officers, Provider’s Office) must be treated as not authenticated, even if verified in the IVR.
NOTE: L1 agents must gather 3 pieces of security before transferring to a SR agent.
conditions: NOTE: L1 agents must gather 3 pieces of security before transferring to a SR agent.

units.heading: Fully
units.text:

units.heading: Slack Best Practices
units.text: Slack serves as a floor support forum during production offering agents with real-time communication with SMEs, TLs, and Floor Support. Agents can quickly ask questions and receive support, reducing downtime and enhancing efficiency.

units.heading: Slack Best Practices
units.text:
- There will be certain channels available to you in Slack. You can click on them to move from channel to channel.
- The Emoji and Reactions menu allow you to reply to a question as its own thread by selecting the comment bubble (this is the best practice). You can also react with different emojis on posts.
- This is where you will post your question in the forum channel.
- Clicking the profile icon will allow you to update your status, manage notifications, update profile information, and choose or update Preferences.
- Any private conversations you have will show on the left side menu.

units.heading: Best Practices
units.text:
Best Practices
- Stay Professional: Maintain a professional tone, especially in urgent situations.
- Be Concise: Keep your messages brief and to the point for quicker responses, be sure to always reply to a thread when having a conversation.
- Use Emojis Sparingly: They can add a friendly touch, but you should not use emojis unprofessionally.

sources.title: Sponsor Roles in the FEDVIP
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Sponsor Roles in the FEDVIP.pptx

units.heading: Sponsor Roles in the FEDVIP
units.text:
The sponsor is the Uniformed Service Member (USM) who is eligible for TRICARE benefits, which allows enrollment in the FEDVIP for themselves and eligible family members. Eligibility for dental, vision, or both types of coverage depends on the USM’s status.
- Retired USM: May enroll as the sponsor and primary account holder based on their own military service. Most retirees are eligible for dental coverage, and for vision coverage if enrolled in a TRICARE health plan.
- Active Duty USM: Not eligible for FEDVIP dental or vision coverage but may sponsor eligible family members. A spouse, child, or dependent of an active duty USM (serving full-time for over 30 days) may enroll in FEDVIP vision if covered by a TRICARE health plan. In this case, the family member becomes the primary account holder and can add other eligible dependents.
- Account Access: A USM sponsor has the same access level as an approved third party, including the ability to discuss coverage and billing. However, they cannot make enrollment changes. The only billing change a sponsor may request is the removal of their payroll authorization.
- Minor Children: A biological parent listed as the primary does not require third-party documentation to discuss and manage the account. They may make all changes and transactions on behalf of the minor child.

sources.title: Survivor Annuitant Lump Sum vs Coupon Program
sources.file: L1 Job Aids/Survivor Annuitant Lump Sum vs Coupon Program.pptx

slides.title: Survivor Annuitant Lump Sum vs Coupon

units.heading: Survivor Annuitant Lump Sum vs Coupon
units.text:
What are Lump Sum Survivor Annuitants?
A survivor annuitant is generally an eligible dependent (spouse, child, or certain other dependents) of a federal employee, federal annuitant, or USM sponsor who has passed away. Normally, these survivors receive a continuing monthly survivor annuity.
However, a lump sum survivor annuitant refers to cases where the survivor is connected to a situation involving a lump sum death benefit, rather than ongoing annuity payments.
- Survivors annuitants are not eligible if they are not receiving a monthly annuity with the following exception:
EXCEPTION:
- Survivors of a Federal employee who received a lump sum one-time death benefit (BEDB) are eligible because the Federal Employee may not have had the opportunity to set up a survivor annuity. Opposed to an Annuitant (already retired) who passed and did not set up a survivor package for dependents, in which this group is not eligible for FEDVIP.
The below information clarifies the 'Lump Sum or Coupon Program' question in the Customer Service System. The question appears after selecting a spouse and answering “yes” to whether the beneficiary has received a Survivor Basic Employee Death Benefit. The descriptions below will help in selecting the correct payment setup for new survivor annuitant accounts.
Lump Sum Option:
A one-time payment received by the beneficiary. Deductions for FEDVIP premiums cannot be taken directly from this amount, so beneficiaries are set up with Automatic Bank Withdrawal (ABW) or direct billing for premium payments immediately.
Coupon Program:
The lump sum is divided into 36 monthly payments over three years. During this period, FEDVIP premiums can be deducted directly from these payments. After the three-year term, BENEFEDS coordinates with OPM to transition the beneficiary to ABW or direct billing for future payments.

units.heading: System Down Checklist for Admins and SMEs
units.text: This resource is to be used when troubleshooting issues that require agents to go into System Down status in CXone.

units.heading: System Down Checklist for Admins and SMEs
units.text:
Prior to following the checklist below for login issues, remind agents to refer to their credential emails to ensure they are using the correct login information.
CXone Issues:
- Agent can’t receive calls
- Confirm agents have connected to the Agent Leg in CXone (refused status).
- If the agent’s headset is muted or permissions are not allowed, the system may not connect.
- Agent cannot log in and is not receiving a password reset.
- Check that the agent hasn’t saved a redirect URL as a favorite (have them access CXone from their production folder).
- Confirm they are using the correct URL: fedpoint.my.niceincontact.com
- System is timing out (usually associated with being in meetings or scheduled trainings).
- Agents should have CXone Agent open with the User Hub closed.

units.heading: BENEFEDS CS System Issues
units.text:
BENEFEDS CS System Issues:
- Agent can’t log into BENEFEDS CS System.
- Confirm they are connected to the VPN.
- Confirm they are using the correct URL: https://www.benefedservice.com/login
- They should be using the production link to BENEFEDS CSS above after passing their final certification and preparing to take calls.
- Often, agents will mistakenly use the training region. Be sure they have closed out of all tabs with the training region URL: https://trn.benefedservice.com/login. Look for “trn” at the beginning of the training URL.
- Confirm if the agent is using the correct credentials.
- If unable to login, perform a password rest.
- If locked out, perform a password reset.

units.heading: NICE Webstation Issues
units.text:
NICE Webstation Issues:
- Agent cannot log into Webstation.
- Confirm they are using the correct username (full email address).
- Perform a password reset using the “Forgot Your Password?” option.
Microsoft Teams Issues:
- Agent cannot access MS Teams.
- Check if the agent is using their vendor Teams login credentials (FedPoint does not supply a separate login for Teams.)
LEARN Issues:
- Agent cannot log into LEARN.
- Confirm the agent is using their email address as their username.
- Use the password rest option on LEARN to reset the password.
- Reach out to the training team, trainingteam@fedpointusa.com, for further assistance.
SharePoint Online Issue (Seasonal QA only):
- Agent cannot log into SharePoint Online.
- Verify they are using the same login for SharePoint Online as they are for Microsoft Teams.

units.heading: Federal Civilians / USPS employees:
units.text:
Federal Civilians / USPS employees:
- When a Federal Civilian or USPS employee separates without retiring, their agency payroll office (APO) will send BENEFEDS a termination code.
- The enrollee will remain eligible and active until a termination code is received.
- Coverage will continue as long as premium payments are made.
- Enrollees may continue to pay premiums through the pay period in which we receive the termination code.
- Once the termination code is received, the customer is no longer eligible, and PAT will inactivate the enrollment effective the most recent paid‑through date.
- PAT is unable to inactivate their enrollment until the termination code is received.
If the enrollee is a Federal Civilian or USPS employee and states they have terminated, the enrollee must contact their HR or HR services to process them out.
- DO NOT submit an inactivation ticket.
Exception: If the enrollee is in a direct bill location or on ABW due to intermittent payments, you must submit a Primary - Inactivation ticket if the enrollee says they have terminated.
- PAT will confirm and then inactivate.
conditions: DO NOT submit an inactivation ticket.

units.heading: USMs:
units.text:
USMs:
- If the enrollee is Army, Navy, Air Force, on Active Duty, Reserves, or Guard and paying through DFAS payroll, DFAS will send BENEFEDS a separation code and PAT will inactivate their account.
- If the enrollee is Army, Navy, Air Force, on Active Duty, Reserves, or Guard and on DB/ABW, and is calling to state they have separated without retirement, submit a Primary – Inactivation ticket.
- PAT will confirm and then inactivate.

units.heading: Talking Points:
units.text:
Talking Points:
Q: I received a direct bill in the mail, but I left federal service a while ago. Why am I still being billed?
A: You’re receiving a direct bill because your agency payroll office has not yet sent BENEFEDS a separation notice. We will continue to direct bill you and you may remit payment to maintain coverage until we receive a separation code. Once we receive notice of your separation, BENEFEDS will inactivate your account.
Q: What happens if I don’t pay the direct bill?
A: If you don’t pay your direct bills, BENEFEDS has a termination for non-pay process. If the first direct bill is not paid, the next direct bill will include a termination warning. If we do not receive a termination code or payment by the due date of the bill, the account will term for non-pay effective the most recent payment.
Q: If my account terms for non-pay, will I be reported to a collection agency?
A: No, BENEFEDS will inactivate based on your most recent paid through date and all past due amounts will be removed from your account.

- Ask if he/she gives the 3rd party authorization to discuss and make changes to the account for this call only.

- You may not indicate whether a FEDVIP, FSAFEDS, or FLTCIP enrollment exists.
- EXCEPTION: If the 3rd party is a covered dependent under the FEDVIP enrollment, you may provide the name of the insurance carrier they are enrolled with, along with the carrier's contact information. You may not provide any other details about the enrollment (e.g., other covered dependents, premium information, etc.).
- Advise the caller about the functions of an Authorization for Disclosure of Information Form as well as that of a Power of Attorney. This way, the third party can take action to provide such documentation to BENEFEDS. Be clear about what each allows a BENEFEDS representative to do (discuss or take action) with a third party.
- L1 Agents will guide the caller to BENEFEDS.gov to locate the ADI form. If the customer requests the form mailed to them a Correspondence AWD ticket must be created by a Senior Rep.

units.heading: HOW TO SEND BENEFEDS A POA OR ADI
units.text:
HOW TO SEND BENEFEDS A POA OR ADI
U.S. Postal Service Address:
BENEFEDS
Attn: Compliance Department
P.O. Box 797 Greenland, NH 03840
Fax: 1-833-889-3666
E-Mail: compliancecs@benefeds.gov., Attn: Compliance Department
Note 1: The preferred type of POA is either a Durable Finance for Insurance & Banking, or a Finance for Insurance & Banking POA. Either of those may allow a 3rd party to discuss and make changes to a primary’s enrollment.
Note 2: BENEFEDS will accept legal documents in languages other than English. If a translated version is available (preferably certified, but not required), this needs to be included with the submission.
Note 3: Healthcare POAs or Medical POAs generally do not allow changes and may not even allow discussion. Guardianship (or conservatorship) Papers allow a legal guardian to discuss and make changes to an account.
Timeframe for Approval of Documentation
Once a legal document is received by Compliance, it will be reviewed for accuracy. Once approved the documentation should be visible in the CS System within 3-5 business days of receipt by Compliance.
If a customer is calling stating they sent in documentation and it is not yet viewable, you can contact your Team Lead who can then contact Compliance for a status check on the documentation.

units.heading: Transfer Notes
units.text: Transfer notes must be included for all internal cold transfers to allow receiving agents to understand the full situation. Below are some expectations and common examples of transfer notes. For directions on how to leave transfer notes, see CXone Softphone: Cold Transfer (Internal).

units.heading: Transfer Notes:
units.text:
Transfer Notes:
Transferring internally requires you to leave transfer notes with the following:
- Your First and Last Name (viewed internally, no customer will see this).
- Security Verification (3X, 3X Verified, Verbal auth provided for John Doe, etc.)
- Member ID (if not authenticated in the IVR).
- A brief reason for the transfer.
General Info:
- For all transfers, agents are required to put their first and last name so that the receiving agent can provide them Kudos & feedback during Open Season. Your full name will never be provided to customers.
- All cold internal transfer MUST include acknowledgment of security verification (3X, 3X Verified, Verbal auth provided for John Doe, etc.).
- This is to ensure security is gathered prior to transferring.
- Senior reps expect security to be verified when receiving a transfer, so be sure to verify appropriately.
- If authenticated via the IVR:
- Full Authentication does not require you to provide a member ID but include that security was gather.
- Partial Authentication requires you to obtain one more piece of security (cannot be SSN or DOB), but you do not need to provide the Member ID.
- No Authentication requires you to obtain 3 pieces of security AND include the Member ID in the transfer notes.
Examples:
“Cam Parsons, Full authentication via IVR, calling to enroll into Dental Plan this year.”
“Eva Miller, 3X verbal authorization obtained for John Smith from Primary, calling to change current Vision plan.”
“Jeremy Cook, 3X verified, calling to inform of agency change.”
“Emily Kulik, 3X verified, calling to ask about direct bills received.”

sources.file: L1 Job Aids/USM Dependents Process for Reactivation.pptx

units.heading: USM Students:
units.text:
USM Students:
For a full-time student to be reactivated (retroactive coverage) from an enrollment they dropped from (aged off), the following must apply:
- The account must have been a continuous Uniformed Service Member (USM) account with no status change from Civilian to USM.
- The drop of the dependent must have been within 60 days of the request to reactivate.
- If the request is outside the 60 days, the account must be a Self and Family enrollment before and after the drop of the dependent. (Except in cases where the address is invalid. See Address Exceptions below.)
- Action is required to reactivate a dependent if they have aged off.

units.heading: USM Students · To re-activate the dependent
units.text:
To re-activate the dependent:
- Agents should update the relationship status to full-time student.
- Reach out to your TL/Floor Support to reactivate the dependent.
- If no one is available to reactivate the dependent, submit a dependent ticket.
- If there is an increase in enrollment type, confirm this and the premium change with the customer before requesting reactivation.
Note: If a dependent was dropped from a USM enrollment due to turning 21 while a student, the dependent should be re-activated to ensure seamless coverage. They should not be added as a dependent in the CS System.
conditions: Note: If a dependent was dropped from a USM enrollment due to turning 21 while a student, the dependent should be re-activated to ensure seamless coverage. They should not be added as a dependent in the CS System.

units.heading: USM Students · Address Exception
units.text:
Address Exception:
If the Primary address was incorrect and they did not receive the aging off letter (DV18) we can reactivate.
- The address must be updated after the date listed on the letter for the dependent to be reactivated.
- Is the Transaction date of the dependent removal before the first day of the most recent Federal Benefits Open Season?
- If no, continue with the process of reactivating the dependent using the considerations and guidelines outlined in this resource.
- If yes, was the reactivation requested between the first day of the Open Season (next OS after inactivation) and December 31st (of that same year)?
- If no, the dependent may not be reactivated.
- If yes, continue with the process of reactivating the dependent using the considerations and guidelines outlined in this resource.

units.heading: Sponsors may only request inactivation without consent from the primary if:
units.text:
Sponsors may only request inactivation without consent from the primary if:
- The sponsor is enrolling due to retirement
- The Primary is a minor child
- The sponsor submits a divorce decree*
*Divorce Decree: The CS agent must first attempt to contact the primary. If unable to make contact, direct the sponsor to send the divorce decree. They must submit a divorce decree as proof that the divorce took place:
- Email to: Benefedsadministration@benefeds.gov
- Mail to: BENEFEDS-FEDVIP PO Box 797, Greenland, NH 03840-0797
- Advise the sponsor that it may take 3-5 business days for processing and to call back to complete the inactivation.
In all other scenarios, the primary will need to consent to the inactivation. If the sponsor wishes to continue coverage under a different federal affiliation, these scenarios may require you to transfer to Research.
For an inactivation due to divorce, we will use the divorce date regardless of dependents. Inactivation will be retro to the date of the divorce. Exception: If the primary was never eligible due to the Divorce occurring prior to the enrollment effective date. If the primary was never eligible, the inactivation will be prospective.

units.heading: Sponsors may only request inactivation without consent from  · Agent Actions
units.text:
Agent Actions:
- Gather the date of divorce.
- Determine if the customer (spouse) qualifies for FEDVIP under the 20/20/20 or 20/20/15 rule or another status:
- Are you an eligible Federal Civilian Employee, or eligible under another applicable federal status?
- If they qualify for the FEDVIP under another status, we can change their affiliation appropriately.
- Have you been married to the military member for at least 20 years at the time of the divorce, dissolution or annulment?
- Did the military member perform at least 20 years of service that is creditable in determining eligibility for retired pay (the member does not have to be retired from active duty)?
- Have you been married to the member during at least 20 years of the member's retirement-creditable service?
- Do they qualify as eligible for FEDVIP?
- If YES, and there were no dependents during the period of coverage between the divorce date and today's date:
- Update the customer's affiliation
- The customer will retain vision under the affiliation of Unmarried Former Spouse. If they are eligible under another affiliation, i.e., Retired Uniformed Service Member or Federal Employee, they can update their status to obtain dental through a QLE or Open Season.
- If YES, and there were dependents (current or aged off) between the divorce date and today's date:
- Advise we will enroll the dependents on their own plan retroactively to the date of divorce
- Advise this will result in a past due amount (Research will explain this further)
- Warm transfer the caller to Research and relay the details of the call to them
- If NO, and there were no dependents during the period of coverage between the divorce date and today's date:
- Submit an Inactivation ticket. The account will be inactivated retro to the event date (unless the divorce was prior to enrollment, then inactivated prospective)
- Refunds will be sent if applicable
- If NO, and there were dependents (current or aged off) between the divorce date and today's date:
- Submit an Inactivation ticket. The account will be inactivated retro to the event date (unless the divorce was prior to enrollment, then inactivated prospective)
- Refunds will be sent if applicable
- Advise we will enroll the dependents on their own plan retroactively to the date of divorce
- Advise this will result in a past due amount (Research will explain this further)
- Warm transfer the caller to Research and relay the details of the call to them

units.heading: Understanding the Direct Bill Process
units.text:
This process outlines how the Direct Bill, Termination Warning, and Inactivation process is executed for a Federal Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) employee as an example (see Page 2 for illustration of the below process).
Direct Bill Process Steps:
- This only begins once the account has been confirmed, with the exception of OPM Annuity locations.
- For Direct Bill locations, the below process is the same but will not include attempted deductions from an APO.
- Initiation of Direct Bill:
- Pay Sequence 1: Enrollee’s APO is billed; no payment is received.
- Pay Sequence 2: APO is billed and no payment is received; Enrollee is switched to Direct Billing due to non-payment.
- Issuance of Direct Bills:
- Pay Sequence 3: APO is billed a single deduction amount and no payment is received; Enrollee is sent a direct bill (Direct Bill 1) for all past due premiums (2 pay periods) at the same time the APO is billed.
- Direct bills are sent every odd pay sequence for federal employees and every pay sequence for annuitants and compensationers.
- The amount on the Direct Bill includes the full past due amount necessary to prevent inactivation.
- Pay Sequence 4: APO is billed and no payment is received.
- Non-Payment and Warnings:
- Pay Sequence 5: APO is billed and no payment is received; Direct Bill 2 is sent. The amount that totals pay sequence 1 and 2 is due 25 days later.
- A Termination Warning will be included in the direct bill that follows the first unpaid bill.
- It will state that the enrollee will be inactivated if the minimum payment is not received within 25 days.
- Inactivation:
- Pay Sequence 6: APO is billed and no payment is received.
- Enrollee will be terminated on the date provided in their termination warning letter.
- If the enrollee fails to send a payment to prevent inactivation after two missed pay sequences, the enrollee is inactivated on the next odd pay sequence unless the APO begins to submit payment.
- Reinstatement Considerations:
- General reinstatement after inactivation due to non-payment is typically not allowed unless an exception applies:
- Incorrect address preventing receipt of bills.
- The APO submits payment.
- We receive a direct payment for the minimum amount required within 5 days of termination.
- If the enrollee is in active pay status and payment from the DV35 is received.
- They are on Worker’s Compensation and began receiving pay (payroll only, not medical pay) from OWCP prior to inactivation.
- Documentation:
- A DV24 letter is sent after the second $0.00 payment informing the enrollee of the transition to Direct Bill.
- Adjustment letters are sent as needed based on changes in the deductions.

units.heading: Key Points
units.text:
Key Points:
- Ensure to check the payroll schedule for specific pay sequences when reviewing or discussing billing with enrollees.
- Direct Bills (DB01) for customers with both dental and vision will now be sent together and will be locatable in IMAGE as one document.
- Direct bills must be paid promptly to avoid inactivation, with clear communication on due dates and consequences provided to the enrollee.
- Agents may not suggest non-payment as a way to cancel coverage. If the customer independently states they will stop making payments, you may explain the standard non-payment termination process.

units.heading: Physical Address Requirement for BENEFEDS Account Creation and Updates
units.text:
Physical Address Requirement for BENEFEDS Account Creation and Updates
When creating or updating a BENEFEDS account, it is essential for customers to provide a valid physical address for their residential address. This requirement ensures that all accounts are associated with a specific, physical location for verification and security purposes. Please note that while P.O. boxes can be used for billing purposes, they are not acceptable as the primary physical address on your account. It is important to adhere to this policy to maintain the integrity and accuracy of our records.

units.heading: Prohibited Use of Premium Postal Services
units.text:
Prohibited Use of Premium Postal Services
Customers must refrain from using premium postal services, such as those offered by USPS or UPS, which provide a P.O. box with an associated street address. Utilizing such services for registering or updating a physical address on a BENEFEDS account is a violation of the terms of the USPS. If a customer mentions using these services, please use the following script:
"Please note that you must provide a physical residential address, as using a P.O. Box 'street address' is against postal regulations and could lead to legal issues and service termination."

units.heading: VA Benefits Inactivation
units.text:
An exception was added to allow an enrollee or sponsor, who pays premium on a post-tax basis, to cancel FEDVIP enrollment or decrease their enrollment type if the sponsor, enrollee, or TEI family member becomes eligible for dental or vision benefits from U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The request for cancellation or removal of a dependent must be received within 60 days after notification of eligibility for VA dental and/or vision service eligibility. After 60 days the cancellation or change to enrollment type can be made during Open Season or via a Qualifying Life Event.
Enrollees seeking to cancel or decrease their enrollment type due to being approved for VA dental and vision benefits, should be given the following contact information:
The email must contain: Name, address, the request to be inactivated due to being awarded VA Benefits, and the date of the VA letter from the VA confirming those benefits. If OPM need more information from the customer, they will communicate directly to them.
The enrollee must have approval for disability having been received AFTER they enrolled in FEDVIP.
OPM is reviewing requests on a case-by-case basis and will be reaching out to enrollees to obtain documentation/proof of the VA approval. If the documentation is in good order, OPM will advise BENEFEDS to process the inactivation or dependent removal – if approved.
All calls regarding canceling coverage or decreasing enrollment type due to the approval of VA benefits must be tracked on the VA Benefits Inactivation log, located in the CCC Workspace. Each entry should include the Member ID, enrollee's name, employment status (CIV or USM) and comments.
Note: OPM Annuitants approved for VA benefits without a USM affiliation should be aware that their dependents will lose FEDVIP coverage. However, if the dependents are eligible as FEDCIV or through their own USM status, they may enroll as the primary due to loss of coverage.

- Identify the date & time the issue started
- Describe the issue by providing relevant details as well as the following when applicable: CXone Contact ID, complete error message, etc.
- Click Submit

units.heading: Workforce Changes Resource Compilation
units.text:
Due to recent workforce changes, you may receive calls from enrollees inquiring about their FEDVIP coverage after accepting a Deferred Resignation (the fork in the road memo) or being terminated from federal service.
Allowed Actions for Impacted Population:
- Update all contact information. This includes email address, home address, phone number, and if possible, request that they provide a secondary contact for their email and phone.
- Reinstate their previous dental/vision coverage.
- FEDCIV employees hired on or after January 20th, 2025, separated from the federal government, and have since returned to work can enroll in FEDVIP coverage.
- Exceptions will be made for only this affected population to enroll past their eligibility window (60 days from date of hire).
Table of contents
- Workforce Changes Talking Points – Page 2
- Handling Reinstatements – Page 3
- New Hire Exceptions – Page 4 & 5

units.heading: I’ve accepted the Deferred Resignation. What happens with my FEDVIP coverage?
units.text:
I’ve accepted the Deferred Resignation. What happens with my FEDVIP coverage?
- Your coverage will continue through the last day of the pay period in which BENEFEDS has received premiums.
- Your premiums will be deducted via payroll deductions.
- You will no longer be eligible for FEDVIP when your employment with the federal government ends.
- If you fully self-resign prior to Sept 30th, your eligibility will end on your resignation date
- If you’ve secured a non-federal job and wish to cancel your FEDVIP Coverage prior to Sept 30th, you must contact your ABO/HR to discuss early self resignation. Once the termination code is received, your account will inactivate. If you do not self resign prior to Sept 30th, your account will inactivate after the deferred resignation date.

units.heading: I’ve accepted the Deferred Resignation. What happens with my · I’ve been terminated from federal service. What happens with my FEDVIP Coverage?
units.text:
I’ve been terminated from federal service. What happens with my FEDVIP Coverage?
- Your coverage will continue through the last day of the pay period in which BENEFEDS has received premiums.
- You are no longer eligible for FEDVIP when your employment with the federal government ends.
- There is no 31-day temporary extension of coverage or opportunity to convert to private coverage.
- Your coverage ends on the last day of the pay period during which you separate.
- If you’re a Uniformed Service Member, you can change your affiliation now, prior to your inactivation or 60 days after your inactivation.

units.heading: I’ve accepted the Deferred Resignation. What happens with my · What if I am retiring? What happens with my FEDVIP Coverage?
units.text:
What if I am retiring? What happens with my FEDVIP Coverage?
- If you are retiring (includes Voluntary Early Retirement Authority, VERA), no action is needed. Your Agency will advise BENEFEDS of your retirement and we will begin the transition to retirement process.
- During your transition to retirement, you can expect to receive direct bills from BENEFEDS while we work to establish premium deductions from your annuity.
- You are expected to pay any direct bills sent to you to maintain your FEDVIP coverage during this time.

units.heading: I’ve accepted the Deferred Resignation. What happens with my · Am I allowed to reinstate my FEDVIP coverage?
units.text:
Am I allowed to reinstate my FEDVIP coverage?
- If your employment with the federal government is reinstated, you may be eligible to have your FEDVIP coverage reinstated as well.
- If you have been reinstated, inform BENEFEDS so that we can begin the process to reinstate your coverage.
- Submit a Primary – Reinstatement AWD (There is no timeframe for these scenarios).
- Select Incorrect Code as the Reinstatement Reason.

units.heading: I’ve accepted the Deferred Resignation. What happens with my · Is there anything I need to do?
units.text:
Is there anything I need to do?
- No. There is no action you need to take. Your Agency Benefits Office will advise BENEFEDS of any updates to your status, except for being reinstated.
What if I have further questions about the Deferred Resignation Program?
- If you have further questions about the Deferred Resignation Program, or about your eligibility for FEDVIP, consult your Human Resources or Agency Benefits Office for further information.

units.heading: How Impacted Enrollee Will Reinstate:
units.text:
- How Impacted Enrollee Will Reinstate:
- Enrollees whose agencies have sent BENEFEDS a list of individuals to reinstate
- In these cases, no action is needed by the enrollees or agents
- Some individuals may call in even when their agency has notified BENEFEDS of their reinstatement
- Enrollees who call BENEFEDS to reinstate
- Enrollees may call BENEFEDS to make us aware of their reinstatement or email us at reinstatefedvip@benefeds.gov.
- Agents will see that their account is inactive and will create a Primary – Reinstatement ticket
- Regardless of the differences, if an enrollee calls in asking to be reinstated, was impacted by recent workforce changes, and has an inactive account, agents will process their reinstatement.
- Barring applicable Qualifying Life Events, they do not have the option to disenroll or choose to not be reinstated. (This applies even if they have received other insurance.)
- A comment will be placed on accounts that have reinstated via the email: “Enrollee has sent an email to state their employment has been restored. I have processed the reinstatements on both the dental and the vision.”

units.heading: How Impacted Enrollee Will Reinstate: · A caller does not want to be reinstated or is asking why they must be reinstated
units.text:
A caller does not want to be reinstated or is asking why they must be reinstated:
“We understand your concern (and/or) frustration. All federal employees who have been impacted by recent workforce changes and have since returned to federal service must be reinstated, per OPM. Should your employment be reinstated, we will be notified by your agency and will then reinstate your FEDVIP coverage. You will receive a confirmation of your reinstatement once processed. ”

units.heading: How Impacted Enrollee Will Reinstate: · Handling Reinstatements for Impacted Enrollees
units.text:
Handling Reinstatements for Impacted Enrollees:
If the employee has recently separated from service and was subsequently reinstated due to recent federal workforce changes:
- Submit a Primary – Reinstatement AWD ticket.
- Select Incorrect Code as the reinstatement reason.
- Select all programs previously enrolled in (Dental/Vision). They may only reinstate their coverage (they cannot change their coverage or reenroll).
- In the AWD comments field, explain that the enrollee has been reinstated after a recent separation from federal service.

units.heading: How Impacted Enrollee Will Reinstate: · Advise
units.text:
Advise:
- Coverage will be reinstated back to the date of their initial separation date.
- We will attempt to double deduct for any past due premiums.
- So long as we successfully deduct from their agency, they will not receive any direct bills.
FSA Reinstatements:
- Transfer all FSA reinstatements to the FSAFEDS call center who will further assist.
- Agents will provide the FSAFEDS phone number - 1-877-372-3337.
- Agents will then place the caller on hold, dial FSAFEDS and then transfer.

units.heading: Agent Actions:
units.text:
Agent Actions:
- Update the enrollee’s profile information (Address/Email/Phone)
- You may advise the enrollee of the above information, then process the reinstatement.
- If they have questions, direct them to speak their agency or HR office.

units.heading: Steps to Follow When Processing a New Enrollment for Impacted Group:
units.text:
Steps to Follow When Processing a New Enrollment for Impacted Group:
- Identify if the caller was a new hire on or after January 20, 2025, and has been impacted by recent workforce changes.
- Create or locate their account in the BENEFEDS CS system.
- In the enrollment flow, select Newly Eligible, and provide their eligibility date (date of hire).
- If they are within their 60-day window, they may enroll belated following the process below or continue to enroll as normal.
- For those who are outside of 60 days, upon selecting Next, you will be presented with the Override Confirmation window.
- DO NOT read the Override Confirmation scripting. Instead, say, “Premiums will be double deducted from your pay until the past due is satisfied.”
- Under Override Reason, enter “Override per reinstatement of employment.”
- Click Override, then continue the enrollment as normal. The enrollment will be retroactive.
conditions: DO NOT read the Override Confirmation scripting. Instead, say, “Premiums will be double deducted from your pay until the past due is satisfied.”

units.heading: Workforce Changes Resource Compilation
units.text:
NOTE: If submitting enrollments for both Dental and Vision, complete both enrollments prior to completing the following steps.
- After processing the enrollment, submit a Primary – Change Enrollment AWD ticket. This is to remove the belated enrollment flag and belated past due from their account.
- Select Change Enrollment from the Action Needed dropdown.
- Select either Dental, Vision, or both from the Plans Requiring Change box.
- In the Event Date box, put the enrollee’s date of hire.
- Select No for the *Is Dependent Info Needed drop down.
- Comment in AWD, “Submitted belated enrollment due to reinstatement of employment. Please remove belated flag and belated past due.”
- Select Continue.
- Return to the CS system. You will ignore the Action Required notification for Payment Due since we will deduct past due premiums from their agency.
